topics.title: Electrical Safety & Standards
topics.zh: 电气安全与标准

sections.b:
Electricity is the most common form of energy in homes, offices, factories and construction sites. When it passes through the human body it causes electric shock and/or burns, and accidents also cost industry lost production time and damaged property.

Ministry of Manpower statistics put the common causes into six groups:

  1. Ignorance or negligence — wrongly connected wires and other mistakes
  2. Failure or lack of earthing
  3. Physical damage to wiring and equipment
  4. Lack of maintenance and checks
  5. Carelessness and unsafe operating procedures
  6. "DIY" repairs by unauthorised or incompetent persons

sections.h: Electric shock — what the current does
sections.b:
An electric shock happens when the body becomes part of an electrical path. What decides the harm is the current through the body, given by Ohm's law. The notes' example: a person of about 1000 Ω touching 120 V carries I = 120 ÷ 1000 = 120 mA — well into the fatal range.

Current through the bodyTypical effect (from the notes' chart)
A few mACan just feel it; increasing pain as current rises
≈ 10–30 mA"Can't let go" — muscles clamp onto the conductor
≈ 50–60 mASevere pain, breathing affected
≈ 80–100 mA and aboveProbably fatal (heart fibrillation)

Direct contact — touching a part that is normally live (e.g. bare terminals of a damaged plug). Indirect contact — touching exposed metal that has become live because of a fault, such as insulation failure inside an appliance. The current that flows through the person is the touch current Is; the current leaking to the protective earth conductor is the insulation fault current Id.

Effects can last: burns leave scars, current through the eyes can cause cataracts, and internal injury may cause pain, numbness or muscle weakness. Damage may not show for up to 10 days.

Someone is receiving a shock
Can you switch OFF the supply?
No → move the source away with a dry wooden stick — NEVER touch the person with bare hands, or you become part of the circuit
Switch off the current source (first step)
Attend to the victim; check for breathing
Breathing?
No → start CPR and call emergency medical aid
If breathing: do a physical examination, treat minor burns
Re-establish vital functions (BP, pulse); serious burns need hospital care

The Electric Shock Treatment chart must be displayed in premises so that anyone nearby can follow the correct first-aid steps immediately.

• Switch off equipment that is not in use.
  • Use plugs with proper earthing (grounding) prongs.
  • Inspect cords regularly for fraying and wear.
  • Keep cords out of walkways; avoid extension cords in offices.
  • Do not overload outlets or surge protectors; a surge protector is not an extension cord.
  • Keep paper and other combustibles away from outlets and connections.

sections.h: Electric shock — more from your notes
sections.b:
• How do you treat an electric shock? Depending on the injuries, potential treatments include: (1) burn treatment, including the application of antibiotic ointment and sterile dressings; (2) pain medication; (3) intravenous fluids; (4) a tetanus shot, depending on the source of the shock and how it occurred.
  • After a shock: the shock can cause a burn where the current enters and leaves the body. The electricity may have injured blood vessels, nerves and muscles, and could have affected the heart and lungs. You might not see all the damage for up to 10 days after the shock.
  • NEVER touch the person receiving the electric shock, or you could suffer one too. After removing the person from the source of electricity, if the person is unconscious call for an ambulance immediately. Only those with the necessary knowledge and skill should carry out first aid.

worked.q: Tutorial: classify each situation as direct or indirect contact. (a) A plastic hair dryer with part of its cover missing. (b) A kettle body becomes live through a plug wiring fault. (c) Removing toast from a toaster with a knife. (d) A vacuum cleaner with a damaged plug top. (e) Vibration loosens the cable terminations inside a washing machine.
worked.s:
(a) Direct — internal live parts are exposed and can be touched.
(b) Indirect — normally-dead metal became live through a fault.
(c) Direct — the heating element is a normally live part.
(d) Direct — the live pins/terminals are exposed.
(e) Indirect — a loose live wire can touch the metal case, making it live.

worked.q: A worker with a body resistance of 2000 Ω touches a 230 V live conductor. Find the current and the likely effect.
worked.s:
I = V ÷ R = 230 ÷ 2000 = 0.115 A = 115 mA
This is above about 80–100 mA → probably fatal.

topics.title: Atomic Theory, Current & Materials
topics.zh: 原子理论、电流与材料

sections.b:
The atom is the smallest particle of a substance that still has the characteristics of that substance. Every atom contains:

ParticleChargeWhere
ProtonPositive (+)Nucleus — heavy and fixed
NeutronNoneNucleus — heavy and fixed
ElectronNegative (−)Orbits (shells) — light and movable

Each shell holds at most 2N² electrons, where N is the shell number: K = 2, L = 8, M = 18, N = 32. Hydrogen is the simplest atom (one proton, one electron). Copper has 29 electrons arranged 2, 8, 18, 1.

The outermost shell is the valence shell; its electrons are valence electrons (an atom can have up to 8). They are furthest from the nucleus, so they are held most loosely. If a valence electron gains enough energy (heat, light, voltage) it breaks away and becomes a free electron.

  • The more complete the outer shell, the more tightly its electrons are held, the more stable the atom, and the more energy is needed to free an electron.
  • Atoms with few valence electrons (1–3) give up electrons easily → conductors (copper, aluminium).
  • Atoms with nearly full shells (5–8) hold them tightly → insulators.
  • Atoms with 4 valence electrons → semiconductors (silicon, germanium).

Charges exert a force on each other: like charges repel, unlike charges attract. A difference in charge between two points is a voltage (potential difference, electromotive force). It is this push that makes free electrons drift through a circuit.

Without a voltage, free electrons drift randomly in all directions. With a voltage applied, they move from the negative end toward the positive end — this flow of charge is electric current.

Electron flowConventional current
Direction− to + (what electrons actually do)+ to − (the convention used on circuit diagrams)
Used forExplaining how conduction worksCircuit analysis, symbols (diode and transistor arrows)

Voltage is the cause; current is the effect.

worked.q: How many electrons can the 3rd and 4th shells hold?
worked.s:
2N²: N = 3 → 2 × 9 = 18 electrons
N = 4 → 2 × 16 = 32 electrons

topics.title: Ohm's Law & Resistor Circuits
topics.zh: 欧姆定律与电阻电路

sections.b:
Ohm's law links voltage, current and resistance: current is directly proportional to voltage and inversely proportional to resistance.

I = V / RV = I × R, R = V / I
UnitsI — ampere (A)V — volt (V)R — ohm (Ω)

Cover the quantity you want in the V–I–R triangle: V on top, I and R below. 1 Ω is the resistance that passes 1 A when 1 V is across it.

P = V × I = I²R = V²/Rpower, in watts (W)
UnitsP — watt (W)V — volt (V)I — ampere (A)R — ohm (Ω)

SeriesParallel
CurrentSame through every resistorSplits; IT = I1 + I2 + I3
VoltageSplits; V = V1 + V2 + V3Same across every branch
Total resistanceRT = R1 + R2 + R3 (larger than any)1/RT = 1/R1 + 1/R2 + … (smaller than the smallest)
One part fails openWhole circuit stopsOther branches keep working
RT = R1 × R2 / (R1 + R2)two resistors in parallel: product over sum
UnitsRT, R1, R2 — ohm (Ω)

Series–parallel circuits: reduce them step by step — combine each parallel group into one equivalent resistor, add the series parts, find the total current, then work back out to each resistor.

4-band resistor: band 1 = first digit, band 2 = second digit, band 3 = multiplier, band 4 = tolerance. Example: brown–black–red–gold = 1, 0, ×100 = 1000 Ω = 1 kΩ ±5 %.

An LDR (light-dependent resistor) changes its resistance with light — high in the dark, low in bright light.

worked.q: Series (notes): 10 Ω, 20 Ω and 30 Ω carry 2 A. Find the supply voltage and each voltage drop.
Parallel (notes): 10 Ω, 20 Ω and 30 Ω across 12 V. Find each current, the total current and RT.
Series (notes): 3 kΩ, 10 kΩ and 5 kΩ across 9 V. Find the current and each voltage.
Series–parallel: 4 Ω and 6 Ω in parallel, in series with 2.6 Ω, across 10 V. Find the total current and the current in the 4 Ω resistor.
worked.s:
4 ∥ 6 = 4 × 6 ÷ (4 + 6) = 2.4 Ω
RT = 2.4 + 2.6 = 5 Ω
IT = 10 ÷ 5 = 2 A
Voltage across the parallel pair = 2 × 2.4 = 4.8 V
I(4 Ω) = 4.8 ÷ 4 = 1.2 A (and 0.8 A in the 6 Ω)

topics.title: Passive Components: R, C and L
topics.zh: 无源元件：电阻、电容与电感

sections.b:
Passive components do not need a source of energy to do their job and cannot amplify. They dissipate energy (resistors) or store it (capacitors in an electric field, inductors in a magnetic field). Resistors, capacitors, inductors and transformers are the building blocks of every circuit. Active components — diodes and transistors — control current and need a supply.

ComponentUnitWhat it doesTypical uses
ResistorOhm (Ω)Opposes current; turns energy into heatLimit current, divide voltage, bias transistors
CapacitorFarad (F)Stores energy in an electric field; blocks DC, passes ACSmoothing, filtering noise, coupling/decoupling, timing
InductorHenry (H)Stores energy in a magnetic field; passes DC, opposes changes in ACChokes, filters, tuned circuits (with capacitors)

A capacitor is two conducting plates separated by an insulator (dielectric). It stores charge; 1 farad stores 1 coulomb at 1 volt (Q = C × V). Practical values are µF, nF and pF.

  • Electrolytic capacitors are polarised — the + lead must go to the more positive point, or the capacitor can fail or burst. The value and maximum voltage are printed on the body.
  • Ceramic / film capacitors are non-polarised and use a 3-digit code in picofarads: two digits then the number of zeros. 104 = 10 × 10⁴ pF = 100 000 pF = 100 nF = 0.1 µF.
  • Always respect the maximum voltage rating.
µFnFpF
1 µF1000 nF1 000 000 pF
0.1 µF100 nF100 000 pF
0.001 µF1 nF1000 pF

An inductor is a coil of wire. Current through it creates a magnetic field; the field opposes any change of current. So an inductor passes steady DC easily but opposes AC — an inductor used for this is called a choke.

  • Cores: air (small inductance, high frequency), iron (large inductance, low frequency), ferrite (high frequency with less loss). Each can be fixed, variable or pre-set.
  • Inductance is usually millihenrys (mH) or microhenrys (µH), measured with an LCR meter.
  • Inductor + capacitor = a tuned circuit that picks one frequency (radio and TV tuning).

topics.title: Semiconductors & the PN Junction
topics.zh: 半导体与 PN 结

sections.b:
Semiconductors conduct better than insulators but worse than conductors, and conduct more when heat, light or voltage is added. Their atoms have 4 valence electrons: silicon (Si, 14 protons) and germanium (Ge, 32 protons).

  • An intrinsic semiconductor is a pure crystal. Each Si atom shares one electron with each of its four neighbours — covalent bonds.
  • Heat gives some valence electrons enough energy to break free. Each leaves behind a hole — the absence of an electron, which behaves like a positive charge.
  • Electron current: free electrons move from − to +. Hole current: a neighbouring valence electron jumps into a hole, so the hole appears to move the other way (toward −).
  • Germanium has more free electrons (higher conductivity); silicon has a higher temperature rating, so silicon is used far more widely.

A pure semiconductor has very few free carriers. Doping adds a tiny amount of impurity to make an extrinsic semiconductor.

N-typeP-type
ImpurityPentavalent (5 valence electrons): arsenic, phosphorus, antimonyTrivalent (3 valence electrons): aluminium, boron, gallium
Name of impurityDonor (gives an extra electron)Acceptor (accepts an electron, creating a hole)
Majority carriersElectronsHoles
Minority carriersHolesElectrons
The notes label the P-type slide "donor acceptor" — the correct term for trivalent impurities is simply acceptor.

sections.h: The PN junction and the diode
sections.b:
1. When P and N material are joined, electrons from the N side diffuse across and recombine with holes on the P side.
  2. This leaves a region of fixed positive and negative ions near the junction with no free carriers — the depletion layer.
  3. The ions create a barrier potential VB: about 0.7 V for silicon and 0.3 V for germanium at 25 °C. It falls slightly as temperature rises.
BiasConnectionResult
ForwardP (anode) to +, N (cathode) to −, above VBDepletion layer narrows → diode conducts
ReverseP to −, N to +Depletion layer widens → only a tiny leakage current

Breakdown voltage VBR is the reverse voltage that breaks down the junction; the manufacturer's peak inverse voltage (PIV) is the maximum safe reverse voltage. Above VBR, reverse current builds up rapidly and can destroy an ordinary diode.

Testing a diode with an ohmmeter

ResultForward check (+ to anode)Reverse check (+ to cathode)
Good diodeLow resistanceHigh resistance
Open diodeHighHigh
Shorted diodeLowLow

topics.title: AC to DC Power Supplies & Zener Regulators
topics.zh: 交流变直流电源与稳压二极管

sections.b:
A zener diode is designed to work in reverse breakdown. Its breakdown voltage VZ is set by the doping level, and in breakdown it holds an almost constant VZ over a range of currents — so VOUT = VZ.

  • The zener is connected reverse-biased, in parallel with the load, so VL = VZ.
  • The series current-limiting resistor R drops the excess voltage and limits the current so the zener does not overheat.
  • Line regulation = keeping the output constant while the input voltage changes (load current constant). Load regulation = keeping it constant while the load current changes.
VR = VIN − VZIR = VR/R, IL = VZ/RL, IZ = IR − IL
UnitsVR, VIN, VZ — volt (V)IR, IL, IZ — ampere (A)R, RL — ohm (Ω)

An LED (light-emitting diode) gives out light when forward-biased. Its forward voltage is about 1.8–3.3 V depending on colour — red ≈ 1.8 V, blue ≈ 3–3.3 V. An LED must always have a series resistor to limit its current.

R = (VS − VF) / IFseries resistor for an LED
UnitsR — ohm (Ω)VS, VF — volt (V)IF — ampere (A)

sections.h: Rectifier — the definition in your notes
sections.b: A rectifier is an electrical device that converts alternating current (AC), which periodically reverses direction, to direct current (DC), which flows in only one direction. The process is known as rectification, since it "straightens" the direction of current.

worked.q: Notes Example 1: a 10 V zener, R = 5 kΩ, RL = 10 kΩ, VIN = 25 V. Find VZ, VL, VR, IR, IL and IZ.
worked.s:
VZ = 10 V; VL = VZ = 10 V (in parallel)
VR = 25 − 10 = 15 V
IR = 15 V ÷ 5 kΩ = 3 mA
IL = 10 V ÷ 10 kΩ = 1 mA
IZ = IR − IL = 3 − 1 = 2 mA

worked.q: A transformer secondary gives 12 V rms. Find the average DC from (a) a half-wave and (b) a bridge rectifier (ignore diode drops).
A red LED (VF = 1.8 V) runs from 5 V at 20 mA. Find the series resistor.
worked.s: R = (5 − 1.8) ÷ 0.02 = 160 Ω → use the next standard value, 180 Ω (a little less current)

topics.title: Bipolar Junction Transistors
topics.zh: 双极结型晶体管

sections.b:
A BJT has three doped regions — emitter, base, collector — separated by two PN junctions (base–emitter and base–collector). It comes as NPN or PNP.

RegionDopingSizeJob
EmitterHeavily dopedThickSupplies the charge carriers
BaseLightly dopedVery thinControls the flow of carriers
CollectorSlightly lighter than emitterThickCollects carriers from the emitter

For normal (amplifying) operation: the base–emitter junction is forward-biased and the base–collector junction is reverse-biased.

  1. Forward bias narrows the B–E depletion layer; electrons from the N-type emitter cross into the base.
  2. The base is thin and lightly doped, so only a few electrons recombine with holes there — this forms the small base current IB.
  3. Most electrons are swept across the reverse-biased B–C junction into the collector — the large collector current IC.
  4. Increasing the B–E voltage increases IB, and with it IC and IE. A small base current controls a much larger collector current.
IE = IC + IBemitter current is the total
UnitsIE, IC, IB — ampere (A)
αdc = IC / IEtypically 0.95 – 0.99
Unitsαdc — no unitIC, IE — ampere (A)
βdc = IC / IBtypically 20 – 200
Unitsβdc — no unitIC, IB — ampere (A)
α = β / (1 + β)β = α / (1 − α)
Unitsα, β — no unit

sections.h: Switch or amplifier, and the three configurations
sections.b:
As a switch the transistor is driven fully OFF (cut-off) or fully ON (saturation) — a small base current switches a larger load such as a relay or lamp. As an amplifier it is biased part-way on so a small input signal produces a larger output signal.

ConfigurationVoltage gainCurrent gainPower gainIn/out phaseInput / output resistanceTypical use
Common emitter (CE)Medium–highMedium–highHigh180° (inverting)Medium / mediumGeneral amplifier
Common base (CB)HighLow (< 1)Low0°Low / highHigh-frequency amplifiers
Common collector (CC, emitter follower)≈ 1HighMedium0°High / lowVoltage buffer
The notes' common-collector page repeats the common-emitter facts (180°, inverting). The correct facts are in the table: the emitter follower's output follows the input in phase (0°) with a voltage gain just under 1, and is used as a buffer because of its high input and low output resistance.

sections.h: Transistor as a switch — the wording in your notes
sections.b: A transistor switch is used for opening or closing a circuit. The transistor is commonly used as a switch in electronic devices only for low-voltage applications, because of its low power consumption. A transistor works as a switch when it is in the cutoff and saturation regions.

worked.q: Notes: IB = 10 µA, IC = 1 mA. Find β. Then IC = 7 mA, IE = 8 mA — find α.
worked.s:
β = IC ÷ IB = 1 mA ÷ 10 µA = 100
α = IC ÷ IE = 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875 (the notes round to 0.88)

worked.q: A transistor has β = 150 and IB = 40 µA. Find IC, IE and α.

topics.title: Digital Concepts & Number Systems
topics.zh: 数字概念与数制

sections.b:
An analogue signal varies continuously; a digital signal has discrete values — in binary systems just two, 1 (HIGH, on, true) and 0 (LOW, off, false). Digital signals can be sent and stored without being degraded by noise, more bits give more precision, and digital circuits are easier to design and cheaper.

A bit (binary digit) is the smallest unit of information. In positive logic HIGH = 1 and LOW = 0 (negative logic is the reverse).

TTL logic levelVoltage
HIGH (binary 1)2 V to 5 V
Uncertain — not allowed0.8 V to 2 V
LOW (binary 0)0 V to 0.8 V

f = 1 / Tfrequency (Hz) and period (s)
Unitsf — hertz (Hz)T — second (s)
Duty cycle = tw / T × 100 %tw = pulse width
Unitstw, T — second (s)

A clock waveform sets the bit time; each bit of data occupies one bit time. A timing diagram shows several related waveforms against the same time axis, so the HIGH/LOW state of each can be read at any instant.

SystemBaseDigitsPlace weights
Binary20 1… 8 4 2 1 . ½ ¼
Octal80–7… 512 64 8 1
Decimal100–9… 1000 100 10 1
Hexadecimal160–9, A–F (A = 10 … F = 15)… 4096 256 16 1
  • With n bits you can count from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1 (4 bits → 0 to 15).
  • LSB (least significant bit) has weight 2⁰ = 1; the MSB's weight depends on the number of bits.
  • Binary → decimal: add the weights where there is a 1.
  • Decimal → binary (sum of weights): take the largest power of 2 that fits, subtract, repeat.
  • Binary ↔ hex: group in 4s from the binary point (add leading zeros). Binary ↔ octal: group in 3s.
  • BCD (binary-coded decimal) writes each decimal digit as its own 4-bit group. Codes 1010–1111 are invalid in BCD.

sections.h: Digital systems — the wording in your notes
sections.b:
• What is meant by digital systems? A digital system stores data in a discrete way. The opposite is an analogue system, which stores data in a continuous way. Usually, digital systems store information in a binary way: every bit of information cannot have a value other than zero (off) or one (on).
  • Why are digital systems important? Signals represented digitally can be transmitted without degradation caused by noise. A more precise representation of a signal can be obtained by using more binary digits to represent it.
  • Advantages of digital: the effect of distortion, noise and interference is much less in digital signals; digital circuits are easy to design and cheaper than analog circuits; the hardware implementation in digital circuits is more flexible than analog.

worked.q: Notes waveform: pulses are HIGH from 0 to 1 ms and repeat every 10 ms. Find the period, frequency and duty cycle. Then: tw = 25 µs, T = 150 µs.

topics.title: Binary & Hexadecimal Arithmetic
topics.zh: 二进制与十六进制运算

sections.b:
AdditionSumCarry
0 + 000
0 + 110
1 + 010
1 + 101
SubtractionDifferenceBorrow
0 − 000
1 − 010
1 − 100
0 − 111

Work right to left exactly as in decimal: a carry goes to the next column on the left; a borrow takes 1 from the next column (worth 2 in the current column). Also 1 + 1 + 1 = 1 carry 1.

1's complement (inverting every bit) is done with one inverter per bit: 1101 0001 → 0010 1110.

Adding: add each column in decimal. If the column total is 16 or more, subtract 16, write the remainder (as a hex digit) and carry 1. Example: 4C + 3A → C + A = 12 + 10 = 22 = 16 + 6 → write 6 carry 1; 4 + 3 + 1 = 8 → 86.

Subtracting: if the top digit is smaller, borrow 1 from the next column — it adds 16. Example: D7 − A8 → 7 + 16 = 23, 23 − 8 = 15 = F; D becomes C, C − A = 12 − 10 = 2 → 2F.

Check any answer by converting to decimal: D7 = 215, A8 = 168, 215 − 168 = 47 = 2F ✓

16-bit: 0100101000101101 + 0001101000101111, and the same subtraction. Hex: A049 + 0AFC, 8BB0 + 4AC8.

topics.title: Logic Gates
topics.zh: 逻辑门

sections.b:
ABAND A·BOR A+BNANDNOR
000011
010110
100110
111100
  • NOT (inverter): output is the complement of the input, Y = A̅. 0 → 1, 1 → 0.
  • AND: output HIGH only when all inputs are HIGH.
  • OR: output HIGH when any input is HIGH.
  • NAND: output LOW only when all inputs are HIGH (AND followed by NOT).
  • NOR: output LOW when any input is HIGH (OR followed by NOT).

A circuit with n inputs has 2ⁿ input combinations — 2 inputs give 4 rows in the truth table, 3 inputs give 8.

• A NAND gate is equivalent to a negative-OR: output is HIGH if A or B is LOW.
  • A NOR gate is equivalent to a negative-AND: output is HIGH only when A and B are both LOW.
Application (notes)GateHow it works
Car seat-belt alarmANDAlarm sounds when ignition ON (HIGH) AND belt unbuckled (HIGH) during the 30 s timer
Door/window intrusion alarmORAny open sensor (HIGH) triggers the alarm
Two tanks both above ¼ fullNAND / negative-ORLevel sensors HIGH when above ¼; the output drives a green light
One or both tanks below ¼Negative-ORAny sensor LOW → red light
Aircraft landing gearNOR / negative-ANDExtended = LOW; green LED only when ALL gear are extended (all LOW)

Timing diagrams

To find an output waveform, look at each time interval separately and apply the gate's truth table to the input levels in that interval. Example (notes): AND inputs A = 1 0 1 1 0 and B = 1 1 1 0 0 give Y = 1 0 1 0 0.

Gates come in 74-series TTL integrated circuits in DIP packages. Pin 1 is marked by a dot, notch or bevelled edge — the dot is always next to pin 1.

  • Families: standard 74, Schottky 74S, low-power Schottky 74LS, advanced Schottky 74AS, advanced low-power Schottky 74ALS.
  • Fan-out = number of gate inputs one output can drive (large fan-out → slower). Fan-in = number of inputs a gate has (large fan-in → bigger and slower).
  • Packaging history (slide timeline): 1970s DIP, QFP, SOP, LCC → 1980s PGA → 1990s BGA, QFN → 2000s CSP, SiP, PoP, WLP → 2010s 2.5-D and 3-D ICs. The slides also show DIP chip packages (DIP 4 to DIP 48) and DIP sockets.

topics.title: Boolean Algebra & DeMorgan's Theorems
topics.zh: 布尔代数与德摩根定理

sections.b:
Boolean algebra has three operations: OR (logical addition, +), AND (logical multiplication, ·) and NOT (inversion, bar).

LawRuleDual
CommutativeA + B = B + AA·B = B·A
AssociativeA + (B + C) = (A + B) + CA(BC) = (AB)C
DistributiveA(B + C) = AB + ACA + BC = (A + B)(A + C)
Identity / redundancyA + 0 = A, A + 1 = 1, A + A = A, A + A̅ = 1A·1 = A, A·0 = 0, A·A = A, A·A̅ = 0
AbsorptionA + AB = AA(A + B) = A
InvolutionA̿ = A—
OtherA + A̅B = A + BA(A̅ + B) = AB

Each law can be checked by trying every combination in a truth table, or shown as switch/ladder circuits — e.g. A + B = B + A is two parallel contacts in either order.

A·B = A̅ + B̅1st theorem: NAND = negative-OR
A + B = A̅ · B̅2nd theorem: NOR = negative-AND

Rule of thumb: break the bar, change the sign. When a bar over a group is split over the individual variables, AND becomes OR and OR becomes AND.

Universal gates: NAND alone (or NOR alone) can build every other gate:

FunctionUsing NAND onlyUsing NOR only
NOTOne NAND with inputs tied togetherOne NOR with inputs tied together
ANDNAND followed by a NAND-inverterInvert each input with NOR, then NOR them: (A̅ + B̅)̅ = AB
ORInvert each input with NAND, then NAND themNOR followed by a NOR-inverter

worked.q: Prove (A + B)(A + C) = A + BC (from the notes).
worked.s:
Expand: AA + AC + AB + BC
AA = A → A + AC + AB + BC
A + AC = A (absorption) → A + AB + BC
A + AB = A → A + BC ✓

worked.q: Try this: expand (A + B)(C + D).
worked.s: = AC + AD + BC + BD (each term in the first bracket ANDed with each in the second)

worked.q: Simplify Y = AB + AB̅ and Y = (A + B)·A̅.
worked.s:
AB + AB̅ = A(B + B̅) = A·1 = A
(A + B)A̅ = AA̅ + BA̅ = 0 + A̅B = A̅B

topics.title: Wiring Practice & Control Components
topics.zh: 布线实践与控制元件

sections.b:
Cable trunking is an enclosure, usually rectangular with one removable or hinged side, that protects cables and conceals them neatly. Types include PVC mini-trunking, slotted panel (wiring) duct, floor/dado trunking, steel trunking and round conduit.

PVC-coated flexible conduit (a steel core with a PVC skin) compared with plain steel: more durable (the PVC stops water and corrosion), resists oil, acid and alkali, is fire-retardant, smooth inside so cables pull through easily, and looks neater.

Cables: conductors are usually copper (low resistance, flexible) or aluminium. Insulation materials include rubber, vulcanised India rubber, impregnated paper, varnished cambric and PVC. A power cable may have conductor → insulation → inner sheath → armour → PVC outer sheath.

ConductorOld colour codeNew (harmonised) colour code
Phase — single-phaseRedBrown
Phases — three-phase L1 / L2 / L3Red / Yellow / BlueBrown / Black / Grey
NeutralBlackBlue
Protective earthGreen-and-yellowGreen-and-yellow

• Multimeter — measures voltage, current and resistance, and tests continuity.
  • Insulation tester (megger) — applies a DC test voltage (typically 250 V, 500 V or 1000 V for low-voltage equipment) and reads the insulation resistance; used as a quality-control check.
  • Cable termination — the physical and electrical connection of a cable end to another cable or to equipment, using termination lugs.
  • Cable labelling — identifies every wire in panels and harnesses; a small upfront cost that saves time and labour in fault-finding and modification.

• Push buttons (NO start, NC stop) and indicating lights (pilot lamps, stack/tower lights).
  • Relays — switches that open and close one circuit when another circuit energises the coil. An NO contact is open when the coil is de-energised; an NC contact is closed.
  • Timer relays — a relay plus a timing circuit; contacts change before or after a pre-set time (delay-on / delay-off).
  • Limit switches and other sensing switches (flow, temperature, pressure, liquid level) — each has NO and NC versions with their own symbol.
  • Fuse, circuit breaker (MCB), overload, coil, motor, transformer — each has a standard symbol.

A control circuit controls a separate power circuit — e.g. a 24 V or 230 V control circuit switches the contactor of a large high-voltage motor. The main circuit breaker protects the whole installation; branch breakers protect individual circuits from overload. A block diagram is a high-level flowchart of a system's main parts and how they connect. Ladder logic draws control circuits as rungs between two rails and is the common PLC programming language.

sections.h: Block diagram, input and output — the wording in your notes
sections.b:
• Block diagram: a specialized, high-level flowchart used in engineering. It is used to design new systems or to describe and improve existing ones. Its structure provides a high-level overview of major system components, key process participants and important working relationships.
  • Electrical input and output: the INPUT is what sort of electrical system you need to supply to the adapter (i.e. what your power company supplies). The OUTPUT is what is supplied to your device.
  • Control system: a system is a combination of components that act together to perform a specific goal. Reference input is the actual signal input to the control system. Open-loop control system: a system in which the output has no effect on the input action.
  • Input-output control: a technique that allows operations to manage facility work flow. It is used to control the size of the queues in front of work centres, thereby helping to control manufacturing lead times.

A megger applies a ___ test voltage.

topics.title: Safety in the Maintenance Workshop
topics.zh: 维修车间安全

sections.b:
Good housekeeping means an orderly arrangement of tools, equipment, operations, storage and materials — an orderly, clean, tidy and bright workplace is far safer, and it must involve everyone.

BenefitWhy
Reduces fire hazardClutter speeds the outbreak and spread of fire
Higher moraleClean surroundings and freedom from injury improve attitudes
Lower operating costOnce established, less time and effort is needed
More productionNo excess material, tools or scrap obstructing the line

Basic rules: keep the bench neat; keep every tool in its place; keep the floor clear and clean; wipe up spilt oil at once.

A safe working environment is everyone's responsibility: safe work, safe tools and machines, safe handling and storage of dangerous substances, training and information for workers, and regular workplace checks with records.

• Wear a one-piece overall (torn clothing can catch in machinery); no rings, bracelets or watches; safety boots; safety glasses or goggles; keep hair short or wear a cap.
  • Tools: carry sharp tools points-down; never use defective tools; tie tools on with safety lines when working overhead.
  • Lifting: get help for heavy loads, use lifting equipment where possible; feet slightly apart, bend the knees with the back straight, grip firmly and lift by straightening the legs.
  • Machines: know how to stop a machine before you start it; switch off when not in use (put a notice on any machine left running); never touch moving parts — gears, belts, chains, saws, cutters; all guards in place before starting.
PPEUse
Cotton glovesOily or greasy parts
Rubber gloves / apronAcids and caustic solutions
Heat-resistant glovesHot materials (welding, forging)
Leather gloves / apronSharp, bulky items; hot metal and sparks
Safety helmetFalling objects, confined spaces
Breathing apparatusPolluted air or lack of oxygen (confined spaces)
Eye protectionProjectiles, chemicals and radiation — the most important rule in a machine shop
The notes list "asbestos gloves" for hot work. Asbestos is now banned because it causes cancer — modern heat-resistant gloves use materials such as aramid or leather.

Before maintenance on a machine
Disconnect the power supply
Lock the switch in the OFF position
Remove the fuses
Remove the drive belt, if any
Display a notice warning people not to reconnect the power
  • Replace all guards before switching on again.
  • Working at height: if a person can fall more than 3 m, provide a safety belt anchored no lower than the working position.
  • Lifting equipment must be inspected by an approved person, and its safe working load (SWL) must never be exceeded.
  • Dangerous machine parts must be fenced; vessels of corrosive or poisonous liquid fenced to at least 1 m high or covered; floor openings securely fenced.

recap: A safety belt is needed if a person may fall more than ___ m.
Never exceed the ___ of lifting equipment.
Before maintenance, lock the switch in the ___ position.

topics.title: Common Engineering Tools
topics.zh: 常用工程工具

sections.b:
The adjustable frame takes different blade lengths and lets the blade be turned to four cutting positions for tight spaces.

  • Pitch = number of teeth per 25 mm (1 inch): 18, 24 or 32 TPI. 18 TPI is the most common.
  • Fine teeth for thin metal, coarse teeth for thick metal.
  • Choose a pitch that keeps at least three teeth in contact with the metal — fewer and the teeth snag and break.

Chisels cut by a combined wedging and shearing action. They are hardened only at the cutting edge; the head stays soft to absorb hammer blows and is chamfered to limit the "mushroom head". Made from high-carbon, tool or alloy steel.

Cutting angle: about 70° or more for hard metal, down to about 30° for soft metal (smaller angles need more frequent sharpening). Too large — metal builds up and the chip won't curl; too small — the chisel digs in.

ChiselUse
Flat (60°)General: chipping flat surfaces, trimming castings, cutting thin metal and rivet heads
Side-cuttingSides of slots and keyways, squaring corners
Diamond-pointSharp internal corners, square holes, V-grooves for weld repair
Round-noseOil grooves in bearings and bushes, enlarging holes
Cross-cut (cape)Square keyways and grooves

Safety: chisel away from the body; wear goggles and use a chipping screen; grind off any mushroom head — pieces can fly off when struck.

A file has a handle, tang, heel (shoulder), face (side), edge and point. Files are classified by shape, length, grade and cut.

  • Double cut — two crossing sets of teeth (diamond-shaped) for fast metal removal; grades bastard, second cut, smooth. Single cut — one set of parallel teeth, lighter pressure, smoother finish.
  • Shapes: flat (general), hand (one safe edge with no teeth, for filing against a shoulder), warding (narrow slots), square (keyways, square holes), three-square (corners and angles over 60°), half-round (concave surfaces, enlarging holes), round ("rat tail", holes and fillets — use with a rolling motion).
  • Cross filing for flat surfaces; draw filing for a final even-grained finish on long narrow work.
  • Pinning — metal particles stuck in the teeth cause deep scratches (common on soft metal and aluminium, or with too much pressure). Clean with a file card or a flattened soft wire; chalk reduces pinning but also cutting.
  • Care: keep clean and dry, never knock on the bench or bend, store separately, ensure the handle is sound.

• Electric hand drill — motor drives a three-jaw chuck through gears. Keep the correct chuck key (tied to the lead with non-conducting tape); grip firmly before pressing the trigger; check the voltage; drill running before it touches the work; never press so hard that the motor slows; ease off at break-through. Never use a faulty drill — check the lead for cuts, a proper three-pin plug with earth connected, clear air vents and an undamaged casing. A dropped drill goes for electrical testing.
  • Pneumatic drill — air-driven, regarded as "safer" than electric. Check for cut or chafed air lines, insecure end fittings and blocked exhaust ducts.
  • Bench drilling machine — usually belt-driven, capacity ≤ 13 mm, sensitive hand feed with a return spring. Choose a machine by drilling capacity, spindle-to-column distance, spindle-to-base distance, depth of feed and feed type.

Drilling safety: the drill can grab loose clothing or hair, spin swarf or loose work, or shatter when jammed. Do not wear gloves at a drilling machine; roll or button sleeves; cover long hair; always wear safety goggles and boots; clamp the work.

Keep at least ___ teeth in contact when sawing.
Do not wear ___ at a drilling machine.

topics.title: Engineering Materials
topics.zh: 工程材料

sections.b:
PropertyMeaning
Tensile strengthMaximum pull (stretching) a material withstands before breaking
Compressive strengthAbility to withstand squeezing forces without fracture
DuctilityCan be bent, twisted or drawn out without breaking — needed for wire drawing
MalleabilityCan be permanently shaped by hammering, rolling or pressing without cracking (gold, lead high; cast iron low)
HardnessResists indentation, scratching, wear and abrasion
ToughnessWithstands sudden shock or impact without fracture
BrittlenessBreaks with very little deformation (e.g. cast iron)
ElasticityReturns to its original shape when the force is removed (e.g. a spring)
MachinabilityEase with which the material can be machined
Don't mix up: hard ≠ tough. Glass and cast iron are hard but brittle; mild steel is tough.

• Ferrous metals are mainly iron and carbon: wrought iron, low/mild/medium/high carbon steel, cast iron. Almost all are magnetic.
  • Non-ferrous metals contain little or no iron: copper, brass, aluminium, tin, lead. Strength can be raised by alloying.
  • An alloy is a mixture of two or more metals. Alloying elements are added to increase hardness, tensile strength, toughness, wear and corrosion resistance, and to improve strength, machinability, magnetic properties and high/low-temperature behaviour.

Thermosetting plasticThermoplastic
On heatingCures irreversibly — cannot be remeltedCan be melted and reshaped again and again
ExamplesAraldite, Bakelite, epoxy, silicone, polyimide, polyesterNylon (polyamide), acrylic, polypropylene, polystyrene, LDPE, HDPE
PropertiesHarder, stronger, heat- and solvent-resistant, good adhesion, more brittle, hard to recycleLower strength, less heat-resistant, less brittle, recyclable, often transparent

Rubber stays elastic over a wide temperature range (about −80 °C to +300 °C for special grades); it seals, absorbs vibration and noise, insulates, grips well and can be made flame-retardant, conductive or oil-resistant.

Glass is an amorphous (non-crystalline) solid made by fusing sand, soda and lime and cooling quickly — hard, transparent, waterproof, rust-free, but brittle and hazardous when broken.

topics.title: Measuring Instruments
topics.zh: 测量仪器

sections.b:
A vernier calliper reads to 0.02 mm (or 0.05 mm); common sizes 150 mm and 300 mm. It measures outside dimensions, inside dimensions (holes, slots), depths of holes, slots and steps, and checks parallelism.

The chapter introduction says vernier instruments are accurate to "0.2 mm"; the correct figure, as in section 4.1, is 0.02 mm.
Reading a 0.02 mm vernier (notes example)
Whole centimetres on the main scale × 10: 3 × 10 = 30.00 mm
Add whole millimetres past that: 6 mm → 36.00 mm
Find the vernier line that lines up best with a main-scale line: 28 divisions
28 × 0.02 = 0.56 mm
Reading = 30 + 6 + 0.56 = 36.56 mm

• Vernier height gauge — a vernier scale on a heavy hardened, ground base with a hardened scribing blade; range about 300–400 mm. Used on a surface table to measure height, check parallelism and alignment, and scribe lines at a set height.
  • Protractor — a dial in degrees with a swivelling blade, accurate to 30 minutes (½°). Used to set work to an angle, test angles and mark out hole positions.

Measures external sizes to ±0.01 mm. Parts: frame, anvil, spindle, sleeve (barrel), thimble, lock clamp, ratchet stop. Ranges go up in 25 mm steps: 0–25, 25–50, 50–75, 75–100 mm.

1 division = 0.5 mm ÷ 50 = 0.01 mmspindle pitch 0.5 mm, 50 thimble divisions
Reading (notes example)
Whole millimetres on the sleeve: 21 → 21.00 mm
Is a half-millimetre line showing beyond it? Yes → + 0.50 mm
Thimble division on the datum line: 32 × 0.01 = 0.32 mm
Reading = 21 + 0.5 + 0.32 = 21.82 mm

Zero error: clean the faces, close them with the ratchet; if the thimble zero does not meet the datum line there is a zero error (check larger micrometers with a gauge block or standard bar). Within ±0.01 mm: lock the spindle and turn the sleeve with the hook spanner. Larger errors: lock the spindle, loosen the ratchet stop, reset the thimble to zero, re-tighten.

Care: use the ratchet for correct pressure, never twirl the frame, avoid knocks, clean and store in its box.

worked.q: A 0.02 mm vernier shows 4 cm and 2 mm on the main scale, with the 13th vernier line aligned. Reading?
A micrometer sleeve shows 12 mm, no half-mm line, thimble at 47. Reading?

recap: A vernier calliper reads to ___ mm.
A protractor is accurate to ___ minutes.

topics.title: Drills
topics.zh: 钻头

sections.b:
Drilling forms round holes with an end-cutting tool. A drilled hole is not precise — it is always slightly bigger than the drill. Drills are high-carbon steel or high-speed steel (HSS); HSS can run at about twice the speed.

PartFunction
BodyCarries two helical grooves (flutes)
FlutesLet coolant in and chips (swarf) out
LandsNarrow strips that set the drill size and keep it aligned
Body clearanceReduced diameter behind the lands — less friction with the hole wall
LipsThe cutting edges
Chisel edgeWhere the two lips meet at the point
WebCentral core between the flutes; thickens toward the shank
Point angle118° for general purpose
ShankFits the chuck — straight (usually < 12 mm) or Morse taper (usually > 12 mm)
TangFlat end of a taper shank; a drift in the slot drives it out

Morse taper sleeves fit a small taper into a larger spindle; sockets fit a larger taper. Remove them with a drift lightly tapped through the tang slot.

Pilot hole / step drilling — a large drill's long chisel edge makes it wander, so drill a small pilot hole first (e.g. for 12 mm: 3 → 5 → 8 → 11 → 12 mm).

PointAngleUse
Conventional118°Most ferrous metals (mild steel)
Long angle60°–90°Non-ferrous metals, soft cast iron, plastics, fibre, wood
Flat angle135°–150°Hard, tough materials

Cutting fluid lubricates the chips, cools the lips, chips and work, washes chips away so flutes don't clog, improves the hole finish, increases drill life (lips don't overheat and soften) and stops the work warping.

OperationWhat it doesSpeed
CountersinkingCone-shaped chamfer (90° or 120° tool) so a countersunk screw or rivet head sits flush; also deburrs holesAbout ⅓ of drilling speed (avoids chatter)
CounterboringEnlarges the end of a hole to a flat-bottomed recess for a cheese/socket head screw; a pilot keeps it centredAbout ¼ of drilling speed
Spot facingMachines a smooth flat seat around a hole so a washer, bolt head or nut sits squarely—

Use the machine's depth stop when countersinking several identical holes.

recap: The general-purpose drill point angle is ___°.
Flutes let coolant in and ___ out.

topics.title: Cutting Speed & Spindle Speed
topics.zh: 切削速度与主轴转速

sections.b:
The aim is to remove the most metal in a given time without resharpening the drill too often. That needs a correctly sharpened drill and the right combination of speed, feed and cutting fluid.

The outer corner of each lip works hardest: in one revolution it travels πd, while the mid-point of the lip travels only πd/2. So the recommended speed is the ideal cutting speed for the outer corners.

Material (HSS drill)Cutting speed
Mild steel25–30 m/min
Cast iron20–30 m/min
Brass40–60 m/min
Aluminium60–90 m/min
N = 1000 × V / (π × d)spindle speed in rpm
UnitsN — revolutions per minute (rpm) †V — metre per minute (m/min) †d — millimetre (mm)† not an SI unit, but it is the unit your notes use
V = π × d × N / 1000cutting speed in m/min
UnitsV — metre per minute (m/min) †d — millimetre (mm)N — revolutions per minute (rpm) †† not an SI unit, but it is the unit your notes use

FaultResult
Speed too highOuter corners wear and break down; discoloration is a warning sign
Feed too highAbnormal end thrust breaks the chisel point and lips; drill splits up the centre
Lip clearance too largeLittle support behind the edge → quick dulling, short life
Lip clearance too smallDrill rubs behind the edge, works hard, heats up, more thrust → poor holes, breakage
Improper web thinningMore stock taken from one edge than the other
Lips at unequal anglesOne edge works harder → bell-mouthed holes, fast dulling
Lips of unequal lengthPoint off-centre → oversize holes

Never use a hard-faced hammer to fit a drill, and don't let a drill drop onto the machine table when removing it — the chisel edge may be damaged.

worked.q: Notes example: rpm of a 6.35 mm drill at 30.48 m/min.
Exercise 1 — complete the table: (1) 12 mm mild steel 30 m/min, (2) 9 mm cast iron 30 m/min, (3) 20 mm brass 50 m/min, (4) 6 mm aluminium 80 m/min.
Exercises 2–4: (2) 10 mm hole in mild steel at 30 m/min; (3) Ø22 mm at 30 m/min — choose 330/430/530/630 rpm; (4) cutting speed of a Ø20 mm drill at 400 rpm.

Discoloured outer corners mean the speed is too ___.

topics.title: ISO Limits & Fits
topics.zh: ISO 极限与配合

sections.b:
Limits and fits allow mass production, easy assembly, lower cost and interchangeable replacement parts. The ISO system sets recommended limits so parts from different makers fit.

TermMeaningExample: Ø20 ± 0.2 shaft
Nominal sizeSize used to identify the part20 mm shaft
Basic sizeSize from which the limits are derived20 mm
High limitLargest size allowed20.2 mm
Low limitSmallest size allowed19.8 mm
ToleranceHigh limit − low limit0.4 mm
AllowanceDifference in size between mating parts that gives the class of fitsee below
Max allowance = hole high limit − shaft low limit
Unitsallowance, limits — millimetre (mm)
Min allowance = hole low limit − shaft high limit
Unitsallowance, limits — millimetre (mm)

Positive allowance = clearance (shaft smaller than hole). Negative allowance = interference (shaft bigger than hole).

FitMaximum allowanceMinimum allowance
Clearance fitPositivePositive
Transition fitPositiveNegative
Interference fitNegativeNegative

worked.q: Notes: shaft Ø20 +0 / −0.02, hole Ø20 +0.02 / +0.01. Find the allowances and the type of fit.
worked.s:
Shaft: 19.98–20.00; hole: 20.01–20.02
Max allowance = 20.02 − 19.98 = +0.04 mm
Min allowance = 20.01 − 20.00 = +0.01 mm
Both positive → clearance fit

worked.q: Shaft Ø25.02–25.04, hole Ø25.00–25.03. Find the fit.
worked.s:
Max allowance = 25.03 − 25.02 = +0.01 mm
Min allowance = 25.00 − 25.04 = −0.04 mm
One positive, one negative → transition fit

topics.title: Fasteners
topics.zh: 紧固件

sections.b:
FastenerDescription and use
Machine screwGeneral assembly; slotted or recessed heads in many styles; nuts sold separately
Machine boltSquare or hex head with a nut; parts that don't need close tolerances
Cap screwPasses through a clearance hole and screws into a tapped hole in the other part — no nut; closer tolerances, better finish (hex, socket, flat, fillister, button heads)
Set screwHeat-treated; stops pulleys or collars slipping on shafts; classified by head and point style
StudHeadless, threaded both ends or full length; one end into a tapped hole, nut on the other (e.g. engine heads)
Thread-forming screwForms its own thread as it is driven — no tapping; self-drilling versions drill their own hole too
Thread-cutting screwHardened; actually cuts a thread — heavy sheet metal and non-ferrous parts
Drive screwHammered into a drilled or punched hole — permanent

• Standard hex nut — regular (only threads machined), regular semi-finished (bearing face machined) or finished (closer tolerances).
  • Jam nut — thinner, locks a full nut in place. Castellated / slotted nut — a cotter pin through the slots and bolt stops it loosening under vibration. Self-locking nut — nylon insert or deformed thread; no hole needed. Cap (acorn) nut — neat appearance, no sharp exposed edges. Wing nut — tightened by hand for quick adjustment.
  • Inserts (e.g. Heli-Coil) give strong threads in soft metal and plastic, and repair stripped threads.
  • Washers spread the load over a larger area and prevent marring. Lock washers stop nuts loosening: split-ring, external tooth (greatest resistance), internal tooth (small heads, hidden teeth), internal-external (oversize holes), countersunk (flat/oval heads).

FastenerUse
Solid rivetPermanent joint, set by hand or machine
Blind rivetJoint reachable from one side only; needs a special setting tool
Dowel pinFitted in reamed holes to locate mating parts accurately; may carry much of the load
Cotter pinThrough a cross-drilled hole to stop parts slipping or falling off a shaft (standard, humped, clinch, hitch)
Retaining ring (circlip)Internal or external, usually in a groove, to hold parts on a shaft or in a bore; self-locking types need no groove

recap: A ___ nut is used with a cotter pin.
A ___ rivet is used when only one side is accessible.

topics.title: Cutting Screw Threads
topics.zh: 螺纹加工

sections.b:
Threads are cut by tapping (internal), die threading (external) or on a lathe. Hand taps (high-carbon or HSS) come in sets of three:

TapTaperUse
Taper tap8–10 threads taperedUsed first; starts easily; cannot reach the bottom of a blind hole
Intermediate (second) tap3–4 threads chamferedFinishes through holes; taps soft material directly; reaches almost the bottom of a blind hole
Bottoming tapFull thread to the endFinal tap; threads a blind hole to full depth

Tap wrenches: bar type (two jaws, one sliding; smallest takes 3–13 mm taps) and T-type (small chuck on a stem, for confined spaces, up to 13 mm).

Clamp the work; drill the correct tap-drill size
Start the taper tap with downward pressure while turning
Check it is square with a try square in two positions 90° apart; correct with slightly more pressure on one side
Turn one full turn clockwise, then a quarter turn back to break the chip; use cutting fluid
Blind hole: put a nut on the tap as a depth stop; clear chips often — invert the work, use a magnet or a bent wire; never blow chips out with compressed air
Change to the intermediate, then the bottoming tap as each reaches depth

sections.h: Tap drill size and tapping problems
sections.b:
An accurate, full thread needs a hole drilled to the thread's minor diameter; this drill is the tap drill.

Tap drill = major diameter − pitchmetric threads
Unitstap drill, major diameter, pitch — millimetre (mm)
ProblemResult
Drill too smallThreads may break, tap may break or ream instead of cutting
Drill not ground correctly → out-of-round holeUneven thread depth
Dull drill work-hardens the hole surfaceTap hard to start, threads chip, tap may break
Swarf left in a blind holeTap jams on packed swarf and breaks

A tap extractor has fingers that slide into the flutes of a broken tap to unscrew it.

• A die (hardened and tempered alloy tool steel) has accurate internal threads, three or more flutes forming cutting edges and chip spaces, a chamfered leading end for easy starting, and a split for small size adjustment.
  • The die stock (mild steel or malleable iron) holds and turns the die, has screws to adjust the die size and knurled handles.
  • Split die (HSS) — the common die for cutting external threads; tapered leading face. Solid die nut — only for repairing damaged threads, not cutting new ones.
  • Roughing: leading (tapered) face toward the work — cannot thread fully up to a shoulder. Finishing: reverse the die to thread up to the shoulder; adjust the stock screws for correct depth.
  • Check the thread with a screw pitch gauge (0.35–6 mm) or by trying a nut.

worked.q: Find the tap drill for M10 × 1.5 (notes), M6 × 1.0 and M12 × 1.75.

recap: The first tap used is the ___ tap.
A solid die nut is only for ___ threads.

topics.title: Bearings
topics.zh: 轴承

sections.b:
Bearings support moving parts, reduce friction and wear, and provide a replaceable wear surface.

Plain bearing (bushing)Anti-friction (rolling) bearing
ContactSlidingRolling — balls or rollers
AdvantagesLittle radial space, low cost, quiet, rigidLow friction, can be packed (less lubrication), many designs, less axial space
DisadvantagesHigher friction, frequent lubrication, more axial spaceMore radial space, noisier, higher cost, less rigid

Loads on bearings: radial (sideways, at 90° to the shaft), axial / thrust (along the shaft), or combined.

Plain bearing types: solid sleeve (copper, brass, bronze — radial only); flanged sleeve (radial + thrust); fluted rubber, water-lubricated (radial); split bearings (metal, wood, plastic or rubber — e.g. crankshaft bearings); steel-backed bronze-lined; rolled (wrapped) bushes.

BearingRadial loadThrust loadNotes
Deep-groove ballHeavyYes, both directionsMost common; single or double row
Self-aligning ballYesLittleOuter race swivels to allow slight misalignment
Angular-contact ballYesOne direction onlyUsed in pairs for two-way thrust
Thrust ballNoYesOnly where there is no radial load
Spherical rollerVery heavyHeavyLarge contact area; tolerates some misalignment
Cylindrical rollerHighNoneHighest-speed roller bearing; can come apart under thrust
Tapered rollerHeavyHeavy, one directionFitted in opposed pairs; adjustable (car wheel bearings)
Needle rollerHighNoLong thin rollers; often no inner race — the shaft is the inner race; for limited space

• Removal: mechanical or hydraulic pullers (impact pullers for small bearings, screw pullers for most jobs, puller plates to push on the inner race when the bearing is to be reused); mechanical (arbor) or hydraulic presses; or hammer and driver if nothing else is available. When pressing a bearing off a shaft, support the inner race.
  • Fitting: arbor press, push puller, or hammer and tube. Press only on the race that is being fitted — the outer race into a housing, the inner race onto a shaft. Never transmit force through the balls.
  • Maintenance: correct lubrication, cleanliness, correct shaft and housing fits, burr-free mounting.
  • Warning signs: rising temperature, excessive noise, rough running, excessive clearance. Plain bearing failures: dirt, lack of lubrication, improper assembly, misalignment, overheating, corrosion.

recap: Cylindrical roller bearings carry ___ thrust load.
When fitting onto a shaft, press on the ___ race.

topics.title: Gears
topics.zh: 齿轮

sections.b:
Gears are a positive drive: toothed discs transmit power with no slip. They transmit power between shafts and change speed, torque or direction (a gearbox). They need correct operation, cleanliness and proper tooth engagement.

GearShaftsKey points
SpurParallelTeeth parallel to the axis; low cost, easy to make and maintain, no side thrust
HelicalParallel (or non-intersecting at an angle)Teeth at a helix angle; longer teeth, more contact — stronger, smoother, quieter, good at high speed; produces axial thrust
HerringboneParallelDouble helical; the thrusts cancel
InternalParallelTeeth cut inside a ring
Rack and pinion—Converts rotary ↔ linear motion
BevelIntersecting (usually 90°)High power capacity, smooth, high-speed use
WormAt 90° but not intersectingVery high speed reduction in one step; quiet, steady output with no pulsation

N1 × T1 = N2 × T2speed × teeth is the same for meshing gears
UnitsN1, N2 — revolutions per minute (rpm) †T1, T2 — number of teeth, no unit† not an SI unit, but it is the unit your notes use
  • Simple train — each gear on its own shaft. Idler gears do not change the final speed; they change the direction of rotation and bridge the gap between driver and driven.
  • Compound train — two or more gears on one shaft turn at the same speed (N2 = N3), so N4 = N2 × T3/T4 = N1 × (T1/T2) × (T3/T4). This gives big reductions in a small space.
  • Gear ratio = driven teeth ÷ driver teeth = driver speed ÷ driven speed.
In the notes' lathe example the "where" list swaps NA and NB. With A the driving gear on the spindle: TA/TB = NB/NA, where NA is the driver (spindle) speed and NB the driven (leadscrew) speed — the same as NATA = NBTB.

SignCause
Corrosion (pitting)Acid, alkali or moisture contamination
CrackingFaulty heat treatment (quench cracks), overload, bad design
FractureSudden shock load, overload, misalignment
Bent teethOverload, misalignment
Burning (discoloured teeth)Overload, excessive speed or faulty lubrication
Abrasive wearGritty particles in the oil

Misalignment means shafts out of line, gears mounted eccentrically, or gears not fully (or too deeply) in mesh.

Maintenance: check gear and shaft alignment; check and set the correct backlash; check the gearbox oil level and top up; drain and change the oil at regular intervals.

worked.q: A 20-tooth driver at 600 rpm meshes with a 60-tooth gear. Find the driven speed and the gear ratio.
worked.s:
N2 = N1 × T1 ÷ T2 = 600 × 20 ÷ 60 = 200 rpm
Gear ratio = 60 ÷ 20 = 3 : 1 (speed reduced 3 times)

worked.q: Simple train: driver 30 T at 900 rpm → idler 45 T → driven 15 T. Find the driven speed and direction.
worked.s:
The idler does not affect speed: N3 = 900 × 30 ÷ 15 = 1800 rpm
With one idler, the driven gear turns the SAME direction as the driver.

worked.q: Compound train: T1 = 20 (driver, 1500 rpm), T2 = 60, T3 = 25 on the same shaft as T2, T4 = 75. Find N4.

recap: An idler gear changes the ___ but not the speed.
Worm gears give a very high speed ___.

topics.title: Belt Drives
topics.zh: 带传动

sections.b:
TermMeaning
Driver sheaveOn the motor; usually the smallest pulley with the highest rpm
Driven sheaveOn the machine; usually the largest pulley with the lowest rpm
Idler sheaveRegulates tension, detours the belt, reduces vibration, provides take-up
Pitch lengthBelt length at its neutral axis (about ⅔ of the way up from the bottom of a V-belt)
Pitch diameterPulley diameter where the belt's neutral axis contacts it
Arc of contactDegrees of wrap round the pulley — less wrap, less power capacity
Centre distanceDistance between the driver and driven shaft centres
Speed ratiorpm of the fast shaft ÷ rpm of the slow shaft
Tight side / slack sideBelt being pulled into the driver / leaving the driver toward the driven pulley
Slip / creepSlip: belt slides on the pulley from too little tension (correctable). Creep: small movement of the belt on the pulley face from stretching (cannot be corrected)
N1 × D1 = N2 × D2speed × pulley diameter is the same on both pulleys
UnitsN1, N2 — revolutions per minute (rpm) †D1, D2 — millimetre (mm)† not an SI unit, but it is the unit your notes use

Belt drives need no lubrication. Because they work by friction, a belt can slip if the driven machine is overloaded — which protects the drive.

The notes list "no belt slip when the driven shaft is overloaded" as an advantage. That is the wrong way round: friction belts do slip under overload, and that slip acts as overload protection. Chapter 13 says the same — chains "cannot provide slippage, which is sometimes desirable (for overload protection)".

BeltFeaturesCare
FlatSlips more easily, needs high tension (high bearing loads), no misalignment, noisier (belt slap); leather, rubber or canvasKeep tight, clean (avoid glazing), dress leather belts occasionally, keep cool and dry
V-beltMost widely used: less slip, lower tension than flat, tolerates slight misalignment, quiet, no dressing. Light duty (2L–5L, 3M–11M), standard (A–E), high capacityKeep free of oil, grease and dirt; never apply belt dressing
Timing (toothed)Positive, slip-proof engagement for timing; lower tension than V-belts, less bearing load, no chatter, very small backlash, no lubricationCorrect tension and alignment
RibbedFlat belt with V-ribs — combines flexibility with grip—
V-belt installation
Turn off (and lock off) the power
Inspect and clean the sheaves
Use the correct belt for the sheave
Slacken the take-up and fit the belts — never lever them on
Take up until snug; check belt and sheave alignment
Adjust to the proper tension
Re-check and readjust after several days of running

Misalignment types: angular, parallel and sheave misalignment. Check with a string across the pulley faces (touching four points), string and two squares, or a machinist's level and bars/rule.

Idlers should be avoided if correct tension can be kept. Inside idler: slack side, near the large sheave, at least as big as the small sheave. Backside idler: close to the small sheave, ≥ 1.5 × small sheave diameter. Kiss idler: controls vibration and whip, ≈ 1.5 × small sheave diameter.

worked.q: Notes: driver 200 mm at 600 rpm, driven 300 mm. Find N2 and the speed ratio.
worked.s:
N2 = N1 × D1 ÷ D2 = 600 × 200 ÷ 300 = 400 rpm
Speed ratio = 600 ÷ 400 = 1.5 (speed reduced 1.5 times)

worked.q: A 1450 rpm motor must drive a fan at 580 rpm. The motor pulley is 100 mm. Find the fan pulley diameter.

recap: Never apply belt dressing to a ___ belt.

topics.title: Chain Drives
topics.zh: 链传动

sections.b:
Roller chain is a flexible, positive drive for shafts at long centre distances (forklifts, cement mixers, photocopiers). The rollers turn on bushings, so contact with the sprocket is rolling rather than sliding — less friction, higher efficiency, longer life. A chain is made of pin links and roller links (side plates joined by pins, rollers over the bushings).

Chain driveCompared with a belt drive
Positive contact, no slipMore efficient; suits low speed, high torque
No tension needed when idleChain weight provides take-up on the slack side
Chains stretch with wearOccasional tension adjustment needed
Can be joined in placeEasy assembly and removal
AdvantagesDisadvantages
CompactVery little misalignment allowed
InexpensiveNoisy
Withstands heat, dirt and weather when lubricatedNeeds frequent lubrication
—Cannot slip, so gives no overload protection

Sprockets: detachable-hub (flat, bolted to a flange; also in friction clutches), single-hub (flat on one side so it sits close to the machine), double-hub (driven sprockets carrying more weight).

Components of roller chain

ProblemEffects
MisalignmentNoise, stiff joints, wear on sprocket tooth sides and inside the link plates
Worn chainNoise, rides high on the teeth, jumps teeth, broken components
Wrong tensionNoise, wear inside roller link plates, climbs the teeth, chain whip
Poor lubricationRuns hot, stiff joints, noisy
  • Cleaning: remove the chain, soak it rolled up in cleaning agent, hang it vertically, scrub with a stiff brush, rinse in fresh cleaner. Oiling: soak in an oil bath for several hours.
  • Wear check: stretch — compare compressed and stretched lengths; bend — bend the chain sideways; more curvature means more wear.
  • Sprocket wear: pointed or hooked teeth → replace the sprocket.
  • Alignment: straight edge across both sprocket faces.
  • Tension: push the mid-point of the span in, pull it out, note the total deflection. To adjust: slacken the clamping bolts, move the unit with the adjusting screws, tighten the bolts evenly so it stays aligned, re-check.

recap: Chain drives are ___ drives — no slip.
Pointed or hooked sprocket teeth mean the sprocket is ___.

topics.title: Couplings
topics.zh: 联轴器

sections.b:
Couplings give a semi-permanent connection between shafts, disconnected only for repair or maintenance.

TypeWhenExamples
RigidAccurate axial alignment can be guaranteedSolid flange coupling, sleeve coupling
FlexibleSlight misalignment may occurSpider (jaw), Oldham, chain, gear, flexible (rubber) joints
Universal jointLarge angular misalignment — more than 2–3°, up to about 20°Hooke's joint (two forks and a cross), ball joint

Flexible couplings: allow slight misalignment (e.g. bearing wear), allow end-play for thermal expansion, damp out vibration and starting shock, and can electrically insulate one shaft from the other.

  • Spider coupling — misalignment beyond its rating wears the spider's load faces rapidly.
  • Oldham coupling — parallel misalignment only; angular misalignment wears its front face; needs lubrication.
  • Chain coupling — two sprocket hubs joined by a double-strand roller chain.
  • Gear coupling — needs lubrication; covers have grease fittings and seals.
  • Flexible joint — metal hubs with a rubber or elastic member; also cushions sudden load changes.

• Parallel — shafts parallel but displaced sideways. Angular — shafts not parallel. Combined — parallel in one plane and angular in another.
  • Even flexible couplings last longer the better the alignment. Vertical misalignment is usually corrected with shims (thin sheet-metal pieces) under the feet.
MethodChecksAccuracy
Straight edge + feeler gaugesVertical or horizontal alignmentBasic
Vernier height gaugeVertical alignment onlyBetter
Dial test indicatorVertical and horizontalMost accurate

recap: An Oldham coupling suits ___ misalignment only.
The most accurate alignment tool is the ___.

topics.title: Lubrication
topics.zh: 润滑

sections.b:
Lubrication reduces friction and wear, reduces noise, damps shock loads, prevents rust and corrosion, cools moving parts and seals out dirt.

LubricantNotes
Mineral oilRefined from crude petroleum, with additives
Animal / vegetable oilFrom natural sources (animal tissue, fish oil, plants)
SyntheticMade from chemical compounds; expensive but very good at high temperatures (over about 200 °C)
Light oilThin — high speed, light loads (spindle bearings)
Medium oilCrankcases; main bearings and stressed parts
Heavy oilThick — slow speed, heavy loads (gearing, power transmission)

Special-purpose oils: hydraulic oil (transmits power — never mix with other oils or fluids), cutting oil, rust-preventive coatings for stored parts, flushing oil to clean recirculating systems.

PropertyMeaning
ViscosityResistance to flow
Flash pointTemperature at which vapour from the oil will ignite
Pour pointLowest temperature at which the oil flows under its own weight
OxidationBreakdown of the lubricant by heat and air
PenetrationGrease test — depth a dropped cone sinks shows its thickness
AdditiveSubstance added to improve a particular property

Grease is oil thickened with soap; the soap type sets its properties.

GreasePropertiesUse
Calcium soapVery water-resistant, low melting pointMedium-duty plain and roller bearings
Sodium soap (−30 to 80 °C)High melting point, poor water resistancePlain bearings
Lithium soap (−30 to 110 °C)High melting point and good water resistanceRolling-contact bearings
Aluminium soapInsoluble in waterFast-moving cams, reciprocating parts

Solid lubricants: graphite for high temperatures; molybdenum disulphide for extreme pressures.

Application: brushing, spraying, wiping. The method chosen depends on accessibility, load and speed.

MethodHow it works / where used
Oil bathParts run in oil; low speed only (worm gears, gearboxes)
SplashMoving parts dip into a sump and fling oil to other parts (engines, reciprocating compressors)
RecirculatingTotally enclosed; oil pumped from a sump or tank
Ring, chain or collar feedRing/chain on the shaft lifts oil from a reservoir, or a collar from which oil is scraped — plain bearings at low/medium speed
Wick feed / padSiphon action through a wick, or an oil-soaked felt pad — low supply rates
Drip feed / cup oilerNeedle valve gives a controlled drip to a bearing
Oil mistDry compressed air carries an oil mist (air-line lubricator)
Grease cupSpring- or screw-operated
Grease gunPumps grease through a non-return nipple

Storage: large tanks are rectangular, raised a little to stop the bottom corroding (or up to about 1 m so containers fill by gravity from non-drip taps) and tilted slightly forward so they empty completely. Drums are best racked horizontally with non-drip taps.

recap: Heavy oil suits ___ speed and heavy loads.
___-soap grease is used for rolling bearings.
___ is a solid lubricant for high temperatures.

topics.title: Commissioning, Installation & Maintenance
topics.zh: 调试、安装与维护

sections.b:
Alignment tests check the accuracy of form (roundness, flatness, straightness) and relationship (squareness, parallelism, concentricity) of machine-tool elements, so the machine can produce dimensionally and geometrically accurate work. Examples: true running of the spindle, spindle square with the table, slide parallel or square to the table, straightness and flatness of the table or lathe bed.

Level first with a spirit level so the machine sits on a true horizontal plane — an unlevelled lathe bed will be twisted.

MachineEquipment for alignment tests
Lathe (should turn and bore parallel, face flat)Dial indicator (0.01 mm), spirit level (≈ 0.01 mm/m), test mandrel (≈ 25 mm, taper to fit the spindle, ≈ 300 mm parallel, ground on centres), parallel test bar, straight edge (≈ 300 mm)
Drilling machineTest mandrel to fit the spindle taper, dial indicator set with attachment, block square (square frame with spirit levels)

Commissioning tests installed (or nearly complete) equipment to verify it works to its design objectives, so it can be handed over properly. A documented approach gives traceable verification, avoids oversights, eliminates start-up problems and supports regulatory documentation.

StepActivity
1 Pre-designSet and communicate the basis for judging final performance
2 DesignDevelop and document the commissioning requirements
3 ConstructionMake sure the work is installed to specification
4 AcceptanceTest performance and train the operators
5 Post-acceptanceMaintain, keep records, re-test periodically

Procedure: finalise the machining sequence, prepare log sheets, analyse requirements, start up each system to plan, integrate systems (feeds, monitor parameters, correct I/O signals), reliability run, installation and axis alignment, functional test of machine and control system, connect and test I/O devices.

Tasks: position and align parts, level the machine, tighten fasteners, move and lift the machine, clean it, connect electrical terminals, test-run.

Validation = objective evidence that a requirement for a specific use can be consistently met: the equipment can operate within the required parameters, and its control, monitoring and measuring instruments can too.

Maintenance is work to keep or restore every facility to an acceptable standard. Planned maintenance is organised and carried out with forethought, control and records: the policy is considered, planned in advance, controlled to the plan, and recorded to guide future policy.

TermMeaning
PreventiveDirected at preventing failure
RunningCan be done while the facility is in service
Shut-downCan only be done when the facility is out of service
CorrectiveRestores a facility to an acceptable standard
Breakdown (planned corrective)Done after a failure, but with spares, labour and equipment prepared in advance
Emergency (unplanned)Needed because of an unforeseen breakdown
Down timePeriod when a facility is not available
Schedule / programmeFull list of maintenance and how often / maintenance allocated to specific periods
History cardRecord of all work done on a particular facility
Maintenance
Planned?
No → unplanned emergency maintenance
Preventive (before failure)?
No → planned corrective: breakdown maintenance (spares ready in advance)
Planned preventive → running maintenance (in service) or shut-down maintenance (out of service)

Benefits: fewer breakdowns, maintenance at the most convenient time, less downtime (spares and tools ready), regular servicing cheaper than sudden repairs, higher productivity and quality, labour spread evenly, better morale.

Maintenance done while the facility is in service is ___ maintenance.

topics.title: CAD & 3D Printing
topics.zh: CAD 与 3D 打印

sections.b:
3D printing is a form of additive manufacturing: an object is built from 3D model data by joining material one layer at a time (machining, by contrast, removes material).

ProcessHow it worksMaterialsStrengths
FDM — fused deposition modellingThermoplastic filament is melted and extruded through a nozzle, layer by layerPLA, ABS; can be filled with metal, ceramic, wood or carbon particles, or carbon-fibre reinforcedMost widely used (hobby printers); cheap, quick proof-of-concept and simple prototypes
SLA — stereolithographyA laser cures liquid resin into hard plastic (photopolymerisation)Resins matching many engineering plasticsHighest resolution and accuracy, finest detail, smoothest finish of all plastic printing; versatile materials
SLS — selective laser sinteringA high-power laser fuses small particles of polymer powderPolymer powder (e.g. nylon)Parts are strong; unfused powder supports the part, so no support structures needed
SLS cycle
A thin layer of powder is spread on the build platform and pre-heated to just below melting point
The laser scans the cross-section, heating the powder to (or just below) melting so the particles fuse
The platform lowers one layer; repeat until all layers are done
Parts cool slowly inside the printer
The build chamber goes to a cleaning station; parts are separated and excess powder removed

Why 3D printing is so common: easy to use, affordable, works in offices, labs and homes, turns 3D data straight into solid parts, and is used for concept development, product design, fittings, crafts and jewellery.

recap: SLA cures liquid ___ with a laser.

topics.title: Interpreting Engineering Drawings
topics.zh: 识读工程图

sections.b:
Orthographic projection shows an object as separate 2D views. The object is imagined inside three planes — the vertical plane (VP), horizontal plane (HP) and side vertical plane (SVP) — and the views projected onto them are unfolded flat.

First-angleThird-angle
IdeaObject between the viewer and the plane — each view is projected through the object onto the plane behind itPlane between the viewer and the object — you draw what you see, as if through a glass box
Plan (top view)Drawn below the front viewDrawn above the front view
View from the leftDrawn on the right of the front viewDrawn on the left of the front view

The type of projection must always be stated on a drawing, using its standard symbol (a truncated cone shown in two views). In the first-angle symbol the circles (end view) are on the right of the cone; in the third-angle symbol they are on the left.

sections.h: Third-angle projection — the wording in your notes
sections.b: Whatever your eyes see from that angle is the drawing of that projection. In all drawings, the type of projection must be clearly stated (using the standard projection symbol).

In third-angle projection the plan is drawn ___ the front view.
The type of projection must be shown with its ___.

topics.title: 3D Modelling in SolidWorks
topics.zh: SolidWorks 三维建模

sections.b:
• Menus give access to every command (Windows conventions; right-click for context menus).
  • Toolbars are grouped by function (Sketch, Assembly…); they can be docked, floated, customised, and remember their layout. Hover for tooltips.
  • Heads-up View toolbar — transparent toolbar in the graphics area for view commands (fly-out buttons have a small arrow).
  • CommandManager — context-sensitive toolbar whose tabs change with the document type (part, assembly, drawing) — e.g. the Features tab shows feature tools.
  • Feedback while you work: pointers, inference lines and previews.

Choose a plane or planar face
Sketch a 2D profile (lines, circles, arcs, slots, rectangles, centre lines)
Add dimensions and relations until the sketch is fully defined (black lines)
Turn it into a feature — e.g. Extruded Boss/Base, cut, fillet
Combine features to make a part
Mate parts together into an assembly
Create 2D engineering drawings from parts or assemblies
  • Sketch colours: blue = under-defined (can still move); black = fully defined. Starting a rectangle at the origin makes that corner coincident with the origin, which constrains it.
  • Smart Dimension: select an entity, click to place the dimension, type the value in the Modify box.
  • Extruded Boss/Base: End Condition Blind with a depth (e.g. 30 mm); the new feature appears in the FeatureManager design tree.
  • Editing: right-click a feature in the design tree → Edit Feature to change it (e.g. fillet radii).
  • View styles: shaded, shaded with edges, hidden lines removed, hidden lines visible, wireframe. Normal To faces a plane straight on; Zoom to Fit shows the whole model.
