Features are listed in the FeatureManager design ___.

topics.title: Workplace Safety & Safe Work in Pneumatics
topics.zh: 工作场所安全与气动安全作业

sections.b:
The Workplace Safety and Health Act (WSHA) replaced the Factories Act on 1 March 2006. It aims to build a strong safety culture: the organisation must take measures to keep its employees, and anyone else affected by the work, safe and healthy.

Principles of WSH:

  1. Reduce, eliminate or minimise risk.
  2. Industry takes greater ownership of safety and health.
  3. Higher penalties for poor safety and health management.

Every person must take reasonably practicable steps to ensure safety and health at work. Compared with the prescriptive Factories Act, the WSHA specifies liabilities for a range of persons, focuses on safety goals and systems, and stipulates greater penalties.

sections.h: Safe work procedures with compressed air
sections.b:
Compressed air is not "just air": it is a focused, high-velocity stream that can seriously injure or kill. Fooling around with it can be lethal.

  1. Work on the pneumatic system only under a trainer’s supervision.
  2. Do not exceed the maximum permissible pressure of 600 kPa (6 bar).
  3. Turn on the air only after all tubing is connected and secured.
  4. Never disconnect tubing while it is under pressure.
  5. Isolate and bleed all lines before disconnecting a circuit; turn the air off before altering it.
  6. Use the shortest possible tubing.
  7. Never blow compressed air at anyone.
  8. Keep fingers clear of piston rods — cylinders may advance and retract automatically.
  9. If a tube slips off, switch the air supply off immediately.

There is no standard written specifically for pneumatic safety, so guidance comes from general engineering regulations. Before maintenance: isolate the system and exhaust it totally before dismantling.

Air stored in receivers, pipes and tubing is effectively a pressure vessel. When a line is opened, the stored energy escapes in a very short time — a loose tube can whiplash, and the blast can throw particles into the eyes. Inspect receivers regularly and think before opening any connection.

Cylinder force is often underestimated. The notes: a 40 mm bore at 6 bar lifts about 75 kg, a 50 mm bore about 117 kg — enough to lift a person. (Check: F = P × A = 600 000 × π × 0.02² ≈ 754 N ≈ 77 kgf.)

  • Set the working pressure at the minimum needed for the task, plus a small margin.
  • Never remove or tamper with safety guards. Think before you act.

terms: 工作场所安全与卫生法
recap: The WSHA replaced the Factories Act on 1 March ___.
Maximum permissible pressure in the lab is ___ bar.
Before disconnecting a circuit, isolate and ___ all air lines.

topics.title: Compressed Air & Pressure
topics.zh: 压缩空气与压力

sections.b:
In a pneumatic system compressed air is the working medium: it controls automated machines and powers air tools such as drills and hammers.

AdvantagesDisadvantages
Amount — available everywhere, unlimitedPreparation — must be free of dirt and moisture or components wear
Transport — easily piped; no return line neededCompressibility — uniform, constant piston speed is not possible
Storage — kept in a receiver; compressor need not run all the timeForce limit — economical only up to about 20 000–30 000 N (at about 7 bar)
Temperature — insensitive to temperature changesExhaust noise — loud, but solved largely by silencers
Explosion-proof — no fire or explosion risk
Clean — leaks do not contaminate (food, textiles, wood)
Simple construction — inexpensive components
Speed — cylinders run at about 1–2 m/s
Overload safe — can be loaded until they stall

Air is invisible, colourless, odourless and tasteless: about 78 % nitrogen, 21 % oxygen and 1 % carbon dioxide, water vapour and other gases. Releasing it to atmosphere is safe.

Pressure is force per unit area.

P = F / A1 bar = 100 000 Pa = 100 kPa = 10⁵ N/m²
UnitsP — pascal = N/m² (Pa)F — newton (N)A — square metre (m²)
Pressure unitForceArea
psilbin²
kg/cm²kgcm²
Pa (pascal) = N/m²Nm²
kPa = kN/m²kNm²

The pascal is tiny, so kPa or bar are used. In the notes 1 kg/cm² = 1 bar — this is why the worked examples give forces in kg-force (kgf).

Unit drill (notes’ exercise): 1 kN/m² = 1000 N/m² · 1 kPa = 1000 Pa · 80 N/m² = 0.08 kN/m² · 2.5 kPa = 2500 Pa · 900 N/m² = 0.9 kN/m² · 2.5 kg/cm² ≈ 2.5 bar ≈ 250 kN/m².

• Atmospheric pressure — the weight of the air above each m² of the earth’s surface: 1.013 bar at sea level (≈ 1 bar).
  • Gauge pressure — what a pressure gauge reads: pressure above (or below) atmospheric. A gauge reading of zero means atmospheric. Below atmospheric is called vacuum.
  • Absolute pressure — measured from a perfect vacuum.
Pabs = Patm + PgaugePabs = Patm − Pvacuum
UnitsPabs, Patm, Pgauge, Pvacuum — bar; 1 bar = 100 000 Pa (bar) †† not an SI unit, but it is the unit your notes use

Rearranging P = F/A gives F = P × A. On the extend stroke the air acts on the whole piston area A. On the return stroke the rod occupies area a, so the air only pushes on the annulus (A − a).

Extend: F = P × ARetract: F = P × (A − a)A = πD² / 4
UnitsF — newton (N)P — pascal = N/m² (Pa)A, a — square metre (m²)D — metre (m)

The notes’ examples (1 bar ≈ 1 kg/cm²):

  • 6 bar, A = 10 cm², a = 2 cm² → forward 6 × 10 = 60 kgf; return 6 × (10 − 2) = 48 kgf.
  • 40 bar, A = 15 cm², a = 4 cm² → pulling force 40 × 11 = 440 kgf.
  • 20 kg/cm² on a 50 cm² piston → maximum load 20 × 50 = 1000 kgf.
  • Needed 5000 kgf at 100 bar → A = F/P = 5000/100 = 50 cm².
Section 8.01(d) of the notes prints "Force = Pressure / Area (Refer to Chapter 1)". The correct relation is Force = Pressure × Area, and it is in Chapter 2.

worked.q: A force of 7000 N acts on 0.01 m². Find the pressure in kPa and bar.
500 N acts on 1 cm². Find the pressure in bar.
5 bar acts on 1 cm². What force does it exert?
300 N acts on a circular face of 20 mm diameter. Find the pressure.
A gauge reads 6 bar. What is the absolute pressure?
worked.s: Pabs = 1.013 + 6 ≈ 7 bar abs.

recap: The return force of a single-rod cylinder is P × (A − ___).

topics.title: Air Compressors
topics.zh: 空气压缩机

sections.b:
The compressor is the heart of the air supply. It draws in atmospheric air, squeezes it into a smaller volume to raise its pressure, and delivers it to an air receiver for temporary storage.

TypeHow it worksNotes
Single-stage pistonPiston moves down → inlet valve opens, air drawn in; piston moves up → inlet closes, air compressed, outlet valve opens to the receiver3–7 bar. Valves open and close by pressure difference, not mechanically. Crankshaft driven by motor or engine.
Two-stage pistonStage 1 compresses to about 3 bar; air cooled in an intercooler; smaller stage-2 cylinder takes it to about 7 barMore efficient than single-stage; delivery temperature about 120 °C
DiaphragmA diaphragm changes the chamber volume — intake on the down stroke, compression on the up strokeUp to 5 bar, totally oil-free (food, pharmaceutical, chemical)
Rotary vaneEccentric rotor with sliding vanes; the space between vanes shrinks from inlet to outletCompact, quiet, smooth steady delivery
Rotary screwTwo meshing helical rotors turn in opposite directions; trapped air is squeezed axiallyContinuous pulse-free flow, over 400 m³/min, up to 10 bar. Dry type uses timing gears (no lubrication); oil-flooded type is more efficient but needs oil separators.
The notes print the two-stage delivery temperature as "1200C"; it means 120 °C.

• Check the air-intake filter for blockage; clean or replace the cartridge.
  • Check the crankcase oil level; top up. Change oil at the recommended interval, and if it is contaminated with water.
  • Check the compressor and fittings for oil, water and air leaks.
  • Clean the crankcase air breather regularly.
  • Check and adjust belt tension; replace worn belts.
  • Clean the cooling fins and fan.

Compressor delivery must be matched to demand.

MethodHow
No-load: exhaustAt the set receiver pressure a relief (safety) valve opens and the compressor blows to atmosphere; a check valve stops the receiver emptying (very small plants only)
No-load: shut-offThe suction side is closed; the compressor keeps running in vacuum and cannot draw air in
No-load: grip-armOn piston compressors the suction valve is held open by a grip arm, so no air is compressed
Speed regulationThe speed of the engine driving the compressor is changed by hand or automatically from the working pressure
On-off regulationTwo states — full load or standstill. The motor switches off at Pmax and on again at Pmin

topics.title: Compressed Air Treatment
topics.zh: 压缩空气的处理

sections.b:
• Clean — dirt wears seals, wedges into clearances and blocks passages.
  • Cool — hot air makes pipes expand, then contract at shutdown; repeated, this loosens joints and causes leaks.
  • Dry — water washes away lubricant, increases wear and air consumption, can freeze at tool exhausts, spoils products in spraying and cleaning, and corrodes pipes. The cheapest first step is after-cooling.

ItemPurpose and facts
IntercoolerCools air between stages of a multistage compressor → cooled air is easier to compress further, raising overall efficiency
After-coolerHeat exchanger after the final stage, between compressor and receiver. Cooling makes moisture and oil droplets condense so they can be drained. Water-cooled: air ends about 10 °C above the cooling water; air-cooled: 12–16 °C above ambient. Needs a moisture separator, preferably with automatic drain.
Air receiver(1) reserve for sudden heavy demand; (2) prevents too-frequent loading/unloading of the compressor; (3) damps pulsations → steady pressure; (4) lets residual moisture and oil drop out. Inlet below the centre, outlet near the top. Legal fittings: stop valve, safety valve, inlet, pressure gauge, manhole, drain cock, name-plate.
Moisture separatorUses the density difference between air and water. Centrifugal: a spiral plate swirls the air, droplets are thrown to the wall. Baffle: baffles change the flow direction, droplets stick and run down. Water leaves through a manual or automatic drain trap.

A good after-cooler condenses up to 90 % of the water vapour. Without further drying, more water condenses as the air cools in the pipes. A dryer is installed between the receiver and the distribution system.

MethodPrincipleFeatures
Absorption (chemical)A drying agent (flux) combines with the water and drains to a collection chamber; the flux is used up and must be replacedSimple installation, low wear (no moving parts), no external energy. Flux use is least at about 20 °C inlet temperature.
Adsorption (physical, regenerative)Water is deposited on the porous surface of a granular gel; warm air regenerates the saturated bedUsually two dryers in parallel — one drying while the other regenerates. Replace the gel every 2–3 years.
Refrigeration (low temperature)Air is cooled below its dew point (to about 1.7 °C) so water condenses; incoming warm air is pre-cooled by the outgoing cold dry airPre-cooling means the refrigerator works at only about 40 % capacity. Needs a pre-filter to keep oil and dirt off the heat-exchanger walls.

Air picks up dirt and condenses more water in the pipes, so each outlet has an air service unit (FRL): stop valve → filter → pressure regulator → lubricator (optional).

  • Filter — stops solid contaminants, condenses and removes water vapour, arrests sub-micron particles.
  • Pressure regulator — keeps the operating (secondary) pressure virtually constant despite changes in line (primary) pressure and air consumption. Adjusting screw on a diaphragm.
  • Lubricator — injects a fine oil mist (about one drop per minute) to reduce wear and friction and protect against corrosion.

Distribution mains slope 1–2 % in the direction of flow so that gravity and the air flow carry condensate to drain points at the lowest places.

recap: An after-cooler can condense up to ___ % of the water vapour.
The regenerative dryer is the ___ type.

topics.title: Basic Pneumatic System & Symbols
topics.zh: 基本气动系统与符号

sections.b:
Air service unit — clean, dry air at the correct pressure
Directional control valve — start/stop, extend/retract, direction of rotation
Flow control valve — regulates the volume of air → actuator speed
Actuator — linear (cylinder) or rotary; does the useful work

Everyday uses: tyres, vehicle and train brakes, bus doors, air tools, spray guns, dental equipment. Industrial uses: pushing, drilling and forming, testing and quality control, feeding, positioning and sorting, pick-and-place with rotary actuators, and portable air tools (drills, screwdrivers, wrenches) driven by air motors.

From your annotations: in the one-way flow control valve the flow in one direction passes the adjustable throttle (controlled), while flow in the other direction lifts the check valve and returns freely. The silencer on a valve exhaust is replaced when the valve is serviced.

GroupMembers
Energy conversion & preparationCompressor, receiver, filter, water separator, lubricator, pressure regulator, service unit, dryer
Non-return valvesCheck valve, shuttle valve (OR), two-pressure valve (AND), quick exhaust valve
Flow controlThrottle valve (both directions), one-way flow control valve (throttle + check)
Pressure valvesPressure regulator, pressure relief (limiting) valve, sequence valve
ActuatorsSingle-acting and double-acting cylinders (with/without cushioning), rotary actuator, air motor

Rotary actuators give fast, small angular movements — standard 45°, 90°, 180° or 360°, easily adjusted. Air motors give unlimited rotation and are one of the most widely used air-driven working elements.

topics.title: Single-Cylinder Circuits
topics.zh: 单气缸回路

sections.b:
CircuitHow it works
Single-acting, directPress the 3/2 valve: air 1→2 extends the cylinder, 3 is blocked. Release: spring resets the valve, cylinder exhausts 2→3.
Double-acting, direct4/2 or 5/2 valve. Actuated: 1→4 (P→A) extends, the other side exhausts. Released: 1→2 retracts.
Single-acting, indirectSmall valve 1.2 sends a pilot signal to Z (12) of the main valve 1.1, which switches the full flow to the cylinder.
Double-acting, indirect1.2 pilots the impulse valve 1.1 (14) → cylinder extends and stays out (memory) until 1.3 pilots it back (12).

Indirect control is used for large cylinders: the operator’s valve only handles a small signal.

• Shuttle valve (OR) — two signal valves 1.2 and 1.4 can each operate the cylinder. Without the shuttle, air from one valve would escape through the exhaust of the other.
  • Two-pressure valve (AND) — output only when both 1.2 and 1.4 are operated. Used for interlocks and two-hand safety starts.

Place a one-way flow control valve so that it throttles only the stroke you want to slow; two valves control both strokes.

MethodBehaviour (from the notes)
Supply-air throttling (meter-in)Steady initial motion but poor possibility of regulation; used mainly for small cylinders against the load
Exhaust-air throttling (meter-out)An initial jolt, then the forces are equalised; better possibility for regulating

Press start valve 1.2
Impulse valve 1.1 switches (14) → cylinder 1.0 extends
Piston rod reaches roller valve 1.3 at the front end
Timer fitted?
Yes → 1.3 feeds time-delay valve 1.5; after the preset time it pilots 1.1 back
1.1 switches (12) → cylinder retracts

recap: Air from one valve escaping through another valve’s exhaust is prevented by a ___ valve.

sections.b:
Example — bending and punching fixture: clamp (A), two bending cylinders (B, C), punch (D). Sequence in letters: A+ B+ C+ C− D+ D− B− A− (+ = extend, − = retract).

A simpler two-cylinder sequence, A+ B+ A− B−:

Graphically: a displacement-step diagram (movement vs step number) or a displacement-time diagram (movement vs time).

DesignationElementExample
1.0, 2.0, 3.0Working elementsCylinders
1.1, 2.1Actuating (final control) elements4/2, 5/2 valves
1.2, 1.4, 2.2 (even)Signal elements for the advance3/2 valves, shuttle, two-pressure, delay
1.3, 1.5, 2.3 (odd)Signal elements for the returnLimit valves
0.1, 0.2Supply elementsService unit, shut-off valve, cascade reversing valve
1.02, 1.03Auxiliary devicesThrottle, relief, check, quick exhaust

Letter method: cylinders A, B, C; signal valves at the forward end a1, b1; at the rear end a0, b0. In A+ B+ A− B−: a1 starts B+, b1 starts A−, a0 starts B−, b0 (with start) starts A+.

When one movement’s signal is still present while the opposite movement is wanted (e.g. A+ B+ B− A−: b1 is still pressed when B− should start), an impulse valve receives opposing signals and cannot switch. The cascade cures this by signal cut-out: the limit valves are fed from group supply lines switched by reversing valves, and only one line is live at a time — all others are vented.

  • Number of reversing valves = groups − 1.
  • Pressure drop grows with each valve in series, so use no more than 3 reversing valves (4 groups).

sections.h: Designing a cascade: A+ B+ B− A− C+ C−
sections.b:
Write the sequence: A+ B+ B− A− C+ C−
Split into groups — no cylinder may move twice in one group, and use the fewest groups: I = A+ B+ | II = B− A− C+ | III = C−
One supply line per group → 3 lines
Reversing valves = 3 − 1 = 2
Mark limit switches: within a group ABOVE the notation (a1 → B+, b0 → A−, a0 → C+); group change-overs BELOW (b1 → II, c1 → III, c0 + START → I)
The last group must be live at rest; draw change-over valves below the supply lines, in-group valves above

If a cylinder extends two or more times in a cycle, its limit signals must be interlocked with two-pressure valves. Add auxiliary conditions only after the basic sequence works.

Auto-start / auto-stop: extra valves (auto start, auto stop, manual start) with a memory valve let the cycle repeat automatically until stopped.

AdvantagesDisadvantages
Quick to design and checkMay not be the simplest solution for some circuits
Fault tracing is easy — you can see which group has failedPressure drop grows with the number of stages
Signals are inherently long enough to complete their taskCare needed if a limit valve is held down by an outside source

Notes’ examples: distributor A+ B+ | B− A− (2 groups, 1 reversing valve); bending device A+ B+ | B− C+ | C− A− (3 groups, 2 reversing valves).

worked.q: Group A+ B+ A− B− for a cascade.
worked.s: A+ B+ | A− B−. A+ and A− cannot share a group, so the split comes after B+. 2 groups → 1 reversing valve. a1 (in group I) starts B+; b1 changes to group II; a0 (in group II) starts B−; b0 + START changes back to group I.

worked.q: How many reversing valves for A+ B+ B− C+ C− A−?
worked.s: Groups: A+ B+ | B− C+ | C− A− = 3 groups → 2 reversing valves.

recap: The rear-end limit valve of cylinder B is called ___.
In a cascade only ___ supply line is live at a time.

topics.title: Pneumatic Components
topics.zh: 气动元件

sections.b:
An actuator converts supply energy into useful work. Linear: single- and double-acting cylinders. Rotary: air motors and rotary actuators.

ActuatorKey points
Single-acting cylinderPower stroke in one direction; a spring returns it. A small vent at the dead end lets atmospheric air in and out (prevents air lock and keeps seals from drying). Used for clamping, ejecting, lifting, feeding.
Double-acting cylinderAir power in both directions; a port in each end cover, no vent. Return stroke is faster but weaker than the forward stroke (single rod).
CushioningBuilt-in cushions slow the piston as it nears the end of stroke in either direction.
Air motorConverts air pressure into continuous rotation by expanding the air to atmospheric pressure — air screwdrivers, wrenches, grinders.

From your annotations: a single-acting cylinder’s working stroke is normally the extend stroke, because the air-driven stroke gives more force than the spring return.

Identified by: number of ports (2, 3, 4, 5), number of positions (2 or 3), type of element (poppet, spool/slide, disc) and method of operation (manual or automatic).

  • Poppet (seat) valves — balls, discs, plates or cones open and close the ports; few wearing parts, long life, robust and insensitive to dirt, but need a relatively high actuating force.
  • Slide valves — spool, flat slide or rotary (plate) slide link or close the ports.
ValveUse
2/2On/off only; cannot exhaust once closed. Usually ball-seat.
3/2 (NC or NO)Single-acting cylinders, signals, diverter/selector. NC/NO depends on the un-actuated position.
4/2Double-acting cylinders: supplies one side while exhausting the other.
4/3Centre (initial) position plus left and right.
5/2One supply, two exhausts, two outputs — double-acting cylinders.
5/3Can stop a cylinder part-way along its stroke.

sections.h: Logic, flow, time and pressure valves
sections.b:
ValveHow it behaves
Two-pressure valve (AND)Inlets 1 and 1 (P1, P2), outlet 2 (A). Output only when both inlets have signal; with unequal pressures, the lower pressure passes. Interlocks, safety controls, logic.
Shuttle valve (OR)Also called double check valve. Air from either inlet seals the other and flows to the outlet. Needed whenever a cylinder or valve is operated from two or more places.
Throttle valveAdjustable, lockable restriction in both directions; must never be closed fully.
One-way flow control valveThrottles one direction; a check valve gives free flow the other way. Mount it directly on the cylinder if possible.
Time-delay valve3/2 valve + one-way flow control + small air reservoir. Pilot air at 12 fills the reservoir through the throttle; when pressure is high enough the valve switches 1→2. Delay usually 0–30 s. Normally closed or normally open versions.
Pressure limiting (relief) valveOpens to atmosphere if pressure exceeds the setting; recloses by spring. Safety valve.
Sequence valvePasses a signal only after a set pressure is reached (pressure-dependent control).

recap: A single-acting cylinder needs a ___ at its dead end.
A 5/3 valve can stop a cylinder ___ its stroke.
The time-delay valve combines a 3/2 valve, a one-way flow control valve and a ___.

topics.title: Electro-Pneumatics & Solenoid Valves
topics.zh: 电气动与电磁阀

sections.b:
The power section is still pneumatic, but the signals are electrical: switches and sensors give input signals, relays process them, and solenoid-operated valves convert them to air flow. Extra parts: 24 V DC power supply, electrical switches, contacts, relays, solenoid valves.

  • Quick exhaust valve — when P is pressurised the disc covers exhaust R and air flows to A; when P is removed, air from A pushes the disc against P and dumps straight to atmosphere. Raises piston speed (especially single-acting return). Mount on or near the cylinder.
  • One-way flow control valve — speed control, as in pure pneumatics.

When a solenoid is energised, the magnetic field pulls the soft-iron armature in, which moves the valve directly or opens a pilot passage.

ValveBehaviour
Spring-return (single solenoid)Stays actuated only while current flows
Double solenoidKeeps its last position with no current (memory); has no clear initial position. If both coils are energised it does not move.
2/2Initially 1 blocked; energised: poppet lifts, 1→2
3/2 NCInitially 2→3 (exhaust); energised: 1→2, 3 closed
3/2 NOPressure and exhaust ports reversed compared with NC
Pilot-operatedThe armature only opens a small duct from port 1; that air moves the main piston — less coil power for big valves
5/2 single solenoid (pilot)Rest: 1→2, 4→5. Energised: 1→4, 2→3. Spring returns it.
5/2 double solenoidOne coil sends it to 1→4/2→3, the other back to 1→2/4→5; friction holds it when neither is energised
5/3 double solenoidSprings centre it with both coils off: 2→3 and 4→5 vented, 1 closed (exhaust centre)

recap: Electro-pneumatic control circuits normally use ___ V DC.
A double solenoid valve keeps its ___ position when de-energised.
The quick exhaust valve should be mounted ___ the cylinder.

topics.title: Electrical Signal Input Devices
topics.zh: 电气信号输入元件

sections.b:
• Switches — momentary (spring-return) or detent (latching). Available as NO (closes when pressed), NC (opens when pressed) and changeover (one circuit opens as another closes).
  • Contacts — same NO/NC/changeover forms, but operated electrically by a relay or contactor.
  • Relay — an electromagnetic switch: a small coil current switches larger currents through its contacts. Low maintenance, many independent circuits, short switching time, works from −40 °C to +80 °C, high off-state resistance and good isolation between control and main circuits. Used to interface different voltages, for latching, and to switch several paths at once.
  • Contactor — same principle as a relay but for higher loads (usually above 20 A).

From your annotations: the relay coil sits in the low-power 24 V control circuit; its contacts switch the high-power main circuit (110–440 V) to the load. A detent switch is a latch.

DeviceBehaviour
On-delay timer (energising delay)Timing starts when the input S is applied; after the preset time the contact switches (to terminal 18)
Off-delay timer (de-energising delay)Contact switches immediately when S is applied; timing starts when S is released, then the contact resets
Counter — subtractingPre-determined: counts down from a preset; output at zero
Counter — addingCounts up from zero; output when the preset is reached. Both reset manually, electrically or automatically.
Pressure switchAir pressure on a piston works against an adjustable spring; above the setting the contacts switch → converts pressure to an electrical signal

SensorDetectsHow
Limit switchA part at a positionMechanically actuated, usually by a cam; normally a changeover contact (wire as NO, NC or changeover)
Reed switchCylinder piston position (magnet in piston), rotary angleContacts in an inert-gas glass tube close in a magnetic field; small, fast; epoxy-encapsulated for industry
Inductive proximityMetals onlyOscillator makes a high-frequency field; a conductor damps it; trigger + amplifier switch the output
Capacitive proximityMetals and insulators with high dielectric constant (plastic, glass, wood, liquids)An object in the stray field raises the capacitance of an RC oscillator
Through-beamAnything that breaks the beamSeparate transmitter and receiver aimed at each other
Retro-reflectiveAnything that breaks the beamTransmitter and receiver in one housing; beam returns from a reflector
DiffuseReflective objectsTransmitter and receiver in one housing; light reflected by the object itself

Seven common functions: YES, NOT, OR, AND, NOR, NAND, memory. Each can be wired directly (switch drives the load) or indirectly (switch drives a relay K1 whose contact drives the load — the usual method).

FunctionWiringLoad is ON when…
YESNO switch in seriesS1 pressed
NOTNC switch (indirect: NO switch drives K1, load through K1’s NC contact)S1 not pressed
ORSwitches in parallelS1 or S2 (or both)
ANDSwitches in seriesS1 and S2
MemoryStart switch in parallel with K1’s own NO contactafter Start, until Stop

Dominant OFF: stop switch in series ahead of the start/hold parallel — pressing both = OFF. Dominant ON: start switch bypasses the stop — pressing both = ON.

The NOT function uses an NC relay contact in the indirect method so the relay is not energised all the time.

recap: A contactor is like a relay but for loads usually above ___ A.
In an off-delay timer, timing starts when the input is ___.

topics.title: Basic Electro-Pneumatic Circuits
topics.zh: 基本电气动回路

sections.b:
CircuitOperation
Single-acting, directS1 closes → coil Y1 energised → 3/2 valve 1→2 → cylinder extends. Release S1 → field collapses → valve resets → cylinder returns.
Single-acting, indirectS1 energises relay K1; a K1 NO contact energises Y1. Needed when S1 cannot switch Y1’s current, or when Y1 runs on another voltage (e.g. 230 V).
Double-acting5/2 single-solenoid (pilot) valve: S1 pressed → Y1 → extends; released → spring returns valve → retracts.
OR (parallel)S1 or S2 extends; returns when both are released.
AND (series)Only S1 and S2 together extend; releasing either returns it.

CircuitOperation
Double solenoid, two buttonsS1 → Y1 → extends and stays; S2 → Y2 → returns. The valve will not switch while the opposite coil is still energised (opposing signal).
Automatic returnS1 → Y1 extends; the rod hits limit switch S2 at the front → Y2 → returns. S1 must already be released.
OscillationLimit switches S1 (rear) and S2 (front); S1 only works while S3 is held closed. The piston shuttles back and forth until S3 is released, then stops at the rear.
Latching (single solenoid)S1 energises K1; a K1 contact in parallel holds it on; another K1 contact powers Y1. S2 (NC) breaks the hold → valve spring returns the cylinder.
Auto-return by limit switchAs latching, but the NC limit switch at the front end breaks the latch, so the cylinder returns by itself (S1 must be released).

recap: The indirect method is needed if S1 cannot switch the coil current or a different ___ is used.
In the oscillating circuit the piston stops at the ___ when S3 is released.
Pressing S2 in a latching circuit ___ relay K1.

topics.title: Electro-Pneumatic Sequencing
topics.zh: 电气动顺序控制

sections.h: Pneumatic memory (double solenoid valves): A+ B+ A− B−
sections.b:
Limit switches: S1 = A rear, S2 = A front, S3 = B rear, S4 = B front. Each step has its own relay; the valves remember their position.

Start S5 + S3 (B is back) → K1 → Y1 → A+
S2 (A out) → K2 → Y3 → B+
S4 (B out) → K3 → Y2 → A−
S1 (A back) → K4 → Y4 → B− → ready for a new start

Reed switches can replace the limit switches.

Now the relays must hold the state, so each relay latches.

S5 + S3 → K1 latches → Y1 → A+
S2 → K2 latches → Y2 → B+
S4 (NC, ahead of K1) opens → K1 drops → Y1 off → A−
S1 (NC, ahead of K2) opens → K2 drops → Y2 off → B−; S3 made again → new cycle possible
In step 5 the notes say S1 is "actuated by cylinder B". S1 is the rear limit switch of cylinder A, so it is actuated by A when A retracts.

Signal overlap (e.g. A+ B+ B− A−, where S4 is still made when B− is wanted) is solved as in pneumatics: group the sequence, give each group a supply line switched by relays, with only one line live. Relays = groups − 1.

A+ B+ | B− A− → 2 groups, 1 relay K1
START → K1 latches → line I live → Y1 → A+
S2 on line I → Y3 → B+
S4 (NC, in K1’s rung) breaks the latch → line II live through K1’s NC contact → Y4 → B−
S3 on line II → Y2 → A−; cycle complete

Each step’s relay latches, and needs (a) the limit switch of the previous movement and (b) a confirmation contact from the previous relay, so relays can only switch in order. Solenoids are switched from the relays in the control section. The last step resets the first relay, which resets all others.

ST → K1 latches → Y1 → A+
S2 + K1 → K2 → Y3 → B+
S4 + K2 → K3 → Y3 cut off → B−
S3 + K3 → K4 → Y2 (Y1 cut off) → A−
S1 + K4 → K5 (no latch) → resets K1 and so all relays
The notes give section 14.05 the heading "pneumatic memory" — it is the electrical cascade method. In 14.06 step 6 the confirmation for K5 should come from K4, not K3.

Practice machines: embossing (A+ B+ B− A− C+ C−), assembly (A+ B+ C+ then A− with C− together, then B−), cleaning plant (4 cylinders), milling fixture.

recap: With single solenoid valves, the ___ must hold (latch) each step.
In the stepper method each relay needs a ___ contact from the previous relay.

topics.title: Maintenance & Troubleshooting (Ch 9 & 15)
topics.zh: 维护与故障排除（第 9、15 章）

sections.b:
Systematic maintenance prolongs life and improves reliability. A plan lists tasks and intervals; complex systems also need the function and circuit diagrams. Intervals depend on usage, wear and the environment.

IntervalTasks (Ch 9 and Ch 15 combined)
DailyDrain condensate from filters (if no automatic drain); check lubricator oil level and setting
WeeklyCheck signal devices for dirt and swarf; check pressure-regulator gauges; check hoses for cuts, kinks and porosity; check fittings are tight; check the lubricator works
Monthly / quarterlyCheck all unions and lines for leaks; check valve exhausts for leaks at rest; clean filter elements and blow them out against the normal flow; check automatic drains; replace lines on moving parts
Six-monthlyExamine piston-rod guides and bearings for wear; replace bushes, scraper and seal rings; inspect silencers, replace if fouled

Component checks: service unit (drain, clean bowl, check drain leaks, oil, lock the regulator, gauge), actuators (leaks, alignment, fastenings, sensor positions, flow-control setting, rods for damage; keep cylinders retracted when idle), sensors, tubing, valves (seals, silencers).

The notes conflict in two places. Lubricator rate: Ch 4 and 15 say about 1 drop/min ("never over-oil"), the Ch 9 weekly list says 5 drops/min. Filter cleaning: Ch 9 says wash in kerosene, Ch 15 says soapy water, no solvents. Check with your lecturer which one applies to your equipment.

Troubleshooting uses: how the system works, theory of its components, the equipment’s history (recurring faults), the symptoms — and common sense.

Gather symptoms — look, listen, feel, smell; ask the operator what happened and when
Is the machine still in the position where the fault occurred? Has the operator already changed or repaired anything?
Has the fault happened before?
Localise the fault — operate by hand if there is manual control (think first!)
Decide: is this a symptom or the real problem? Does it occur only under certain conditions?

Causes: wear (accelerated by environment), contaminated air blocking parts, blocked/split/bent lines, deposits causing pressure drop and wrong switching, leaks or fluctuating supply, badly serviced filters, poor cylinder fitting or side loads, wrongly mounted limit valves, over-long signal lines. Under-sized air supply (systems extended without enlarging supply) gives sporadic faults: wrong sequence and momentary loss of force when other actuators run.

SymptomLikely cause → remedy
Water drops in lines, water in lubricator, dirty (black/yellow) silencers, uneven or slow speedsPoor air preparation → service drains, filters, dryer
Filter does not separate dirt/waterFitted against the flow, or condensate above the mark → refit, drain, fit automatic drain
Air escapes at the regulatorRegulator fitted against the flow → refit
Lubricator not working / too much oil / oil used quicklyMounted against the arrow, set wrongly, overfilled, leaking O-ring → remount, reset, drain, replace O-ring
Air leaks at the rod bearing or rodPacking or groove ring worn/loose/fitted wrongly → replace
Single-acting cylinder will not returnBroken spring or blocked vent filter
Cushioning does not workCushion lip seal leaks or fitted backwards
Valve sluggish / does not switchDirt in groove rings; control pressure too low → clean, replace rings, reset regulator
Spool does not reverseDistorted housing or broken switching plunger; overlapping signals
Solenoid hummingDirt between coil and armature tube, worn armature → clean
Air escapes at the exhaustPorts 1 and 4 swapped → reconnect

Cylinder inspection: heavy lengthwise scoring or dry black lubricant on the rod warns that seals will soon fail; audible hissing or continuous blow-off at valves at rest means damaged seals; a sudden rise in valve response time signals an imminent fault.

Solenoid valve faults: open wires (infinite resistance), direct short (too much current back to the supply, fuse blows), cross short (wires bypass the load), high-resistance connections, stuck armature, low/over voltage, corrosion, blocked hoses, no source pressure, sticking spool, blocked exhausts, wrong gaskets.

Finding a direct short: pull the ground cable of the solenoid and retry. If the supply still shorts, the short is at the relay coil; if not, it is at the solenoid. Relay coil not working: measure voltage across leads and switch (open/closed), then coil resistance (infinite = open coil, replace); check a limit switch reads 24 V open, 0 V closed.

  • Use approved tools; no rings or bracelets near live circuits; never assume a circuit is off — test it.
  • Never override interlocks; discharge capacitors; never remove earths.
  • Check the correct voltage; keep metal tools off terminals; never test limit switches with your fingers.
  • Switch off electricity before rewiring, and vent the system before disconnecting any air line.

recap: Filter elements are blown out ___ the normal flow direction.
Sporadic sequence faults after a plant is extended suggest an ___ air supply.
A limit switch should read ___ V across it when open.

topics.title: What Is a Robot? & Basic Components
topics.zh: 什么是机器人？与基本元件

sections.b:
A robot is an electro-mechanical machine (a mechanical device that is electrically operated) guided by a computer program or electronic circuitry. It has four essential characteristics:

CharacteristicExamples
IntelligenceMicrocontroller, algorithm
SensingIR sensor, ultrasonic sensor, laser
MovementDC motor, gripper, arm
EnergyBattery, solar

TypeDescription / examples
Mobile robotMoves around its environment doing tasks autonomously — Festo Robotino, Omron autonomous intelligent vehicles, Robotnik surveillance robot
UAVUnmanned aerial vehicle: no human on board; remote-controlled or autonomous — MQ-1 Predator, RSAF Heron 1, PowerEye drone
Legged robotMobile robot with mechanical limbs for many terrains — Honda ASIMO, Boston Dynamics Atlas, HEXY
Track robotTracks for rugged, uneven ground with good stability
OthersUnderwater, industrial, commercial, military, medical, security robots

• LED — simple light source in many colours; has polarity (+ anode, − cathode); always used with a current-limiting resistor.
  • Resistor — unit ohm (Ω); no polarity; with an LED, 220 Ω or 330 Ω prevents over-current damage.
  • Breadboard — for mounting components and testing circuits without soldering; made of electrically common rows and columns.

Practice 1: wire an LED and resistor on the breadboard to an Arduino pin (see the LED topic for the circuit).

recap: The four essential characteristics: intelligence, sensing, movement and ___.
A UAV has no ___ on board.
An LED has polarity; a resistor has ___.

topics.title: Microcontrollers & Arduino Boards
topics.zh: 微控制器与 Arduino 板

sections.b:
An integrated computing device with three major parts on one chip: microprocessor (CPU), memory and I/O ports. Also called an embedded controller: it is built into another device, dedicated to one task, runs one program stored in non-volatile memory, and uses little power (the slides quote about 50 mW for a battery unit). Makers: Atmel (used by Arduino), Intel, Microchip, Motorola, Texas Instruments.

BlockJob
CPUThe brain — fetches and decodes instructions from program memory
MemoryStores program and data: RAM, ROM, EPROM, EEPROM, flash
Parallel I/O portsDrive and interface devices — LCDs, LEDs, printers
Timers/countersTiming and counting: clock functions, modulation, pulse generation, frequency measurement
Interrupt controlLets an internal or external (pin) event interrupt the running program
ADCConverts an analog signal (e.g. sensor output) into a digital number
DACConverts a digital number into an analog signal to drive analog devices

Microcontrollers measure, store, control, calculate and display — used in biomedical instruments, communications, PC peripherals, robotics and cars.

Arduino is a popular open-source electronics platform: easy hardware and software that read inputs (light on a sensor, a finger on a button) and turn them into outputs (start a motor, light an LED). It is COTS — commercial off-the-shelf. Why Arduino: inexpensive, cross-platform (Windows, macOS, Linux), simple for beginners yet flexible, open-source with free libraries.

UNOLEONARDOMEGA 2560DUE
MicrocontrollerATmega328PATmega32u4ATmega2560ARM Cortex-M3
Operating voltage5 V5 V5 V3.3 V
Input voltage (recommended / limit)7–12 / 6–20 V7–12 / 6–20 V7–12 / 6–20 V7–12 / 6–16 V
Digital I/O (PWM)14 (6)20 (7)54 (15)54 (12)
Analog inputs6121612
Analog outputs0002 (DAC)
Flash (bootloader)32 KB (0.5 KB)32 KB (4 KB)256 KB (8 KB)512 KB
SRAM2 KB2.5 KB8 KB96 KB
EEPROM1 KB1 KB4 KB—
Clock16 MHz16 MHz16 MHz84 MHz
  • UNO — easiest, most robust, the reference board; "uno" is Italian for one (Arduino IDE 1.0).
  • Leonardo — ATmega32u4 has built-in USB, so it can act as a mouse/keyboard; less popular due to awkward re-programming/reset.
  • Mega — "four UNOs in one". The class mobile robot uses Mega pin numbers (e.g. 48, 49).
  • Due — first ARM board, most powerful (about 5× UNO). Pins tolerate only 3.3 V — higher voltages damage it.
Slide corrections: the Due slide labels its chip "ATmega2560" — the Due uses the AT91SAM3X8E. The comparison table lists the Due’s "DC current per I/O pin" as 800 mA; 800 mA is what its 3.3 V / 5 V supply pins can deliver — each I/O pin handles only a few mA (about 130 mA for all pins together).

• Power: USB, or external 7–12 V via the 2.1 mm centre-positive jack or the Vin/GND pins. Below 7 V the board may be unstable; above 12 V the regulator may overheat. Pins: Vin (external input), 5V (regulated), 3V3 (3.3 V, 50 mA), GND.
  • Memory: flash holds the sketch; SRAM holds variables while running (volatile — lost at power-off); EEPROM for long-term data. Flash and EEPROM are non-volatile.
  • Digital pins work at 5 V, set by pinMode(), digitalWrite(), digitalRead(); internal pull-up about 20 kΩ; each pin can provide or receive a maximum of 40 mA. Special: serial 0 (RX), 1 (TX); external interrupts 2, 3; PWM 3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 11 (8-bit, analogWrite()); SPI 10–13; built-in LED 13.
  • Analog inputs A0–A5: 10-bit (1024 values), 0–5 V by default. I²C on A4 (SDA), A5 (SCL); AREF sets the reference; RESET low resets the chip.
The slides say the 3V3 pin is "generated by the on-board FTDI chip". That was true of older boards; on the UNO it comes from a separate 3.3 V regulator.

recap: A microcontroller has CPU, memory and ___ on one chip.
The UNO’s PWM pins are 3, 5, 6, 9, 10 and ___.
SRAM is ___ — lost when power is removed.

topics.title: Arduino IDE
topics.zh: Arduino 集成开发环境

sections.b:
The Arduino Software (IDE) — a text editor, message area, text console, toolbar and menus. It connects to the board to upload programs and communicate with them. Programs are called sketches and saved as .ino files.

PartWhat it does
VerifyChecks (compiles) the code for errors
UploadCompiles and sends the code to the configured board
New / Open / SaveCreate, open (from the sketchbook) and save sketches
Serial MonitorShows serial data from the board; type text and Send. Choose the baud rate that matches Serial.begin().
Message areaFeedback while saving/exporting; shows errors
ConsoleFull error messages and other text output
Bottom-right cornerConfigured board and serial port

• File — New, Open, Open Recent, Sketchbook, Examples, Save As, Preferences.
  • Edit — Copy for Forum, Copy as HTML, Comment/Uncomment (//), indent, Find.
  • Sketch — Verify/Compile (reports memory use), Upload, Upload Using Programmer (overwrites the bootloader), Export compiled Binary (.hex), Include Library (adds #include lines), Add File.
  • Tools — Auto Format, Archive Sketch (.zip), Serial Monitor, Board and Port.
  • Help — offline Getting Started and Reference; Find in Reference opens the page for the word under the cursor.

Tools → Board: choose the board
Tools → Port: COM1/COM2 are usually serial ports; a USB board is often COM4, COM5, COM7 or higher (check Device Manager)
Verify, fix errors in the message area
Upload — RX/TX LEDs blink during upload
"Done uploading" — or an error message

Libraries add functions (e.g. Servo.h). Including one inserts #include lines and the library is uploaded with the sketch, so it uses more memory. Delete the #include line if no longer needed.

recap: The Serial Monitor baud rate must match ___.

topics.title: Arduino C Programming
topics.zh: Arduino C 语言编程

sections.b:
Every sketch has three parts: variable declarations, setup() and loop().

  • setup() runs once after power-up or reset — set pin modes, start libraries, initialise variables.
  • loop() then runs over and over, letting the program respond.
  • // comments; code goes inside { }; every statement ends with a semicolon ;.
  • In the IDE, functions are orange, variables/constants blue, structure keywords green.
int ledPin = 13;            // name pin 13
void setup() {
  pinMode(ledPin, OUTPUT);  // runs once
}
void loop() {
  digitalWrite(ledPin, HIGH);  // LED on
  delay(1000);                 // wait 1000 ms = 1 s
  digitalWrite(ledPin, LOW);   // LED off
  delay(1000);
}
The slide says "every function must end with a semi-colon". It is every statement that ends with ; — a function body ends with }.

FunctionMeaning
pinMode(pin, mode)mode = INPUT, OUTPUT or INPUT_PULLUP
digitalWrite(pin, value)HIGH (5 V) or LOW (0 V)
digitalRead(pin)returns HIGH or LOW
analogWrite(pin, 0–255)PWM output on a ~ pin
analogRead(pin)0–1023 from an analog input
delay(ms) / delayMicroseconds(µs)pause
Serial.begin(9600), Serial.print(), Serial.println()serial communication / print to the Serial Monitor
tone(pin, freq, duration)square-wave tone on a buzzer
#define Buzzer 3names a constant before compiling

sections.h: Loops, arrays, if and the servo
sections.b:
int ledPins[] = {2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9};   // array: ledPins[0] is 2
void setup() {
  for (int i = 0; i <= 7; i++) pinMode(ledPins[i], OUTPUT);
}
void loop() {
  for (int i = 0; i <= 7; i++) { digitalWrite(ledPins[i], HIGH); delay(100); }
  for (int i = 7; i >= 0; i--) { digitalWrite(ledPins[i], LOW);  delay(100); }
}

for repeats with a counter (i++ adds one, i-- subtracts one). An array is a list accessed by index, starting at 0. if runs code only when a condition is true:

if (digitalRead(BUTTON1) == HIGH) { digitalWrite(led1, HIGH); }

Servo (0–180°) — include the library, create an object, attach it to a pin, then write() the angle. Never turn a servo horn by hand — it damages the gears.

#include <Servo.h>
Servo servo1;
void setup() { servo1.attach(9); }
void loop()  { servo1.write(90); delay(1000); servo1.write(180); delay(1000); servo1.write(0); delay(1000); }

worked.q: Lab 1 exercises: what do you see with ON/OFF times of 100/900 ms, 50/50 ms and 10/10 ms?
worked.s: 100/900 ms: a short flash once per second. 50/50 ms: a fast flicker (10 flashes per second). 10/10 ms: 50 flashes per second — too fast for the eye, so the LED looks steadily on but dimmer (persistence of vision; this is the idea behind PWM).

worked.q: Mock test: LEDs on pins 52 and 53 should turn ON with button A2 and OFF with A1; the servo is on pin 9. Find the faults in the given sketch (led1 = 12, led2 = 13, servo1.attach(8), pinMode(led1, INPUT), pinMode(led2, INPUT), BUTTON1 turns the LEDs on).
worked.s: Fix: led1 = 52; led2 = 53; · servo1.attach(9); · pinMode(led1, OUTPUT); pinMode(led2, OUTPUT); · swap the buttons so BUTTON2 (A2) turns the LEDs ON and BUTTON1 (A1) turns them OFF.

worked.q: Lab 3 Exp 4 has two blanks: int BUTTON1 = ___ and a missing line in setup(). Fill them.
worked.s: int BUTTON1 = A1; (button on A1 per Fig. 2) and servo1.attach(9); in setup().

worked.q: Lab 9: the buzzer sketch contains pinMode(tonePin, OUTPUT); but declares int buzzer = 3;. What happens?
worked.s: It will not compile — tonePin is undeclared. Change it to pinMode(buzzer, OUTPUT);.

Servo angles are written with servo1.___(angle).

topics.title: Lighting an LED: Ohm’s Law & Resistors
topics.zh: 点亮 LED：欧姆定律与电阻

sections.b:
Electricity is energy from charged particles — static (accumulated charge) or as a current. It powers equipment (electric power) and electronic circuits with active components (transistors, diodes, ICs).

A basic circuit: battery (here the Arduino’s 5 V output), switch (open breaks the current, closed completes the circuit), resistor (limits current so the LED is not damaged — but too large and the LED is dim) and LED.

An LED converts electrical energy directly into light of one colour; it lasts as long as a transistor. It must be connected the right way round; the slides take a minimum forward voltage of 1.5 V and a current of 10–20 mA. Cathode (−): the shorter leg, the flag (bigger) part inside the lens, and the flat spot on the case.

V = I × RR = (Vsupply − Vforward) / I
UnitsV — volt (V)I — ampere (A)R — ohm (Ω)

Slide example: 5 V supply, 1.5 V LED, 15 mA → R = (5 − 1.5) / 0.015 = 233 Ω → use the nearest standard value, 220 Ω or 330 Ω.

ResistorBands
220 Ωred red brown
330 Ωorange orange brown
1 kΩbrown black red
10 kΩbrown black orange
430 kΩ (slide question)yellow orange yellow
820 Ω (slide question)grey red brown

Band 1 and 2 are digits, band 3 is the multiplier (number of zeros).

• Active HIGH — LED from the pin to GND: writing logic 1 turns it on (the pin sources current).
  • Active LOW — LED from +5 V to the pin: writing logic 0 turns it on (the pin sinks current).

The slides: active LOW is the preferred method to turn on an LED.

terms: 高电平有效 / 低电平有效

worked.q: Using the slide values (5 V supply, 1.5 V LED), find R for 20 mA.
With the same LED and a 330 Ω resistor, what current flows?
worked.s: I = (5 − 1.5) / 330 = 10.6 mA — inside the 10–20 mA range.

topics.title: Flowchart Programming
topics.zh: 流程图编程

sections.b:
A flowchart is a graphical representation of a process: each step is a symbol with a short description, joined by arrows. Flowchart programming lets you see the algorithm before writing code.

Uses: problem solving (break a problem into easy parts), documentation (good paperless records), communication (easy to visualise), effective analysis.

SymbolShapeUse
TerminatorOvalSTART and STOP / END of the program
ProcessRectangleA step, e.g. "Move forward 50 cm"
DecisionDiamondA question with Yes/No (True/False) branches
Input/Output (data)ParallelogramInputs and outputs, e.g. print "Game Over"
ConnectorSmall circle (e.g. A1)Links to another part of the flowchart
ArrowLine with arrowheadDirection of flow

START
Move forward 50 cm
Turn left 90°
Move forward 50 cm
Red object detected?
No → END
Yes → pick object
Light up red LED
END

START
Read door sensor (pin 20)
Person detected?
No → print "DOOR CLOSING", wait 1 s, servo (pin 9) to 0° → back to read sensor
Yes → servo (pin 9) to 180° (door opens)
Wait 1 s
Print "DOOR OPEN"
Back to read sensor
#include <Servo.h>
Servo servo1;
int sensor = 20;
int sensorState = 1;
void setup() {
  servo1.attach(9);
  pinMode(sensor, INPUT);
  Serial.begin(9600);
}
void loop() {
  sensorState = digitalRead(sensor);
  if (sensorState == HIGH) { servo1.write(180); delay(1000); Serial.println("DOOR OPEN"); }
  if (sensorState == LOW)  { Serial.println("DOOR CLOSING"); delay(1000); servo1.write(0); }
}
The slide’s version of this program will not compile as written: it declares servo1 but uses servo.attach and Servo.write, and starts Void setup() with a capital V. The code above is corrected.

worked.q: Draw then code: LED D1 on, print "D1 ON", wait 5 s, LED off, print "D1 OFF", wait 5 s.
worked.s:
Flowchart: START → D1 ON (process) → print "D1 ON" (I/O) → wait 5 s → D1 OFF → print "D1 OFF" (I/O) → wait 5 s → END.
digitalWrite(D1, HIGH); Serial.println("D1 ON"); delay(5000); digitalWrite(D1, LOW); Serial.println("D1 OFF"); delay(5000); (with pinMode(D1, OUTPUT); Serial.begin(9600); in setup).

recap: A small circle labelled A1 is a ___.

topics.title: Mobile Robot: Motors, PWM & Sensors
topics.zh: 移动机器人：电机、PWM 与传感器

sections.b:
PWM adjusts the average voltage to a device by switching the power on and off very fast. The average depends on the duty cycle — ON time as a fraction of the period. analogWrite(pin, 0–255) sets it.

Duty cycle = value / 255Vavg = duty × 5 V
Unitsvalue, duty — no unitVavg — volt (V)

Each motor has a direction pin and a PWM (speed) pin:

Direction pinPWM pin
Left motor ADIRA = 13PWMA = 11
Right motor BDIRB = 12PWMB = 3
int FORWARD = 0, REVERSE = 1;
int DIRA = 13, PWMA = 11, DIRB = 12, PWMB = 3;
void fwd()  { digitalWrite(DIRA, FORWARD); analogWrite(PWMA, 255);
              digitalWrite(DIRB, FORWARD); analogWrite(PWMB, 255); }
void left() { digitalWrite(DIRA, FORWARD); analogWrite(PWMA, 0);    // left wheel stopped
              digitalWrite(DIRB, FORWARD); analogWrite(PWMB, 255); } // right wheel drives
void Stop() { analogWrite(PWMA, 0); analogWrite(PWMB, 0); }
FunctionLeft motorRight motor
fwd()ON, forwardON, forward
rev()ON, reverseON, reverse
Stop()OFFOFF
left()OFFON, forward
right()ON, forwardOFF

Splitting moves into functions keeps loop() short and readable. Programming help sheet order: 1 Declaration → 2 Setup → 3 Functions → 4 IF conditions.

Slide exercise — move in a square, checking for obstacles:

Start
FWD — blink green LED — delay 1 s
Stop
Obstacle closer than 15 cm?
Yes → Stop, delay 1 s → Reverse, delay 0.5 s
No → Right 90° (delay 0.5 s)
Blink blue LED
End of loop() — repeats, tracing a square

Four pins: GND, VCC, Trig, Echo. A 10 µs pulse on Trig makes the module send an 8-cycle burst at 40 kHz; the Echo pin stays HIGH until the reflection returns. On the robot: echo = 49, trig = 48.

distance (cm) = duration (µs) / 29 / 2
Unitsdistance — centimetre (cm)duration — microsecond (µs)
digitalWrite(trig, LOW);  delayMicroseconds(2);
digitalWrite(trig, HIGH); delayMicroseconds(10);   // 10 µs trigger
digitalWrite(trig, LOW);
const unsigned long duration = pulseIn(echo, HIGH); // echo time in µs
int distance = duration / 29 / 2;                   // cm
if (distance >= 15) { blinkGrn(); }                 // no obstacle
if (distance < 15)  { Stop(); delay(500); rev(); delay(500); right(); delay(500); }

Lab 5: the sensor emits ultrasound at 40 000 Hz, which travels through the air and bounces back to the module if there is an object in its path. The sketch converts the echo time to centimetres with duration / 29 / 2.

sections.h: IR proximity sensor, buzzer and RGB LED
sections.b:
• SHARP 2Y0A21 — shines an infrared beam and measures the reflected intensity with a phototransistor. Its analog output varies from 3.1 V at 10 cm to 0.4 V at 80 cm (read with analogRead(); values go down as the object moves away). Two on the left side (A5 front, A4 rear) let the robot track a wall.
  • Buzzer on pin 3 — #define ON LOW, #define OFF HIGH (active-low); tone(Buzzer, 440) plays 440 Hz.
  • RGB LED on pins 30 (blue), 31 (green), 32 (red) — blinkRed(), blinkGrn(), blinkBlue() each light one colour for 500 ms.

worked.q: pulseIn returns 1160 µs. How far is the obstacle?
Which analogWrite value gives about 50 % speed, and what average voltage?
Write loop(): blink green while moving forward, blink blue after turning right (0.5 s for 90°).
worked.s: fwd(); blinkGrn(); delay(1000); Stop(); right(); delay(500); blinkBlue();

recap: The left motor uses DIRA = 13 and PWMA = ___.
The HC-SR04 sends a burst at ___ kHz.

topics.title: Industrial Robots: Uses & Components (Ch 1)
topics.zh: 工业机器人：应用与组成（第 1 章）

sections.b:
"A robot is a re-programmable multifunctional manipulator designed to move material, parts, tools or specialized devices through variable programmed motions for the performance of a variety of tasks."

ApplicationWhat it involves
Pick and placeFast, accurate, smooth, dependable handling — e.g. picking a part and placing it on the line
Material handlingMoving raw materials and parts between machines or areas. It adds no value to the product, so its cost must be kept down.
FabricationWelding, drilling, grinding, polishing, deburring, sanding
AssemblyCalculators, watches, PCBs, electric motors, alternators — anything that can be broken into simple steps

ReasonsOutcomesDisadvantages
Increased productivityLower production costHigh initial cost
High labour cost; labour shortagesHigher productivity and qualityRunning costs
Hazardous, hostile environmentsSafer workplace; no boring, unpleasant workIf the robot breaks down, the whole line is seriously affected
Better product qualityLower staff turnover
Shorter manufacturing lead timeFlexible, rapid production changes; better management control

Basic components: manipulator, end effector, controller (with power supply) and teach pendant.

  • Manipulator — mechanical unit moving like a human arm so that the tooling can do the work: base (anchor point — floor, ceiling, overhead support or a track), shoulder, arm (jointed arm: base, shoulder and elbow rotation — the largest working envelope per floor area), wrist (extension, rotation, twist — reaches places a human arm cannot, e.g. painting a car interior or welding inside a pipe).
  • Teach pendant — turns the system on, has the emergency stop, and is used to program the controller (the robot’s "brain").
  • Control box — motherboard (a micro PC with Ethernet and USB) and flexible I/O for pneumatic relays, PLCs and emergency-stop buttons.

The lab robot is a UR3 articulated (collaborative) robot. The system has three parts: manipulator — enables the robot arm to move to the required position; controller — stores program and position data; teach pendant — used for writing programs, teaching and operating the robot.

AxisType of motionRange of movement
Axis 1 / J1Baserecord in the lab
Axis 2 / J2Shoulderrecord in the lab
Axis 3 / J3Elbowrecord in the lab
Axis 4 / J4Wrist 1record in the lab
Axis 5 / J5Wrist 2record in the lab
Axis 6 / J6Wrist 3record in the lab

The jobsheet leaves the ranges, and what axes 1–3 and 4–6 are for, as blanks you fill in at the robot — so they are not printed here.

  • Working envelope — the extreme positions of the arm. The jobsheet: the UR3 has a cylindrical working envelope and its workspace extends 500 mm from the base joint. Consider the cylindrical volume directly above and directly below the base when choosing where to mount the robot.
  • Controller — contains the electronics that control the manipulator axes, external sensors and peripherals, and the system operating software with all basic functions for operation and programming. It stores and sequences the manipulator’s position data and controls its motions according to the instructions given.
  • Teach pendant — used to operate the robot. Emergency stop buttons are on the teach pendant; there are often other ways of activating an emergency stop, depending on the installation. When it is activated, the power supply to the motors is shut off and program execution stops.
  • Turning on: (a) press the "On" button — power goes only to the controller and teach pendant; (b) tap "On" — power is supplied to the robot; (c) tap "START" — a clicking sound is heard. Note the status shown at each step (blanks on the jobsheet).
  • Turning off: use the "OFF" button, then "Shutdown Robot", which powers off the robot arm and shuts down the control box.
  • Robot cell (1B): manipulator; HMI (emergency stop; green, red and orange buttons); vision; RFID — uses electromagnetic fields to identify and track tags attached to objects. Passive tags collect energy from a nearby reader’s radio waves; active tags have a local power source (such as a battery) and may operate hundreds of metres from the reader. Unlike a barcode, the tag need not be in the reader’s line of sight; conveyor.

recap: The four basic components: manipulator, end effector, controller and ___.
Material handling adds no ___ to the product.

topics.title: Installing a Robot & Robot Configurations (Ch 2)
topics.zh: 机器人安装与机器人构型（第 2 章）

sections.b:
• Risk assessment — the robot is partly completed machinery; the safety of the installation depends on how it is integrated (tool, obstacles, other machines). All safety information must be read, understood and implemented by the integrator.
  • Emergency stop — stops all robot motion immediately. It must not be used as a risk-reduction measure — it is a secondary protective device.
  • Take note of all warning labels.
  • Workspace — avoid moving the tool close to the cylindrical volume directly above and below the base: the joints must move fast even though the tool moves slowly, making the robot inefficient and the risk assessment difficult.
  • Mounting — bolt the arm to its base, tightened to the required torque.

Five groups: controller I/O, tool I/O, Ethernet, mains connection, robot connection. "I/O" means both digital and analog signals.

Controller I/O colourMeaning
Yellow, red textDedicated safety signals
Yellow, black textConfigurable for safety (or general purpose, set in the GUI)
Grey, black textGeneral-purpose digital I/O
Green, black textGeneral-purpose analog I/O
  • Digital I/O are 24 V; supply them from the internal 24 V supply (default: PWR and GND terminals) or an external source via the 24V/0V terminals of the "Power" block.
  • Tool I/O — an 8-pin connector at the tool flange gives power, digital and analog I/O for grippers and sensors; wire colours identify functions.
  • Ethernet (bottom of the control box) — MODBUS I/O expansion, remote access and control.
  • Mains — IEC C20 inlet with a C19 cord. The supply must have earth, a main fuse and a residual current device.

Safety-limiting functions: joint position, joint speed, TCP speed, TCP force, momentum, power. Path control slows the arm or stops the program as a limit is approached.

ConfigurationAxes · envelopeAdvantagesDisadvantagesApplications
Cartesian (rectangular)3 linear (x-y-z) · rectangular box, like an overhead craneEasy to visualise and compute; most rigid for its size (supported at both ends)Needs a large volume and floor area; exposed guides need covers in dirty/corrosive placesAssembly, palletising, machine-tool loading, pick and place
Cylindrical2 linear + 1 rotary · cylinderEasy to visualise; linear axes suit powerful hydraulics; good access into cavitiesCannot reach near the pillar or floor; hard to sealMachine loading/unloading, pick and place, die casting
Spherical (polar)1 linear + 2 rotary · part of a sphereLarge volume from one support; rotary drives easy to sealCoordinates hard to visualise and control; restricted coverageDie casting, injection moulding, machine-tool loading
SCARAx, y, z + rotation · like a cylindrical envelopeMore motion in an arc-shaped space; faster than Cartesian and cylindricalSmall work areaBiomedical, fast assembly and pick and place
Jointed arm (revolute)3 rotary · irregularAll rotary: maximum flexibility; joints can be fully sealed (dust, corrosion, underwater)Hardest to visualise and control; costly with hydraulics (suits electric)Welding, assembly, machine loading, painting, adhesives
Parallel link (delta)Jointed parallelograms to one tool · domeDelicate, precise; highest speedExpensive; more complex to useFood, pharmaceutical, electronics — fast pick and place, conveyor to box

recap: The emergency stop is a ___ protective device, not a risk-reduction measure.
A cylindrical robot has two linear and ___ rotary motion.
The mains supply must have earth, a main fuse and a ___.

topics.title: Robot Terminology (Ch 3)
topics.zh: 机器人术语（第 3 章）

sections.h: Degrees of freedom and the wrist
sections.b:
• Degrees of freedom (DoF) — the number of independent ways the end effector can move in space. Each axis = one DoF. Industrial robots usually have 4–6.
  • The wrist sets the orientation with three motions: pitch (up-and-down), yaw (side-to-side) and roll (rotation). These are the orientation axes.
  • World coordinate system — a fixed frame of reference in the manipulator: x in-and-out, y side-to-side, z up-and-down.
The next slide ("Moving from point to point") swaps these: it calls Y the in-and-out reach and X the side-to-side rotation about the base. Use the world-coordinate definition above, and always check the arrows on the robot you are using.

• Payload — the maximum weight the arm can lift and carry continuously and satisfactorily at a given speed. It includes the end-of-arm tooling (EOAT).
Max payload = weight of end effector + weight of work part
Unitspayload, weights — kilogram (kg)

Example (notes): tooling 4 kg, robot limit 10 kg → the part may weigh at most 6 kg.

  • Reach — vertical: height when extended upwards from the base; horizontal: distance from base to wrist with the arm fully extended. More axes → less linear reach (like your arm: you cannot touch your own elbow but you can reach around obstacles).
  • Work envelope — the perimeter of the work volume.

• Repeatability — the spread of positions over repeated attempts to reach a fixed location: the ability to return consistently to a taught point.
  • Accuracy — the ability to move to a commanded position (and/or velocity) within the working area.
  • Resolution — the smallest incremental change in position the wrist can make.
  • Tool Centre Point (TCP) — the working point of the tool, defined relative to the tool flange. Moving TCP (most applications): moves with the arm — tip of an arc-welding gun, centre of a spot-welding gun. Stationary TCP: defined on fixed equipment (e.g. a stationary spot-welding gun) while the robot carries the part.

worked.q: A gripper weighs 1.2 kg and the robot’s rated payload is 3 kg. What is the heaviest part it can handle?
worked.s: Part ≤ payload − tooling = 3 − 1.2 = 1.8 kg.

worked.q: Fill in (slide exercise): max weight carried continuously = ___; up-and-down wrist motion = ___; perimeter of the work volume = ___.
worked.s: Payload; pitch; work envelope. A tight group on the target shows good accuracy and good repeatability.

recap: Payload includes the weight of the ___.

topics.title: Operating a Robot: Drives & Path Control (Ch 4)
topics.zh: 机器人运行：驱动与路径控制（第 4 章）

sections.b:
The combined movement of all joints creates the path of the end effector; coordinating the actuators to get the desired path is path control. Each joint (rotary or linear) is an actuator coupled to the joint by a mechanical transmission.

ActuatorCost / maintenanceBest for
Pneumatic cylindersLow cost, little maintenanceHigh speed, light payloads
Hydraulic cylindersMore costly, more maintenanceHeavy loads
Electric motorsModerate; easiest to controlApplications without very high speed or heavy loads

Actuator families — each can be linear or rotary/semi-rotary:

Electro-mechanicalPneumaticHydraulic
Conventional motors, linear motors, stepper motors, solenoidsBellows, cylinders, rotary motors, diaphragmsRams, rotary motors

Transmissions connect a load to an awkwardly placed actuator, convert motion (rotary ↔ linear) and convert torque.

DriveNotes
Chain drive / timing beltReduce speed and increase torque, but suffer some elasticity and backlash
Ordinary beltLittle used in robots because of slippage
Ball screwDearer than rack and pinion but more accurate (backlash controlled); balls roll, so friction is low and efficiency high
Harmonic driveRigid circular spline + flexible flexspline + elliptical wave generator. The wave generator forces the teeth to mesh in two places. Each turn of the wave generator moves the flexspline two teeth backwards → large reduction, essentially zero backlash, compact, low friction.

• Non-servo — simplest and cheapest; no feedback. Mechanical stops position the arm at the end of travel; set up by adjusting the stops. It "bangs" into them — a bang-bang robot. Low-technology, but precise and reliable if adjusted: pick and place, stuffing PCBs, loading/unloading machines.
  • Servo — has position feedback, so the controller knows where the arm is. Can stop anywhere in the envelope, do multi-point transfers and follow controlled paths; more sophisticated programming, higher cost. Point-to-point servo = medium technology; continuous-path servo = high technology.

TypeBehaviourApplications
Point-to-point (PTP)Moves from point to point without regard to the path; does no work while moving; path chosen for minimum travel time, not necessarily straightSpot welding, assembly, inspection, palletising, machine loading
Controlled path (PTP with coordinated path)Controller coordinates all axes so the tool follows a straight line (or circle, curve) with constant tool orientation; e.g. line trackingWelding, drilling, polishing, assembly
Continuous path (CP)Arm is led through the path; feedback signals are monitored continuously; the path matters more than the end pointsArc welding, spray painting, laying adhesive

worked.q: Slide exercise: fill the blanks.
worked.s: High speed + light payload → pneumatic actuators. Ordinary belts are unsuitable because of slippage. Servo vs non-servo differ by feedback. The harmonic drive suits robotic systems. Non-servo robots use mechanical stops.

recap: A bang-bang robot is a ___ robot.
Arc welding and spray painting need ___ path control.
The harmonic drive has essentially zero ___.

topics.title: Robot Peripherals: Sensors, Vision & Conveyors (Ch 5)
topics.zh: 机器人外围设备：传感器、视觉与输送机（第 5 章）

sections.b:
Sensors detect objects and send input signals to the controller or PLC. They are binary or analog, and contact or contactless.

SensorTypeNotes
Limit switch / micro switchContactMost common linear position sensor: the machine member physically actuates it at a set position
Strain gaugeContactSenses strain/force
Reed switchContactlessReeds in a sealed glass capsule close when a magnet (or a nearby coil — reed relay) comes near
InductiveContactlessResponds to metals only
CapacitiveContactlessElectrode instead of coil; any object (metal or not) changes the dielectric → detects all materials
PhotoelectricContactlessMetal and non-metal: responds to interruption of a light beam, or to reflection back to its source

Robot vision combines camera hardware and computer algorithms so robots can process visual data — e.g. a 2D camera finds an object to pick up. A machine vision system gives the controller the location, orientation and type of a part, and is used for recognition, inspection, sorting and non-contact measurement. Controllers that adjust their programmed positions in real time from this data use adaptive control.

  • 2D sensors: smart cameras (sensor and processor in one housing) or independent cameras (processing done on another device).
  • Eye-in-hand: camera mounted on or near the gripper — simplifies finding location and orientation, no blind spots from a static overhead camera.
  • 3D scanners: reverse engineering, metrology, exact measurements (e.g. defect depth); shape from shading, laser triangulation, structured light — quick approximate or slow precise scans. Used for bin picking.
  • Pattern matching: teach good and bad parts; the camera sets a pass/fail threshold (deformities, holes present, cap on a bottle). Colour matching: confirm an object’s colour.

A conveyor is line-restricted material-handling equipment: goods rest on or hang from it and move continuously or intermittently along a fixed route — a fixed installation that obstructs vehicles and people.

TypeAdvantagesDisadvantages
Unpowered (gravity or manual)Simpler, cheaper, easy maintenance; goods can accumulateSpeed varies with weight and nature of goods; short distances only
Powered (electric motors)Constant speed, adjustable to the goods; long distancesMore complicated; needs control circuitry and more maintenance
RollerPowered or not; unpowered accumulates automatically; heavy dutyGoods need a firm flat underside; each item should rest on at least 3 rollers
WheelSimple, low cost for light goods (under 20 kg); curved sectionsLight loads only
BeltGentle handling; inclines of 15–20° (up to 40° with treads/flights); high throughput and speed; quiet; adaptableAccumulation and marshalling difficult; belts damaged by hot or sharp goods
ChainUndemanding about the goods’ base; long goods; easy horizontal/vertical direction changesAccumulation hard; high power for sliding chains; noisy

Chains with rollers carry heavier loads such as pallets; chains without rollers are for low-friction work with light/medium loads (up to 1000 kg).

worked.q: Slide exercise: fill the blanks.
worked.s: The inductive sensor detects metallic material. For bin picking, use a 3D scanner. Conveyor chains fitted with rollers handle heavier loads. Roller conveyors suit goods with a flat surface. Limit switches are position sensors.

recap: A camera mounted on the gripper is an ___ system.
Items on a roller conveyor should touch at least ___ rollers.

topics.title: End Effectors (Ch 6)
topics.zh: 末端执行器（第 6 章）

sections.b:
The end effector — gripper, special device or fixture on the robot arm — actually does the work; the manipulator only moves it into place. If it opens and closes mechanically it is a gripper; if it is a tool or special attachment it is process tooling.

  • Finger grippers — the simplest is two fingers that open and close (also three-finger adaptive grippers). Usually only the finger mounts are bought; the fingers are designed and made in the local machine shop to suit the job.
  • Vacuum cups — chosen by the weight to be lifted; a vacuum hose to the cups holds a flat part; the controller switches suction on to pick and off to release.
  • Magnetic gripper — an electromagnet shaped to the part; the part must be flat and ferromagnetic.
  • Process tooling — welding torch, spray gun, grinder/polisher, silicone injector, nut driver, screwdriver. Often fitted through a safety joint that protects the tool in a crash.

• Grip force — how hard the end effector holds the object as the robot moves. It is not the same as payload: like a rock climber, lifting capacity and grip strength are separate.
  • Stroke — how far the fingers can open. Example data: total stroke 0–110 mm (adjustable), gripping force 3–40 N → maximum stroke 110 mm.
  • Weight — the tooling counts against the payload (4 kg tooling on a 10 kg robot leaves 6 kg for the part).

Jobsheet 4B: the gripper can make an external grip, or an internal grip with rotated fingertips, and is operated in the program with the RG() command.

topics.title: Robot Safety & Maintenance (Ch 8–9)
topics.zh: 机器人安全与维护（第 8–9 章）

sections.b:
The incident rate is low but robots have caused severe injuries and a few deaths, and the public has little tolerance for robots that injure people — so plan safety even more carefully than for other capital equipment.

  1. Justification — a key reason for using robots is to remove people from hazardous work: heat, noise, fumes, physical danger, radiation, toxic atmospheres (welding, forging, spray painting, die casting). Since the Occupational Safety and Health Act (OSHA) was enacted in 1971, worker safety has become a significant factor in promoting the substitution of robots for human labour in these dangerous jobs.
  2. Hazards from the robot itself — the robot creates new dangers that need precautions.

Areas of concern: safety requirements, emergency shutdown and power-failure modes.

Emergency shutdown (e.g. intruder close to the robot) is invoked automatically and causes one of:

  • Creep speed — extremely slow movement with low drive power, so no one is seriously hurt.
  • Freeze motion — all activity stops in the current position.
  • Decision-making intelligence — chooses the best response (creep or freeze).

• Braking — mechanical and electrical solenoids: on power failure the solenoids de-energise and immediately lock the arms in their last position, so the robot does not collapse onto itself or the load.
  • Avoid collapse — self-damping drive motors let the arm come down slowly under gravity.
  • After any power failure only operator-assisted manual restarts are allowed: the operator physically checks the cause, corrects it, and only then begins the start-up procedure.

Safety-function tests — at least once a year: emergency-stop button, freedrive mode, backdrive mode, individual joints, and verify the safety settings.

Maintenance depends on the robot’s construction, its duty cycle (how often and how fast it runs) and its environment. Manufacturers specify it in the operating or service information.

  • Articulated arm — regular checks of lubrication, preventive replacement of drive components, inspection of drive-system control components.
  • Controller — minimal: clean the airflow/cooling devices and replace the battery that keeps the memory of the controller’s computer.
  • ESD — use electrostatic-discharge precautions when handling electronic parts.
  • Visual inspection — disconnect the power cable; check all connections; check for dirt or dust inside the controller.

sections.b:

Direct contact = touching a normally live part. Indirect contact = touching exposed metal that became live due to a fault.

Dealing with shock: (1) switch OFF the power; (2) pull the victim free using a dry scarf/towel, or knock their hand clear with a piece of wood — never bare hands.

• Stay alert, keep good housekeeping, know basic first aid, be serious and attentive.
  • PPE: safety boots (insulate you), goggles (splinters, fumes, strong light), protective clothing, helmet (head injury risk), gloves (chemicals, hot work).
  • Tools: use correctly; machines guarded and maintained; power tools must be earthed (unless double-insulated) and the circuit fused/protected.
  • Unsafe conditions: proper tools, safe workshop layout with room to move, train workers, well-stocked first-aid kits.

Electricity is distributed as a 3-phase, 4-wire system from a delta–star step-down transformer whose secondary star point is earthed.

  • Between any two phase wires (line voltage): 400 V, 50 Hz
  • Between any phase and neutral (phase voltage): 230 V, 50 Hz
  • The three phases are 120° apart (Br, Bl, G = brown, black, grey).

Star: VL = √3 · VPIL = IP
UnitsVL, VP — volt (V)IL, IP — ampere (A)
Delta: VL = VPIL = √3 · IP
UnitsVL, VP — volt (V)IL, IP — ampere (A)

P = √3 · VL · IL · cos φP in W, cos φ = power factor
UnitsP — watt (W)VL — volt (V)IL — ampere (A)cos φ — no unit

Same formula for star and delta when the load is balanced. For a purely resistive load cos φ = 1.
