topics.title: Electrical Safety & Accident Prevention
topics.zh: 电气安全与事故预防

sections.b:
About this page. This is a study guide written in my own words. Its structure follows the tables of contents of representative books in your folder of Chinese textbooks; it is not a translation of any one book. Chinese practice follows GB standards, which can differ from what Singapore uses (SS 638, IEC) — for anything you do in the workshop, follow your lecturers and the Singapore rules.

The safety books in the folder open with the same classification.

TypeChineseWhat happens
Electric shock电击Current passes through the body and disturbs the heart, breathing and nerves. The most dangerous kind
Electrical injury电伤Damage to the body’s surface: arc burns, current burns, skin metallisation, electric marks
Electrical fire and explosion电气火灾和爆炸Overheating, arcs or sparks ignite insulation or an explosive atmosphere
Static electricity静电Discharge sparks ignite vapours or dust; shocks cause secondary accidents
Lightning雷电Direct strike, induced over-voltage, or surges entering along lines
Equipment and system accidents设备与系统事故Wrong switching, equipment damage, loss of supply

The books stress three features of electrical accidents: they are severe, they give little warning (electricity cannot be seen or smelt), and they occur in every industry.

FactorEffect
Size of the currentThe deciding factor. Around 1 mA is felt; around 10 mA a person may not be able to let go; from a few tens of milliamperes the heart can go into ventricular fibrillation
DurationThe longer the current flows, the greater the danger. This is why fast disconnection matters
PathPaths through the chest — hand to hand, or hand to foot — are the most dangerous
FrequencyPower frequency (50–60 Hz) is among the most dangerous for the heart
Body resistanceFalls sharply with wet or broken skin, larger contact area and higher voltage
The personHealth, age and fatigue all change the outcome

These figures explain two design rules: a residual current device for personal protection is rated to trip at 30 mA, and it must trip quickly.

Extra-low “safe” voltages. Chinese textbooks teach the series 42 V, 36 V, 24 V, 12 V and 6 V, chosen by how dangerous the location is: for example 36 V for hand lamps in ordinary places, 12 V inside metal vessels and in damp, confined spaces. A low voltage is only safe if its source is isolated from the mains, for example by a safety isolating transformer.

sections.h: Protection against direct and indirect contact
sections.b:
Direct contactIndirect contact
MeaningTouching a part that is live in normal serviceTouching a metal part that is normally dead but has become live through a fault
Main measuresInsulation · barriers and enclosures (屏护) · safe distance (间距) · extra-low voltage · a 30 mA residual current device as additional protectionProtective earthing (保护接地) · protective connection to neutral in TN systems (保护接零) · automatic disconnection · equipotential bonding · double insulation

Earthing systems are named with two or three letters.

SystemSupply neutralEquipment metalworkNote
TTEarthedConnected to its own local earth electrodeNeeds a residual current device to disconnect reliably
TN-SEarthedConnected to a separate protective conductor (PE) run with the supplyFive wires on three-phase: L1, L2, L3, N, PE
TN-CEarthedConnected to a combined neutral-and-protective conductor (PEN)Four wires; a broken PEN is dangerous
TN-C-SEarthedPEN in the first part, then split into N and PENever rejoin N and PE after the split
ITIsolated or earthed through an impedanceEarthedA first fault does not trip; an insulation monitor gives an alarm

Do not mix protective earthing and protective connection to neutral for different equipment on the same supply: a fault on the earthed equipment can make the metalwork of all the others live.

sections.h: Safe working: organisational and technical measures
sections.b:
The operation and maintenance books repeat these lists; in China they are examination content.

Organisational measures (组织措施)

  • The work ticket system (工作票): written authority stating the job, the place, the time and the safety measures.
  • The work permit system (工作许可): the person in charge of the plant confirms on site that it is safe before work starts.
  • The supervision system (工作监护): a named person watches the work and does nothing else.
  • The system for breaks, transfer and completion of work (工作间断、转移和终结).

Technical measures (技术措施), in this order

  1. Isolate (停电): disconnect from every possible source, with a visible break.
  2. Prove dead (验电): test with an approved tester that has just been checked on a known live source.
  3. Apply earths (装设接地线): connect the earth end first, then the conductor end; remove in the reverse order.
  4. Hang warning signs and fit barriers (悬挂标示牌和装设遮栏), for example “Do not switch on — people working”.

The “five preventions” against switching errors (五防)

  1. Prevent opening or closing a circuit breaker by mistake.
  2. Prevent opening or closing an isolator on load.
  3. Prevent applying an earth to a live conductor.
  4. Prevent switching on with an earth still applied.
  5. Prevent entering a live compartment by mistake.

In Singapore the equivalent ideas are isolation with lock-out and tag-out, proving dead, and a permit-to-work, carried out under the direction of a licensed electrical worker.

sections.h: Static electricity, fire and first response
sections.b:
Static electricity builds up when materials rub, separate or flow: belts, plastic film, powders, fuels in pipes. The hazard is the spark, which can ignite vapour or dust.

ControlHow it works
Earthing and bondingGives the charge a path away from conductive parts
Raising humiditySurface moisture lets charge leak away
Antistatic materials and additivesLower the resistance of the material
Ionisers (static eliminators)Neutralise charge on insulators
Limiting flow and separation speedLess charge is generated in the first place

Electrical fires usually start from a short circuit, an overload, a poor (high-resistance) connection, or an arc.

  • Cut off the supply first whenever possible.
  • If the equipment may still be live, use a carbon dioxide or dry powder extinguisher.
  • Do not use water or foam on live equipment.

If someone is being shocked: do not touch them. Switch off or pull the plug; if that is impossible, move the conductor away with a dry non-conducting object. Then call for help and give first aid — only if you are trained.

Books in the folder for this subject (25): 电气与静电安全 (2), 电气事故案例分析与防范 (2), 电气作业现场安全工作手册, 电气装置的保护接地, 电气消防技术 (3), 电气误操作事故100例及原因分析, and others — see the catalogue on the Extra tab.

terms: 剩余电流保护器（漏电保护器）
recap: The four technical measures, in order: isolate, ___, apply earths, hang signs and fit barriers.
A residual current device for personal protection is rated at ___ mA.
In a TN-S system the neutral (N) and the protective conductor (___) are separate throughout.

topics.title: Instruments, Electrical Testing & Maintenance
topics.zh: 电气仪表、试验与维修

sections.b:
About this page. This is a study guide written in my own words. Its structure follows the tables of contents of representative books in your folder of Chinese textbooks; it is not a translation of any one book. Chinese practice follows GB standards, which can differ from what Singapore uses (SS 638, IEC) — for anything you do in the workshop, follow your lecturers and the Singapore rules.

This is the largest group in the folder (about 75 books): electrical instruments, electrical testing, and maintenance and repair.

InstrumentChineseConnectionWatch out for
Ammeter电流表In series with the loadVery low resistance: connecting it across the supply is a short circuit
Voltmeter电压表In parallel with the loadVery high resistance
Multimeter万用表Depends on the functionSelect the function and range before connecting; measure resistance only on a dead circuit
Clamp meter钳形电流表Clamped around one conductorClamping line and neutral together reads zero
Insulation tester (megohmmeter)兆欧表（摇表）Between conductor and earth, or between conductors, on isolated equipmentDischarge the equipment after the test
Earth resistance tester接地电阻测试仪To the earth electrode and auxiliary spikesDisconnect the electrode from the installation first
Wattmeter / energy meter功率表 / 电能表Current coil in series, voltage coil in parallelObserve polarity marks

Accuracy class. Instruments are graded 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.5 and 5.0. The number is the largest permitted error as a percentage of full scale. A class 1.5 voltmeter with a 300 V range may be wrong by up to 4.5 V anywhere on the scale — so choose a range where the reading falls in the upper part of the scale.

Instrument transformers. A current transformer (CT) steps a large current down, usually to 5 A or 1 A; a voltage transformer (VT / PT) steps a high voltage down, usually to 100 V. Two rules are always examined: the secondary of a CT must never be open-circuited while the primary carries current, and the secondary of a VT must never be short-circuited.

The insulation tester applies a DC voltage and reads the resistance of the insulation in megohms. It has three terminals.

TerminalConnect to
L (line)The conductor under test
E (earth)The frame, or earth
G (guard)A guard ring on the insulation surface, so that surface leakage is not measured (used on cables and bushings)

Choose the test voltage by the equipment’s rated voltage. The usual textbook guide: a 500 V tester for equipment rated up to 500 V, 1000 V for equipment between 500 V and 3 kV, and 2500 V for higher voltages. Always check the standard that applies to the equipment.

  1. Isolate the equipment, prove it dead and discharge it.
  2. Check the tester: open leads should read infinity; shorted leads should read zero.
  3. Connect, apply the voltage steadily, and read at 60 seconds.
  4. Record the temperature, because insulation resistance falls as temperature rises.
  5. Discharge the equipment to earth before disconnecting the leads.

Absorption ratio K = R60 s ÷ R15 s. In good, dry insulation the reading keeps rising, so K is well above 1 (1.3 or more is the usual textbook figure for transformers). A ratio close to 1 suggests damp insulation. For large machines the polarisation index, R10 min ÷ R1 min, is used the same way.

Your Week 9 Drives slide grades motor insulation the same way: 2 MΩ or less is bad, 100 MΩ or more is excellent.

The “Electrical Testing” books (16 with that exact title) are written for technicians who test power equipment. The tests fall into two groups, and the order matters: non-destructive tests first, withstand tests last.

TestChineseWhat it findsGroup
Insulation resistance and absorption ratio绝缘电阻和吸收比Dampness, dirt, gross defectsNon-destructive
DC leakage current直流泄漏电流Local defects that the insulation tester misses, at a higher and adjustable voltageNon-destructive
Dielectric loss factor (tan δ)介质损耗因数Overall ageing and moisture in the insulationNon-destructive
DC resistance of windings绕组直流电阻Bad joints, broken strands, tap-changer contact problemsNon-destructive
Ratio, polarity and vector group变比、极性和接线组别Wrong turns or wrong connection of a transformerNon-destructive
Insulating oil tests绝缘油试验Breakdown voltage, moisture, acidity; dissolved-gas analysis shows overheating or discharge insideNon-destructive
Contact (loop) resistance of a breaker回路（接触）电阻Worn or dirty main contactsNon-destructive
Earth resistance接地电阻Whether the earthing system is still effectiveNon-destructive
AC power-frequency withstand工频交流耐压Whether the insulation has enough margin; the decisive testWithstand (can damage weak insulation)
DC withstand直流耐压Used on cables and machines; often combined with leakage measurementWithstand

Three occasions for testing: handover (acceptance) tests on new equipment (交接试验), preventive tests at regular intervals in service (预防性试验), and tests after repair.

Judging a result. Compare it three ways: against the limit in the standard; against the same equipment’s earlier results; and between the three phases, or between identical units. A sudden change matters even when the value is still inside the limit.

sections.h: Finding faults in wiring and equipment
sections.b:
The repair handbooks give a fixed routine before any instrument is used.

  1. Ask: what happened, when, and what was being done at the time.
  2. Look: burnt parts, loose wires, tripped devices, blown fuses.
  3. Listen and smell: humming, arcing, the smell of burnt insulation.
  4. Touch — only after isolating and proving dead: abnormal heat, loose terminals.
MethodChineseHow it is doneSupply
Voltage method电压法With the control circuit live, measure step by step along the rung. The point where the voltage disappears is just after the open partLive — only by a competent person
Resistance method电阻法With the supply off, measure continuity across each contact and coilDead
Bridging (jumper) method短接法Bridge a suspected open contact with an insulated jumper; if the coil pulls in, that contact is at fault. Never bridge a load or a protective deviceLive — only by a competent person
Substitution替换法Replace the suspect part with a known good oneDead while changing
Half-split二分法Test at the middle of the circuit to decide which half holds the fault, then repeatEither

Typical motor-circuit symptoms

SymptomLikely causes
Nothing happens when Start is pressedNo control supply, control fuse blown, overload relay tripped, Stop contact open
Contactor pulls in but drops out when Start is releasedHolding (self-holding) contact or its wiring is open
Motor hums but does not turnOne phase missing (single-phasing), or a mechanical jam. Switch off at once
Fuse blows or breaker trips at onceShort circuit or earth fault in the wiring or the motor
Overload relay trips after a whileMechanical overload, low voltage, single-phasing, or the relay set too low

The maintenance books divide the work by how deep it goes.

LevelChineseWhat is done
Routine inspection日常巡视检查Look, listen and feel while the plant runs: temperature, noise, vibration, smell, indications
Minor overhaul小修Clean, tighten connections, lubricate, replace worn brushes and contacts, test insulation
Major overhaul大修Dismantle, inspect every part, repair or rewind, reassemble and test fully before return to service

Keep records. A test or a repair is only useful later if it was written down: date, conditions, readings, what was changed, who did it. The trend over the years is what warns of a failure — the same idea as the predictive maintenance in Chapter 16 of your PLC notes.

Safety when testing. High-voltage tests are done by at least two people, with barriers and warning signs around the test area, and the equipment is discharged and earthed before anyone touches it.

Books in the folder for this subject (75): 电气试验 (16), 电气试验工 (7), 电气仪表 (8), 电气试验与油化验 (3 levels, with worked answers), 电气与电子测量技术 (2), 电气维修实用手册, 电气线路和电气设备故障检修技巧与实例, and others — see the catalogue on the Extra tab.

topics.title: Control Circuit Diagrams & Their Drawing Rules
topics.zh: 电气控制线路图及其绘制规则

sections.h: What a control circuit diagram is for
sections.b:
Source. Detailed notes on Chapter 2, “Basic links of electrical control circuits”, of 《电气与PLC控制技术》 (Cai Hongbin, ed.), one of the books in your folder. Written in my own words with every diagram redrawn as a ladder-style control circuit; the book draws them vertically. Device codes are the book’s: SB push button, KM contactor, FR thermal relay, KT time relay, KA intermediate relay, SQ limit switch, KS speed relay.

An electrical control circuit controls and protects the machine it serves. Machines differ, so their circuits differ, but every circuit is assembled from a small number of basic links. Chapter 2 teaches those links; this first part covers the drawings themselves.

A control circuit diagram is drawn with standard graphic symbols and letter codes. It records the structure and working principle of the control system, and it is the reference for installing, commissioning, operating, testing and repairing the equipment.

DrawingChineseWhat it showsUsed for
System diagram / block diagram系统图 / 框图The main parts as labelled boxes and the relations between themGetting the overall picture of a plant or a sub-system
Schematic (circuit) diagram电气原理图Every component and terminal, laid out by function. Not drawn to position or sizeUnderstanding how the circuit works; fault-finding
Layout (location) drawing电器位置图Where each device sits in the panel, with dimensionsBuilding the panel; finding a device
Wiring (installation) diagram电气安装接线图Real connections between devices and terminal blocks, with cable sizesWiring, checking wires, maintenance
Function diagram功能图The control logic, as the basis for drawing the schematicDesign
Parts list元件明细表Name, type, rating and quantity of every componentOrdering materials; repair

The designation of each device must be identical on the schematic, the layout drawing and the wiring diagram, so that you can move from one drawing to another.

Graphic symbols are built from three things: a general symbol for a class of device (a resistor, a capacitor), symbol elements that are combined to make a complete symbol (stator, rotor and leads make up a wound-rotor motor), and qualifying symbols added to a general symbol to give extra information (a resistor symbol becomes a variable resistor, a varistor or a thermistor).

Letter codes come in two kinds. Basic codes are one or two capital letters: the single letter gives the class (C capacitors, R resistors), and a second letter narrows it down (RP potentiometer, RT thermistor). Auxiliary codes describe function or state, usually from the English word: L limit, RD red, YB electromagnetic brake.

ItemCodeItemCode
Direct current / alternating currentDC / ACEarth / protective earthE / PE
AC generator / AC motorGA / MASquirrel-cage / wound-rotor induction motorMC / MW
DC generator / DC motorGD / MDStepper motor / servo motorTM / SM
TachogeneratorTGTransformerT
Current transformerTAVoltage transformerTV
Switch (single-pole, multi-pole)QIsolator, load switchQS
Circuit breakerQFManual, rotary (selector) switchSA
Push button (NO, NC, compound)SBPosition (limit) switchSQ
ContactorKMIntermediate relayKA
Thermal relayFRTime relayKT
Lighting lamp / signal lampEL / HLVoltmeter / ammeter / energy meterPV / PA / PJ

Marking of lines and terminals

  • Three-phase supply: L1, L2, L3; neutral N.
  • Main circuit after the supply switch: U, V, W. Branches get a number in front: 1U, 1V, 1W, 2U …
  • Nodes in a motor branch get numbers after the letter: the tens digit is the motor number and the units digit is the position along the branch, counted downwards. U11 is the first node of motor M1; U21 is its second node.
  • Motor winding starts are U, V, W; the ends are U′, V′, W′.
  • Control-circuit wires are numbered with up to three digits on the equipotential principle: all wires at the same potential share one number, and the number changes each time the wire passes through a contact or a coil.

sections.h: The rules for drawing a schematic
sections.b:
A schematic has two parts. The main circuit runs from the supply to the motor and carries the large current. The auxiliary circuits are control, lighting, signalling and protection: coils, relay contacts, auxiliary contacts of contactors, buttons, lamps, the control transformer.

  1. Standard symbols. Every motor, device and live part is shown with the nationally standardised graphic symbol and letter code.
  2. Layout. The main circuit is drawn in thick lines on the left or top; auxiliary circuits in thin lines on the right or bottom. In both, components are arranged in operating order, top to bottom and left to right.
  3. Parts of one device need not be drawn together, but they must carry the same letter code.
  4. Natural state. Every moving part is drawn as it is with no power applied and no external force acting: relay and contactor contacts as with the coil de-energised, controllers at the zero position, buttons and limit switches untouched.
  5. Orientation and crossings. The diagram may run horizontally or vertically. Keep lines few and avoid crossings. A solid dot marks an electrical junction; a hollow dot marks a removable or test connection; crossing lines with no dot are not connected.
  6. Related mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic devices are shown by simplified symbols so that their relation to the electrical control is clear.

sections.h: Zones, contact index and technical data
sections.b:
Zones. To find things quickly, the sheet is divided into zones. Capital letters run down the side and numbers run across; numbering starts at the top-left corner. A function bar above the circuit states in words what each column does — “supply switch”, “spindle motor”, “coolant pump”, “control”, “indication”, “lighting”.

Contact index. A coil and its contacts are drawn in different places, so an index is printed under each coil.

Under a contactor coilLeft columnMiddle columnRight column
Zone numbers of…its main contactsits normally-open auxiliary contactsits normally-closed auxiliary contacts
Under a relay coilLeft columnRight column
Zone numbers of…its normally-open contactsits normally-closed contacts

An unused contact is marked ×.

Technical data. Type and ratings are printed in small type under the device’s code. For a motor, the upper line is the rated power and the lower line the rated speed — for example 4 kW over 1500 r/min.

recap: In a schematic the main circuit is drawn in ___ lines on the left or top.
Under a contactor coil, the left column of the index gives the zones of its ___ contacts.

topics.title: Direct-Start Control Circuits of the Squirrel-Cage Motor
topics.zh: 鼠笼式电动机的直接起动控制线路

sections.b:
Source. Detailed notes on Chapter 2, “Basic links of electrical control circuits”, of 《电气与PLC控制技术》 (Cai Hongbin, ed.), one of the books in your folder. Written in my own words with every diagram redrawn as a ladder-style control circuit; the book draws them vertically. Device codes are the book’s: SB push button, KM contactor, FR thermal relay, KT time relay, KA intermediate relay, SQ limit switch, KS speed relay.

The three-phase squirrel-cage induction motor is simple, cheap, robust and easy to maintain; the book puts its share of electric drives at about 85 %. Its control circuits are built from contactors, relays and push buttons.

A small motor — the book’s figure is below 10 kW — may be started by applying full rated voltage directly. This is direct or full-voltage starting.

In every circuit below, the main circuit is the same: supply → isolator QS → fuses FU1 → contactor main contacts → thermal relay FR → motor. The control circuit is fed between two phases through fuse FU2.

No holding contact, no thermal relay

“Press and it moves, release and it stops.” Press SB → coil KM is energised → main contacts close → the motor runs. Release SB → KM drops out → the motor stops.

Used for: adjusting a machine tool and setting a tool. Because the motor runs only briefly, no thermal relay is fitted.

SB2 starts · KM holds · SB1 or FR stops

Start: close QS, press SB2 → KM pulls in → (a) main contacts close and the motor runs; (b) the normally-open auxiliary contact of KM closes across SB2 — self-holding. SB2 can now be released.

Stop: press SB1 → KM drops out → main and auxiliary contacts open → the motor stops.

Self-holding (自锁) means a contactor keeps its own coil energised through its own auxiliary contact. That contact is the self-holding contact.

ProtectionByHow
Short circuitFuses FU1 (main) and FU2 (control)The fuse element melts
OverloadThermal relay FRAfter a long overload FR operates, its normally-closed contact opens, KM drops out and the motor stops
Under-voltage and loss of voltageThe contactor and its self-holding contactWhen the voltage falls far enough, or fails, KM releases. When the supply returns the holding circuit is open, so the motor does not restart by itself

Under-voltage protection saves the motor from running at low voltage. Loss-of-voltage protection prevents the accidents an unexpected restart could cause.

sections.h: 3 · Jog and continuous running in one circuit
sections.b:
SB2 = run (KA latches, KA switches KM) · SB3 = jog (KM only while held)

Some machines need both. The book gives two ways.

  • With a compound button. A compound button SB3 is added to the self-holding circuit. Its normally-closed contact is in series with the holding contact, and its normally-open contact is in parallel with SB2. Pressing SB3 first breaks the holding path, then energises KM: the motor runs only while SB3 is held. SB2 and SB1 give continuous running.
  • With an intermediate relay KA (drawn above). SB2 energises KA, which latches itself and switches KM: continuous running. SB3 energises KM directly, with no latch: jog. SB1 stops both.

Swapping any two of the three supply phases reverses a three-phase motor. Two contactors do this: KM1 for forward, KM2 for reverse. If both close together the two swapped phases are short-circuited, so the control circuit must make that impossible.

Pressing SB2 and SB3 together closes KM1 and KM2: phase-to-phase short circuit

Forward → stop → reverse: SB1 must be pressed before changing direction

Forward → reverse → stop: the other direction’s button first drops out the running contactor

VersionInterlockOperating sequenceComment
aNone—Pressing SB2 and SB3 together causes a phase-to-phase short circuit. Not acceptable
bContactor (electrical) interlock: a normally-closed contact of each contactor in the other’s coil circuit“Forward – stop – reverse”Safe, but the stop button must be pressed before reversing
cDouble interlock: compound buttons and contactor contacts“Forward – reverse – stop”The opposite button first releases the running contactor, so the motor can be reversed directly

Interlock (互锁) means two contactors restrain each other so that only one can be energised. In practice a reversing contactor with a mechanical interlock is often used as well, for extra reliability.

At end A, SQ1 stops KM1 and starts KM2; at end B, SQ2 stops KM2 and starts KM1

A worktable must travel forward, reverse automatically at the end, travel back, and reverse again. Limit switches SQ1 (at end A) and SQ2 (at end B) are operated by a dog on the table.

  1. Press SB2 → KM1 pulls in and latches → the motor runs forward → the table advances.
  2. At A the dog operates SQ1: its normally-closed contact opens and KM1 drops out; its normally-open contact closes and KM2 pulls in and latches → the motor reverses → the table returns. SQ1 resets as the table leaves.
  3. At B the dog operates SQ2: KM2 drops out, KM1 pulls in → the table advances again.
  4. The cycle repeats until SB1 is pressed.

Pressing SB3 first starts the cycle in the reverse direction. The limit switches are doing the job the operator’s fingers did in the double-interlock circuit.

sections.h: 6 · Control from several locations, and 7 · sequence control
sections.b:
Stop buttons in series · start buttons in parallel

Several locations. A production line may be controlled from a central desk and also at each machine, for setting-up and repair. Each location has its own start and stop buttons. The rule: normally-open (start) buttons in parallel, normally-closed (stop) buttons in series.

M2 can start only after KM1 is on · M1 can stop only after KM2 is off

Sequence control. Where several motors must start or stop in a set order — a lathe spindle must not turn until the lubrication pump is running — the order is enforced with contacts.

RequirementHow it is wired
M2 may start only after M1 has startedA normally-open contact of KM1 in series with the coil circuit of KM2
M1 may stop only after M2 has stoppedA normally-open contact of KM2 in parallel with the stop button of KM1

The circuit drawn gives “start in order, stop in reverse order”.

worked.q: Define self-holding and interlock. (Exercise 2.1 in the book; the answer is mine.)
worked.s: Self-holding: a contactor keeps its own coil energised through its own normally-open auxiliary contact, wired in parallel with the start button. Interlock: two contactors restrain each other — a normally-closed contact of each is wired in series with the other’s coil — so that both can never be energised together.

worked.q: In a two-location control circuit, how are the start buttons and the stop buttons connected?
worked.s: Start (normally-open) buttons in parallel; stop (normally-closed) buttons in series. Any start button can then complete the circuit, and any stop button can break it.

worked.q: Three motors M1, M2, M3 must start in order: M2 only after M1, M3 only after M2. What is added to the control circuit? (Based on Exercise 2.6.)
worked.s: A normally-open contact of KM1 in series with the coil circuit of KM2, and a normally-open contact of KM2 in series with the coil circuit of KM3.

recap: In the double-interlock circuit the operating sequence is “forward – ___ – stop”.
Jog circuits have no ___ relay because the motor runs only briefly.
For M2 to start only after M1, a normally-open contact of KM1 is put in ___ with the KM2 coil.

topics.title: Reduced-Voltage Starting, Braking & Speed Control
topics.zh: 降压起动、制动与调速控制线路

sections.h: Why and when to start at reduced voltage
sections.b:
Source. Detailed notes on Chapter 2, “Basic links of electrical control circuits”, of 《电气与PLC控制技术》 (Cai Hongbin, ed.), one of the books in your folder. Written in my own words with every diagram redrawn as a ladder-style control circuit; the book draws them vertically. Device codes are the book’s: SB push button, KM contactor, FR thermal relay, KT time relay, KA intermediate relay, SQ limit switch, KS speed relay.

A larger motor — the book’s figure is above 10 kW — is usually started at reduced voltage, to cut the starting current and avoid a large dip in the supply voltage that would disturb other equipment.

MethodChineseStatus in the book
Resistance (or reactance) in series with the stator定子串电阻（或电抗）Basically no longer used
Star–delta星形—三角形In common use
Auto-transformer (starting compensator)自耦变压器（补偿器）Used for larger motors
Extended delta延边三角形Basically no longer used
Soft starter软启动器In common use

Resistors are connected in series with the stator during starting to drop part of the voltage and limit the current. When the speed has risen, the resistors are shorted out and the motor runs at rated voltage. A time relay does the changeover automatically.

  1. Press SB2 → KM1 pulls in and latches → the motor starts with resistors R in series. The on-delay time relay KT starts timing.
  2. After the set time (chosen from the starting time needed), the delayed-closing contact of KT closes → KM2 pulls in → its main contacts short out R → the motor runs at full voltage.

Improved version. In the simple circuit KM1 and KT stay energised for nothing once the start is over. The improved circuit puts a normally-closed contact of KM2 in the KM1 and KT coil circuits and gives KM2 its own self-holding contact. Once KM2 is on, KM1 and KT drop out: less energy wasted and longer life. Only KM2 remains energised while running.

KT times out: its delayed-opening contact drops KM3, its delayed-closing contact picks up KM2

Any squirrel-cage motor whose stator is delta-connected in normal running can be started in star.

  1. Close QS, press SB2 → KM1 (line), KM3 (star) and the on-delay time relay KT are energised; KM1 latches.
  2. Winding starts U, V, W are on the supply; ends U′, V′, W′ are joined by KM3 — star. Each phase winding gets 1/√3 of rated voltage.
  3. When the speed is high enough KT times out. Its delayed-opening contact opens → KM3 drops out. Its delayed-closing contact closes → KM2 (delta) pulls in and latches.
  4. KM2 joins U to V′, V to W′ and W to U′ — delta, full voltage on each winding.
  5. A normally-closed contact of KM2 cuts off KM3 and KT. KT is not left energised, and KM2 and KM3 are interlocked so that they cannot short-circuit the supply.
Quantity in star, compared with deltaValue
Voltage on each phase winding1/√3
Starting current drawn from the line1/3
Starting torque1/3

For: low cost and a simple circuit. Against: only one third of the starting torque, so it suits only no-load or light-load starting.

A motor whose windings are star-connected in normal running cannot use star–delta starting. Putting it in delta would apply √3 times its rated voltage to each winding. (This is Exercise 2.11 in the book.)

Auto-transformer (compensator) starting. During starting the stator is fed from the secondary of an auto-transformer, so it receives a reduced voltage. The transformer usually has 65 % and 85 % taps; choosing the tap sets the starting voltage. When the start is over the transformer is cut out and the stator is connected straight to the supply. Ready-made starting compensators are used, with manual or automatic operation.

In the automatic circuit: press SB2 → KM1 and KM2 pull in and latch, putting the auto-transformer in circuit, and KT starts timing. When KT times out, the intermediate relay KA pulls in and latches; KM1, KM2 and KT drop out, removing the transformer, and KA’s contact energises KM3, which puts the motor on full voltage.

Auto-transformer starting
SuitsLarger motors, whether normally star- or delta-connected
AdvantageStarting torque can be changed by changing the tap
DisadvantagesThe auto-transformer is expensive, and frequent starting is not allowed

Extended-delta starting. A method that needs no extra starting equipment yet gives more starting torque than star–delta. It applies to motors with nine terminals (the book cites the JO3 series). During starting, part of each phase winding is connected in delta and the rest in star, as if each side of the triangle had been extended. Each winding then carries a voltage lower than in delta but higher than in star, so the starting current is reduced while the torque is better than with star. A time relay then changes the winding to delta for running.

After the supply is cut, inertia keeps the rotor turning for some time. Machines that must stop quickly and accurately need forced braking: mechanical (usually an electromagnetic brake) or electrical.

Plugging (reverse-connection braking, 反接制动). The phase sequence of the stator supply is reversed, producing a torque opposite to the rotation.

SB1 is a compound button · KS closes above about 120 r/min and opens below about 100 r/min

  • The supply must be cut as the speed nears zero, or the motor will run backwards. So the circuit needs a device that senses speed: the speed relay KS, coupled to the motor shaft.
  • The stator current during plugging is about twice the direct-on-line starting current, so a resistor R is connected in the stator circuit while braking.
  1. Press SB2 → KM1 latches → the motor runs. Above about 120 r/min the normally-open contact of KS closes, ready for braking.
  2. Press the compound button SB1 → KM1 drops out; KM2 pulls in and latches through R → reversed-sequence supply → plugging.
  3. When the speed falls below about 100 r/min, KS opens → KM2 drops out → braking ends.

KM1 and KM2 are electrically interlocked. The book also gives a two-direction version in which KS has separate forward and reverse contacts and the same resistor R limits the starting current as well.

Dynamic braking (energy-consumption braking, 能耗制动). To avoid the heavy plugging current, the stator is disconnected from the AC supply and a DC current is passed through it. This sets up a stationary field; the spinning rotor cuts it and a braking torque results. The motor’s kinetic energy is turned into heat in the rotor.

KM2 connects DC to the stator; KT ends the braking after the set time

  • The DC comes from a transformer and bridge rectifier, through an adjustable resistor RP.
  • The larger the DC current, the stronger the braking, but too much damages the stator winding. The usual setting is 3 to 5 times the motor’s no-load current.
Control principleSensing deviceSuits
TimeTime relay KT ends the braking after a set timeLoads with a fairly steady torque, where the time setting can stay fixed
SpeedSpeed relay KS ends the braking at about 100 r/minMachines whose load changes through the transmission

sections.h: Speed control of the induction motor
sections.b:
n = (60 f / p) × (1 − s)p = pole pairs, f = supply frequency, s = slip

The formula shows three ways to change the speed: change the number of pole pairs p, the slip s, or the frequency f.

MethodHowNotes
Pole changing (变极调速)Reconnect the stator winding to change the number of pole pairsStepped: two, three or four speeds. For squirrel-cage motors
Rotor resistance (转子串电阻)Add resistance to the rotor of a wound-rotor motor through its slip ringsChanges the slope of the characteristic (the slip). More resistance → lower speed
Voltage regulation (调压调速)Lower the stator voltage, usually with a thyristor AC voltage regulatorTorque falls with the square of the voltage. Slip power is lost in the rotor, so efficiency is low
Frequency conversion (变频调速)Change the supply frequency with a variable-frequency driveOnce limited by the lack of a variable-frequency supply; now widespread thanks to power electronics

The 4/2-pole two-speed motor. The winding is reconnected from delta (four poles, synchronous speed 1500 r/min, low speed) to double star, YY (two poles, 3000 r/min, high speed). A star-to-double-star arrangement also exists.

  • Low speed: KM1 connects the winding in delta.
  • High speed: KM2 and KM3 connect it in double star.
  • After the pole change the phase sequence is reversed. Two supply leads must be swapped at the changeover, or the motor will change direction.

Rotor-resistance control of a wound-rotor motor. A master controller SA selects the speed. At position 0 the zero-position relay KV picks up and latches. At positions 1, 2 and 3 the motor runs with two resistors, one resistor, or no resistor in the rotor — low, medium and high speed. KV gives loss-of-voltage protection: after any loss of supply, SA must be returned to 0 before the motor can be restarted. The resistors waste a lot of energy, but the method is simple, so it is used on cranes and hoists that work intermittently.

worked.q: What is reduced-voltage starting, and which methods are common? (Exercise 2.10; the answer is mine.)
worked.s: Starting a motor with less than rated voltage on its stator, to limit the starting current and the dip it causes in the supply voltage; full voltage is applied once the speed has risen. Methods: stator series resistance or reactance, star–delta, auto-transformer, extended delta, and soft starters. Star–delta and soft starters are the common ones today.

worked.q: A motor draws 120 A when started direct-on-line in delta. About what line current does it draw when started in star, and what happens to its starting torque?
worked.s: Star starting takes one third of the delta starting current: 120 ÷ 3 = 40 A. The starting torque is also one third, so the method suits only no-load or light-load starts.

worked.q: Compare plugging and dynamic braking. (Exercise 2.15; the answer is mine.)
worked.s: Plugging: reverse the stator phase sequence. Strong, fast braking, but a very large current (about twice the direct starting current), so a resistor is added, and a speed relay must cut the supply near zero speed. Dynamic braking: disconnect AC and feed DC into the stator. Smoother, with a smaller current and no risk of reversing, but it needs a DC supply and the braking is weaker at low speed.

worked.q: A 4-pole motor on a 50 Hz supply has a slip of 4 %. Find its speed. If it is reconnected as a 2-pole motor at the same slip, what is the speed?

recap: In star–delta starting, the line current and the starting torque are both ___ of the delta values.
In plugging, the speed relay KS closes above about ___ r/min and opens below about ___ r/min.
The DC current for dynamic braking is usually set to ___ times the motor’s no-load current.

topics.title: DC Motor Control Circuits & Protection
topics.zh: 直流电动机控制线路与保护环节

sections.h: DC motor: starting through series resistance
sections.b:
Source. Detailed notes on Chapter 2, “Basic links of electrical control circuits”, of 《电气与PLC控制技术》 (Cai Hongbin, ed.), one of the books in your folder. Written in my own words with every diagram redrawn as a ladder-style control circuit; the book draws them vertically. Device codes are the book’s: SB push button, KM contactor, FR thermal relay, KT time relay, KA intermediate relay, SQ limit switch, KS speed relay.

A DC motor at standstill has no back e.m.f., so the armature current at the instant of starting is limited only by the small armature resistance. Resistors are therefore connected in series with the armature for starting and cut out in steps as the speed rises.

  1. Close the supply switches. The field winding is energised first and sets up the main field. Time relays KT1 and KT2 are energised, and their normally-closed, delayed-closing contacts open. So contactors KM2 and KM3, which short out the starting resistors, stay off, and resistors R1 and R2 are in the armature circuit.
  2. Press SB2 → KM1 pulls in and latches → the motor starts through R1 and R2. A normally-closed contact of KM1 opens and de-energises KT1 and KT2, which begin timing.
  3. As the speed rises, KT1’s contact closes first → KM2 pulls in → R1 is shorted out. The armature current rises, the torque rises, and the motor accelerates further.
  4. Then KT2’s contact closes → KM3 pulls in → R2 is shorted out. Starting is complete and the motor runs normally.

The field must be established before the armature is switched on, and must not be lost while the motor runs (see field-loss protection below).

sections.h: DC motor: reversing, braking and speed control
sections.b:
Reversing. From the torque formula, the direction of torque changes if either the field flux or the armature current is reversed. So there are two methods — and only one of them is applied at a time.

MethodKeep unchangedReverse
1Polarity of the armature windingThe field winding connections
2Polarity of the field windingThe armature winding connections

Dynamic braking. Press the stop button SB1 → KM1 drops out and disconnects the armature from the supply, while the field stays connected. The motor keeps turning by inertia and acts as a generator. A voltage relay KV across the armature is held in by this generated voltage; with KM1’s normally-closed contact now closed, the braking contactor KM4 pulls in and connects the braking resistor R4 across the armature. The speed falls sharply. As it falls, so does the armature voltage; KV releases, KM4 drops out, and braking ends.

The braking resistor must be chosen properly: too large and braking is slow; too small and the armature current exceeds its permitted maximum.

Speed control by armature resistance. A master switch SA has positions 1, 2 and 3. At position 3 contactors KM2 and KM3 are in, both resistors are shorted, and the motor runs at full speed. Turning SA to 2 releases KM3, putting R1 in the armature circuit: lower speed. Turning it to 1 releases KM2 as well, putting R1 and R2 in circuit: lowest speed. The speed with resistance in circuit is always below the speed at position 3.

sections.h: Protection 1 — short circuit, overload and over-current
sections.b:
Besides meeting the process requirements, a control system must act when something goes wrong, to protect people and equipment. The three protections below are all current protections, but the fault current, the operating value and the characteristic differ, so one cannot replace another.

ProtectionFaultDeviceKey facts
Short-circuit (短路保护)Damaged insulation or a wiring fault. The most common and most dangerous fault: the current is ten to several tens of times rated, and the electrodynamic force and heat can destroy equipment or start a fireFuse, or circuit breakerMust cut the supply quickly and reliably. A fuse’s operating value is affected by many factors and replacing it is a nuisance, so fuses suit less demanding, less automated systems. A circuit breaker also gives overload and under-voltage protection, but is more complex and operates less often
Overload (过载保护)Load too large or suddenly increased, supply voltage low, a phase missing. A small, short overload is acceptable if the winding stays within its permitted temperature; a long one ages the insulation and can burn out the windingThermal relay, or a motor protectorBecause of its thermal inertia, a thermal relay does not respond to a brief over-current or to a short circuit. So a circuit with a thermal relay still needs short-circuit protection
Over-current (过流保护)Running above rated current because of wrong starting or too large a load torque. Usually below six times rated — smaller than a short circuit, but more likely to occur, especially with frequent starting, reversing and repeated short-time dutyElectromagnetic over-current relayUsed mainly for DC motors and wound-rotor induction motors. Not normally fitted to squirrel-cage motors, which tolerate a brief over-current. Usually set to about 1.2 times the starting current. In these circuits it also acts as short-circuit protection

sections.h: Protection 2 — voltage, field and other protections
sections.b:
ProtectionWhy it is neededDeviceSetting
Loss of voltage (zero-voltage, 失压保护)A motor that stops when the supply fails and restarts by itself when it returns can injure people and damage equipment; many motors restarting together also cause a large current surge and voltage dipContactor with a self-holding contact; electromagnetic voltage relay; breaker with an under-voltage release—
Under-voltage (欠压保护)At low voltage with the same load torque, the current rises. Contactors and relays may also fail to hold in reliably, causing faultsUnder-voltage relayPicks up at (0.8–0.85) Ue; releases at (0.5–0.7) Ue. It uses a normally-open contact
Over-voltage (过压保护)Large supply swings can damage equipmentOver-voltage relayOperates at (1.05–1.2) Ue. It uses a normally-closed contact
Weak-field and loss-of-field (弱磁和失磁保护)A DC motor needs enough field to start; with a weak field the starting current is very large. If the field weakens or disappears while running, the speed rises rapidly — the motor “runs away” (飞车)Under-current relay in series with the field windingIf the field current falls too low or disappears, the relay releases and its normally-open contact cuts off the main contactor coil
Over-speedLifts, hoists and similar machines must not exceed a safe speedCentrifugal switch, or a tachogenerator—
OthersOver-travel, over-pressure, over-temperatureA contact operated by position, pressure or temperature, in series with the control circuit—

Ue is the rated voltage. The familiar interlock circuits also count as protection.

Earthing for safety is listed with the protections too; it is covered in the Electrical Safety guide.

worked.q: Why must the starting current of a DC motor be limited, and how is it done? (Exercise 2.18; the answer is mine.)
worked.s: At standstill there is no back e.m.f., so the armature current is the supply voltage divided by the small armature resistance — many times rated. It would damage the commutator and winding and jolt the machine. It is limited by starting resistors in series with the armature, cut out in steps as the speed rises, or by starting at reduced armature voltage.

worked.q: A 220 V DC motor has an armature resistance of 0.5 Ω. Find the armature current at the instant of starting with no starter. What total resistance limits it to 44 A?
worked.s: No starter: I = 220 ÷ 0.5 = 440 A. For 44 A: total R = 220 ÷ 44 = 5 Ω, so the starting resistance needed is 5 − 0.5 = 4.5 Ω.

worked.q: A thermal relay is fitted. Why are fuses still needed?
worked.s: A thermal relay has thermal inertia: it takes time to heat up, so it cannot respond to the sudden, very large current of a short circuit. The fuse (or circuit breaker) must clear that fault at once. The thermal relay protects against long overloads, which a fuse does not sense.

worked.q: An under-voltage relay protects a 380 V circuit. Between what voltages will it pick up and release?

recap: A DC motor is reversed by reversing either the ___ winding or the armature winding, not both.
An over-current relay is usually set to about ___ times the starting current.
Loss of field in a running DC motor makes its speed ___ rapidly.

topics.title: Low-Voltage Apparatus: Classes, the Electromagnet, Contacts & Arc Control
topics.zh: 低压电器：分类、电磁机构、触点与灭弧

sections.b:
Source. Detailed notes on Chapter 1, “Common low-voltage apparatus”, of 《电气与PLC控制技术》 (Cai Hongbin, ed.), one of the books in your folder. Written in my own words; curves and block diagrams are redrawn. Type numbers such as CJ20, JR16 or DZ20 are Chinese product series: learn what each one is, not the number. Ratings are quoted from the book’s tables and are for study, not for selecting equipment.

An electrical apparatus is any device that, on an outside signal or by itself, switches a circuit on or off, or changes its parameters, so that the circuit or a non-electrical quantity is switched, controlled, protected, measured or regulated.

Low-voltage means the device works in circuits of up to AC 1200 V or DC 1500 V. Almost everything in a motor control panel falls in this range.

Classified byClassesExamples
Object controlledDistribution apparatus (for the power supply system) · Control apparatus (for drives and automation)Breakers, isolators · contactors, relays
Job in the circuitControl — switches the circuitSwitches, relays, contactors
Master (command) — gives the orderPush buttons, master switches, limit switches
Protective — guards circuit and equipmentFuses, thermal relays, surge arresters
Actuating — does a mechanical jobElectromagnets, electromagnetic clutches
How it is operatedAutomatic (electromagnetic or compressed-air force) · Non-automatic (by hand or by a moving machine part)Contactor, relay · knife switch, button, limit switch
Working principleElectromagnetic · Non-electrical-quantity (responds to force, speed, temperature, pressure, level)Contactor, voltage relay · limit switch, speed relay, thermal relay

FamilyMembers
ContactorsAC contactor · DC contactor
RelaysElectromagnetic: voltage, current, intermediate · Time: DC electromagnetic, air-damped, motor-driven, electronic · Thermal · temperature · speed · pressure
Position (limit) switchesDirect-acting · roller · micro
Low-voltage circuit breakersFrame type · moulded-case · intelligent
IsolatorsKnife switch and its enclosed forms
FusesPorcelain plug-in · tube · screw · fast-acting
OthersPush buttons · signal lamps · universal changeover switch

• Fieldbus — devices that communicate, so a controller can read their state and set them remotely.
  • Solid-state devices — thyristor-based contactors, relays and soft starters with no moving contacts.
  • Vacuum devices — the arc is broken in a vacuum bottle.
  • Two product lines — high-performance ranges and low-cost economy ranges.
  • Environmentally friendly materials, built-in lightning and surge protection.
  • Compact, intelligent assemblies and new contact materials.

sections.h: Three parts of every electromagnetic device
sections.b:
Contactors and most relays are built the same way:

PartJob
Electromagnetic mechanismThe sensing part. Turns electrical energy into the mechanical movement of the armature
Contact systemThe acting part. Makes and breaks the circuit
Arc-extinguishing devicePuts out the arc drawn when contacts open under current

The mechanism is a coil plus a magnetic circuit: a fixed core, a moving armature and the air gap between them. Common shapes are the single E, single U, solenoid (plunger) and double E. The armature either moves in a straight line (direct-acting) or swings about a pivot or knife edge (rotating).

DC coilAC coil
Core materialSolid soft steel or engineering ironLaminated silicon steel
WhySteady flux, so no iron loss in the coreAlternating flux causes eddy-current and hysteresis loss; laminations cut it down
Where the heat comes fromThe coil onlyCoil and core
Coil shapeLong and thin, no former, wound in contact with the core to shed heatShort and thick, on a former, with a gap to the core
Voltage coilCurrent coil
ConnectionIn parallel with the supplyIn series with the load
WindingMany turns of thin wire, high impedanceFew turns of thick wire, low impedance
Responds toVoltageCurrent

Two forces act on the armature. The attraction of the electromagnet pulls it in. The reaction force of the return spring and the contact springs pushes it out; for a spring it rises in proportion to how far the spring is compressed.

F = (10⁷ ÷ 8π) · B² · S

F: force of attraction, in newtons (N) · B: flux density in the air gap, in teslas (T) · S: pole-face area, in square metres (m²).

Curves 1 and 2 must stay above curve 3 over the whole travel for the armature to pull in; to release, the attraction must fall below curve 3.

DC electromagnet. The coil current is I = U ÷ R. It does not depend on the gap. With constant ampere-turns the flux rises as the gap shrinks, and the force varies as 1 ÷ δ²: weak when open, very strong when closed (curve 1).

AC electromagnet. With a fixed supply voltage the peak flux is fixed, so the average force changes little with the gap (curve 2). What changes is the current: a large gap means low inductance, so the coil draws a current several times its sealed value at the instant of switching on.

Consequence. If the armature of an AC device is jammed and cannot close, the large current persists and the coil overheats and burns out. The same is why AC devices are limited in how many times per hour they may operate.

Matching. To pull in reliably, attraction must exceed reaction over the whole stroke. It should not exceed it by much, or the armature slams in and wears the contacts and pole faces. To release, attraction (from residual flux) must fall below the reaction force.

sections.h: Why an AC magnet hums, and the shading ring

sections.b:
Contacts carry the current, so contact resistance decides how hot they run. Good contacts need enough pressure, a clean surface and a suitable material; silver and silver alloys are used because their oxide still conducts.

Contact formTouches atUsed for
PointA pointSmall currents: relay contacts, auxiliary contacts
SurfaceA whole faceLarge currents: main contacts of larger contactors
Line (finger)A line, with a rolling and wiping action as it closesFrequent switching of large currents; the wipe cleans off oxide
  • Main contacts switch the main circuit; auxiliary contacts switch control circuits.
  • Normally open (NO): open with the coil off. Normally closed (NC): closed with the coil off.
  • A bridge contact has one moving bridge and two fixed contacts, so the circuit is broken in two places at once.

When contacts part under current, the air between them ionises and an arc forms. It keeps the circuit alive after the contacts have opened, and its heat burns the contacts. Every method below does the same things: lengthen the arc, cool it, or split it.

MethodHow it worksTypical use
Electrodynamic force with double-break bridge contactsThe current in the two arcs and the bridge forms a loop whose own magnetic force throws the arcs outward and stretches themSmall AC contactors
Magnetic blow-outA blow-out coil in series with the contact makes a field that drives the arc up into the chute. Coil current and arc current reverse together, so the force direction never changes; the bigger the current, the stronger the blowMostly DC contactors
Grid plates (de-ion grids)Steel plates pull the arc in and cut it into many short arcs. Each short arc needs its own voltage to survive, and the plates cool itBest on AC, where the current passes through zero; AC contactors and breakers
Arc chute / narrow slotA ceramic or asbestos-cement cover with narrow slots; the arc is squeezed against the cold wallsDC contactors, larger AC contactors

worked.q: An AC contactor rated 220 V is connected to a 220 V DC supply. What happens, and why?
worked.s: The coil overheats and burns. An AC coil limits its current mainly by its inductive reactance, so it is wound with a low resistance. On DC there is no reactance, only that small resistance, so I = U ÷ R is many times the normal current. (Chapter exercise 1.2(1): the statement that it can be used on both is false.)

worked.q: The shading ring on an AC contactor core has cracked. What will you notice, and why?
worked.s: Loud humming and vibration, and in time worn pole faces and loose parts. Without the ring there is only one flux, and its force falls to zero 100 times a second on a 50 Hz supply. Each time, the springs start to push the armature away. (Exercise 1.8.)

worked.q: True or false: the exciting current of a DC electromagnet is proportional to the armature travel.
worked.s: False. The coil current is I = U ÷ R and does not depend on the air gap. It is the AC coil whose current depends on the gap. (Exercise 1.2(7).)

worked.q: How does an arc arise when a switch opens, and what are the usual ways to put it out?
worked.s: As the contacts part, the last point of contact becomes very hot and the gap is tiny, so the field across it is strong. Electrons are pulled out and the air ionises into a conducting, glowing channel. Methods: electrodynamic force with double-break contacts, magnetic blow-out, grid plates, and the arc chute or narrow slot. (Exercise 1.4.)

recap: Low-voltage apparatus works at up to AC ___ V or DC 1500 V.
The core of an AC electromagnet is ___ to reduce eddy-current and hysteresis loss.
The ___ ring stops an AC electromagnet from vibrating.
Magnetic blow-out is used mostly on ___ contactors.

topics.title: Contactors
topics.zh: 接触器

sections.b:
Source. Detailed notes on Chapter 1, “Common low-voltage apparatus”, of 《电气与PLC控制技术》 (Cai Hongbin, ed.), one of the books in your folder. Written in my own words; curves and block diagrams are redrawn. Type numbers such as CJ20, JR16 or DZ20 are Chinese product series: learn what each one is, not the number. Ratings are quoted from the book’s tables and are for study, not for selecting equipment.

A contactor makes and breaks a main circuit from a distance, and does it frequently. Its usual load is a motor; it also switches heaters, lighting, welding sets and capacitor banks. It releases by itself when the voltage is lost, which gives under-voltage and no-voltage protection.

Contactors are named by what drives them (electromagnetic, pneumatic, hydraulic) and by the current in the main contacts: AC or DC. The book quotes upper limits of AC 1140 V, 630 A and DC 440 V, 630 A for the common ranges.

PartIn an AC contactor
Electromagnetic mechanismCoil, laminated core with shading ring, armature. Usually double-E, direct-acting
Main contactsThree normally-open poles for the motor circuit, bridge type with double break
Auxiliary contactsSmall NO and NC contacts for the control circuit: self-holding, interlocking, signalling
Arc-extinguishing systemFitted to contactors above about 10 A: chute with grid plates
Other partsReturn spring, contact pressure springs, buffer spring, frame, terminals

A DC contactor has a solid soft-steel core and no shading ring, a long thin coil, one or two main poles with finger (line) contacts, and magnetic blow-out, because a DC arc has no current zero and is harder to break.

sections.h: How it works, and the order the contacts move
sections.b:
Coil energised → attraction exceeds the spring force → armature pulls in → main contacts close, auxiliary NO contacts close and NC contacts open. Coil de-energised, or voltage too low → springs return the armature → every contact goes back.

FirstThen
Pulling inNC contacts openNO contacts close
ReleasingNO contacts openNC contacts close

There is a very short moment in between when both are open. Break-before-make is what lets an NC contact of one contactor interlock another safely, as in the forward–reverse circuit of Chapter 2.

sections.h: Ratings to read on the nameplate
sections.b:
RatingMeaningValues the book lists
Rated voltageVoltage of the main contactsAC 220, 380, 660, 1140 V · DC 220, 440, 660 V
Rated currentCurrent of the main contacts under stated conditions6, 10, 16, 25, 40, 60, 100, 160, 250, 400, 600, 1000, 1600, 2500, 4000 A
Auxiliary contact voltageAC 380 V · DC 220 V
Coil rated voltageVoltage of the control supply. It need not equal the main voltageChosen to match the control circuit
Operating frequencyOperations allowed per hourAC contactors 300–1200 per hour
Mechanical and electrical lifeOperations without load, and under rated loadMillions, and hundreds of thousands

Do not confuse the rated voltage (main contacts) with the coil voltage. A contactor with 380 V main contacts may have a 220 V, 110 V or 36 V coil.

Series named in the book. AC: CJ10, CJ12, CJ20, CJX1, CJX2, 3TB, and imported Mitsubishi S-K, Telemecanique LC1-D / LC2-D, BBC B, Siemens 3TB / 3TD. DC: CZ10, CZ18, CZ21, CZ22.

• Not for flammable or explosive atmospheres, conductive dust, or outdoors without protection.
  • Watch for overheating of contacts and coil, and check that the three poles close and open together.
  • A contactor has no short-circuit breaking ability of its own. Always use it with fuses or a circuit breaker.
  • Keep the shading ring sound and the pole faces clean: oil or dust on the faces causes noise or slow release.
  • Inside a closed cabinet it runs hotter, so derate it.
  • Replace badly burnt contacts in sets. Never file silver contacts flat just because they look black; the dark oxide still conducts.

AC contactorDC contactor
Main contacts carryACDC
CoreLaminated, with shading ringSolid, no shading ring
CoilShort and thick; inrush current when closingLong and thin; same current open or closed
Main contactsThree poles, bridge typeOne or two poles, finger type
Arc controlElectrodynamic force, grid platesMagnetic blow-out
Operating frequencyLower, limited by coil inrush heatingHigher
If the armature jamsCoil burns outCoil is unaffected

worked.q: State the purpose, construction and working principle of an AC contactor in three sentences.
worked.s: Purpose: remote, frequent switching of an AC main circuit, with release on loss of voltage. Construction: electromagnetic mechanism, main and auxiliary contacts, arc chute, springs and frame. Principle: the energised coil pulls in the armature, which closes the main and NO contacts and opens the NC contacts; when the coil loses its supply the springs return everything. (Exercise 1.6.)

worked.q: Looking at a contactor, how can you tell whether it is AC or DC?
worked.s: Look at the core and the coil. Laminated core with a copper shading ring in the pole face, and a short fat coil: AC. Solid core, no ring, long thin coil and a blow-out coil: DC. (The type letters also tell you: CJ is AC, CZ is DC.) (Exercise 1.7.)

worked.q: True or false: when an AC contactor is energised but the core cannot close, the coil may burn out.
worked.s: True. With the gap open the inductance is low and the coil current stays several times its normal value. (Exercise 1.2(2).)

worked.q: A contactor is marked 380 V, 40 A, coil 220 V. Which figure do you match to the motor, and which to the control circuit?
worked.s: 380 V and 40 A are the main-contact ratings: match them to the motor’s line voltage and current. 220 V is the coil rating: the control circuit must supply 220 V.

recap: When a contactor coil is energised, the ___ contacts open first and then the normally-open contacts close.
The rated voltage of a contactor refers to its ___ contacts.
A contactor must be used together with ___ protection, because it cannot break a short circuit.

topics.title: Relays: Electromagnetic, Thermal, Time, Speed & Others
topics.zh: 继电器：电磁式、热、时间、速度及其他

sections.b:
Source. Detailed notes on Chapter 1, “Common low-voltage apparatus”, of 《电气与PLC控制技术》 (Cai Hongbin, ed.), one of the books in your folder. Written in my own words; curves and block diagrams are redrawn. Type numbers such as CJ20, JR16 or DZ20 are Chinese product series: learn what each one is, not the number. Ratings are quoted from the book’s tables and are for study, not for selecting equipment.

A relay senses a quantity and, when it reaches a set value, switches a control circuit. The quantity can be electrical (voltage, current) or not (time, temperature, speed, pressure, level). Every relay has a sensing part, which measures the input, and an output part, usually contacts.

Return coefficient K = x₁ ÷ x₂. It is always less than 1.

The output does not follow the input smoothly. It jumps. As the input x rises nothing happens until the pick-up value x₂; then the output goes to y₁. As x falls again the output stays at y₁ until the lower release value x₁. The ratio K = x₁ ÷ x₂ is the return coefficient.

  • A general control relay wants a low K (about 0.1–0.4), so that small dips in the input do not drop it out.
  • A protective relay such as an under-voltage relay wants a high K (above about 0.6), so that it responds to a small change.

RelayContactor
SwitchesControl circuitsMain circuits
Contact currentSmall, typically 5 A or lessLarge
Arc deviceNoneYes, above about 10 A
Main and auxiliary contactsNo distinctionSeparate
Input it responds toMany electrical and non-electrical quantitiesVoltage only
Wanted qualityAccurate, sensitive, repeatable actionBreaking capacity and long life

Built like a small contactor, usually with a U-shaped core. On DC relays a thin non-magnetic copper shim (0.1–0.5 mm) sits between armature and core so that residual magnetism cannot hold the armature in after the coil is switched off.

RelayCoilTypes and actionTypical job
Current relayIn series; few thick turnsOver-current: stays released in normal running, picks up when current exceeds the setting. Under-current: stays pulled in normally, drops out when current falls too lowOver-current: protecting motors that start often or under heavy load. Under-current: loss-of-field protection of a DC motor
Voltage relayIn parallel; many thin turnsOver-voltage: picks up at about 1.1 × rated voltage or more. Under-voltage and zero-voltage: pulled in normally, drop out when the voltage sags or disappearsVoltage protection of the circuit
Intermediate relayVoltage coilA voltage relay with many contact pairs of 5–10 AMultiplying the number of contacts; passing a signal between circuits; driving a small load directly

Intermediate relay data from the book. AC type: for circuits up to 500 V; coils 12, 36, 127, 220, 380 V; 8 contact pairs at 5 A; up to 1200 operations per hour. DC type: for circuits up to 110 V; coils 12, 24, 48, 110 V; coil power 3 W or less; 3 NO + 3 NC at 3 A.

ParameterMeaning
Rated voltage / currentOf the coil, and of the contacts
Pick-up valueSmallest input that makes the relay operate
Release valueLargest input at which it lets go
Return coefficientRelease ÷ pick-up
SensitivitySmallest power (or ampere-turns) that will operate it
Operate and release timeFrom the input changing to the contacts finishing their movement
SettingThe pick-up value the user has adjusted it to

How settings are changed. Tightening the reaction spring or widening the initial air gap raises the pick-up value. Changing the thickness of the non-magnetic shim changes the release value: a thicker shim means a higher release value.

Type (book’s Table 1.2)Adjustable range
DC voltage relayPick-up 30–50 % UN · release 7–20 % UN
AC over-voltage relayPick-up 105–120 % UN
Over-current relayAC 110–350 % IN · DC 70–300 % IN
DC under-current relayPick-up 30–65 % IN · release 10–20 % IN
DC electromagnetic time relayOff-delay 0.3–0.4 s, 0.8–3.0 s, 2.5–5.0 s, 4.5–10 s, 9–15 s by model

A thermal relay protects a motor against overload by using the heating effect of the current. A heater in series with each motor phase warms a bimetal strip: two metals rolled together, an active layer with a high expansion coefficient (an iron-nickel-chromium alloy) and a passive layer with a low one (iron-nickel). When heated the strip bends towards the passive side. After a long enough overload it bends far enough to trip a mechanism that opens an NC contact in the contactor coil circuit. The contactor drops out and the motor stops.

  • Inverse-time: the larger the overload, the sooner it trips. Rated current: no trip.
  • It cannot protect against short circuit. The strip needs time to heat, and a short circuit must be cleared at once. Fuses or a breaker do that job.
  • It should not trip during starting. The starting current is large but lasts only a few seconds, too short to heat the strip. This thermal inertia is exactly what makes the relay suitable for motors.
  • Phase loss. A relay with a differential mechanism also trips when one phase is lost or the phases are badly unbalanced. This matters most for delta-connected motors, where the winding current can be excessive while the line current still looks acceptable.
  • Reset is manual or automatic, after the strip has cooled. The setting current is adjusted with a knob to the motor’s rated current.
  • Unsuitable for motors on repeated short-time duty or with frequent heavy starts; use an over-current relay or embedded temperature sensors there.

Book’s example series: JR16. The JR16-20 frame takes heaters from 0.35 A to 22 A and the JR16-60 from 22 A to 63 A, so one frame size can carry heaters of several ratings.

On-delay: the contact waits t after the coil is energised and returns at once. Off-delay: the contact acts at once and waits t after the coil is de-energised.

A time relay puts a set delay between receiving its signal and moving its contacts.

TypeHow the delay is madeGood pointsLimits
DC electromagneticA copper sleeve on the core. When the coil is switched off, the collapsing flux induces a current in the sleeve that keeps the flux alive a little longerSimple, reliable, long lifeOff-delay only, short (up to about 15 s), DC only
Air-damped (book’s example JS7-A)An electromagnet releases a rod that can move only as fast as air leaks into a rubber air-bag through a small adjustable hole; the rod then operates a micro-switchSimple, cheap, wide range, not affected by supply voltage or frequencyLow accuracy, error ±10–20 %
Motor-drivenA small synchronous motor drives a gear train and camLong, accurate delaysComplex, costly
ElectronicAn RC charging circuit or a digital counterWide range, accurate, small, long lifeSee Chapter 1.8

JS7-A facts. It has an electromagnet, an air-bag delay unit and micro-switches: one micro-switch is instantaneous and one is delayed. The delay is set with a screw that changes the air-inlet opening. Turning the electromagnet through 180° converts an on-delay relay into an off-delay one. Contacts 380 V, 5 A; coils 24, 36, 110, 127, 220, 380, 420 V; delay ranges 0.4–60 s and 0.4–180 s; 600 operations per hour.

ContactWhen the coil is energisedWhen the coil is de-energised
InstantaneousActs at onceReturns at once
On-delay NOCloses after the delayOpens at once
On-delay NCOpens after the delayCloses at once
Off-delay NOCloses at onceOpens after the delay
Off-delay NCOpens at onceCloses after the delay

RelayConstructionActionUse
Speed relay (JY1)A permanent-magnet rotor on the motor shaft, inside a free-swinging stator ring that carries a cage windingThe spinning magnet induces current in the ring, which is dragged round and pushes a lever onto the contacts. Above about 120 r/min the contacts operate; below about 100 r/min they return. Separate contact sets serve the two directionsPlug (reverse-current) braking: it cuts the reversed supply when the motor has almost stopped, so the motor does not run backwards
Liquid-level relay (JYH-02)A float carrying a magnet inside the tank; a fixed magnet and contacts outsideAt the high or low mark the float magnet repels the outer magnet and flips the contactsStarting and stopping a pump to hold the level in a boiler or water tank
Reed relayTwo iron-nickel reeds sealed in a glass tube filled with inert gasA coil round the tube, or a magnet brought near, magnetises the reeds; they attract and touchFast, sealed against dust and corrosion, very long life, tiny load current

worked.q: What is the difference between the protection given by a fuse and by a thermal relay? Why can one not replace the other?
worked.s: A fuse gives short-circuit protection: it must clear a very large current at once. A thermal relay gives overload protection: it responds slowly to a modest excess current. The thermal relay is too slow for a short circuit. A fuse big enough not to blow on starting current will not melt on a 20–50 % overload. A motor circuit needs both. (Exercise 1.3(1).)

worked.q: A motor’s starting current is several times its rated current. Will a thermal relay set at the rated current trip during starting?
worked.s: No, for a normal start. The bimetal has thermal inertia; a few seconds of starting current does not heat it enough to bend to the trip point. It will trip if starting is very long or repeated many times in quick succession. (Exercises 1.3(2) and 1.9.)

worked.q: Compare an AC contactor with an intermediate relay.
worked.s: Same: both are electromagnetic, with a voltage coil, an armature and NO / NC contacts, and they work the same way. Different: the contactor has main contacts for large currents and an arc chute, and it switches the main circuit; the intermediate relay has many equal contacts of about 5 A, no arc device, and switches control circuits. (Exercise 1.3(5).)

worked.q: A voltage relay picks up at 176 V and releases at 66 V. Find its return coefficient.
worked.s: K = x₁ ÷ x₂ = 66 V ÷ 176 V = 0.375 (no unit). This is my own example to practise the formula.

worked.q: True or false: (a) the rated current of a thermal relay is the rated current of its contacts; (b) an intermediate relay is in essence not a voltage relay.
worked.s: (a) False. It is the rated current of the heater circuit that carries the motor current. (b) False. An intermediate relay is a voltage relay with more contacts. (Exercises 1.2(13) and (19).)

recap: The return coefficient of a relay is the ___ value divided by the pick-up value.
A thermal relay works on the ___ effect of the current and protects a three-phase motor against overload.
An intermediate relay turns one input signal into ___ output signals, or amplifies the signal.
A relay whose contacts move a set time after its sensing element receives the signal is a ___ relay.
A speed relay is used mainly for ___ braking.

topics.title: Command Devices & Fuses
topics.zh: 主令电器与熔断器

sections.b:
Source. Detailed notes on Chapter 1, “Common low-voltage apparatus”, of 《电气与PLC控制技术》 (Cai Hongbin, ed.), one of the books in your folder. Written in my own words; curves and block diagrams are redrawn. Type numbers such as CJ20, JR16 or DZ20 are Chinese product series: learn what each one is, not the number. Ratings are quoted from the book’s tables and are for study, not for selecting equipment.

A master (command) device gives the order. It switches only the small current of a control circuit; a contactor or relay then does the work.

Push button. A button cap, a return spring, bridge-type moving contacts and fixed contacts in a housing. A combination button has one NO and one NC pair: pressing it opens the NC first, then closes the NO; on release the NO opens first.

Colour or shapeMeaning
RedStop
GreenStart
Mushroom head, redEmergency stop
With lampThe cap lights to show state
Key-operated, rotaryGuarded against casual use

Book’s series: LA2, LA9, LA10, LA19, LA20. Typical rating 380–500 V, 2–5 A.

A limit switch is a button pressed by the machine. A moving part strikes its operating head and the contacts change over, turning position into an electrical signal. Whether it is called a travel switch, limit switch or end-of-travel switch depends only on its job: sequencing a movement, or stopping over-travel.

It has three parts: operating head, contact system, housing.

TypeFeatureNote
Direct-acting (plunger)Works like a buttonContact speed depends on the speed of the machine part. Below about 0.4 m/min the contacts part slowly and burn
Roller (rotary)A roller arm with a snap-action spring mechanismContacts snap over whatever the approach speed. Single-roller types reset themselves; double-roller types stay put until struck from the other side
Micro-switchA bowed leaf spring gives a snap action with very small travel and forceSmall, sensitive, accurate; lower contact rating

Book’s data. LX19 and JLXK1 series: 5 A, AC 500 V / DC 440 V, contact changeover 0.04 s or less, one NO and one NC. Siemens 3SE3: insulation AC 500 V / DC 600 V, thermal current 10 A, mechanical life 30 × 10⁶ operations, repeat accuracy 0.02 mm.

A proximity switch does the same job without being touched; see Chapter 1.8.

A master controller opens and closes several contacts in a fixed order as its handle is turned, to give commands or to interlock and change over control circuits. It is used in drives such as cranes.

TypeFeature
Adjustable-camCam plates have holes and slots, so their positions can be set to match a required switching table. It can be coupled to the operating machinery through a reduction gear
Non-adjustable-camCams are fixed; contacts can only be arranged according to the switching table. Built into a control desk with a universal joint, the handle can tilt in any direction and gives dozens of positions: up–down, left–right, forward–back

A signal lamp (indicator) shows the state of the circuit: lamp holder, lens, bulb and housing.

A fuse is the simplest and cheapest protective device. It is connected in series with the circuit it protects and works by the heating effect of the current: on a short circuit or heavy overload the fuse element melts and breaks the circuit.

It consists of an element and an insulating base or tube. Elements are wire or strip, of two kinds:

MaterialMelting pointUsed for
Lead-tin alloy, zincLowSmall currents
Silver, copperHighLarge currents; the thinner element makes less metal vapour, so the arc is easier to put out

Points are the book’s Table 1.8 for common fuse elements. Straight lines between points are only a guide.

The protection characteristic (time–current or “ampere-second” characteristic) is inverse-time: the larger the current, the sooner the element melts.

Current ÷ element rated current≤ 11.62.038≥ 9
Melting timeNever melts3600 s30–40 s4.5 s1 sInstantaneous

Read the table: at 1.6 times rated current a fuse takes an hour to melt. That is why a fuse is a poor overload protector for a motor and is used for short-circuit protection.

sections.h: Four ratings, and the difference between two of them
sections.b:
RatingMeaning
Rated voltageMust be equal to or greater than the circuit voltage
Rated current (of the fuse body)The current the holder and contacts can carry continuously without exceeding their permitted temperature rise
Element rated currentThe largest current the element carries indefinitely without melting
Breaking capacityThe largest current the fuse can interrupt at rated voltage. It depends on the arc-quenching ability of the fuse, not on the element rating

One fuse body takes elements of several ratings, and the element rating may never exceed the body rating. Example from the book’s table: an RL1-60 body is rated 60 A and accepts elements of 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 50 or 60 A.

The type code is R (fuse) followed by a letter for the construction: C porcelain plug-in · L screw · M unfilled enclosed tube · T filled enclosed tube · S fast-acting · Z self-resetting.

TypeConstructionTypical data from the bookUse
